A WOMAN has been rushed to hospital after she was allegedly sexually assaulted at knifepoint in Central Park.

New York cops have launched an urgent manhunt for the suspect following the alleged attack at 8:30pm local time on Saturday.

The alleged sexual assault took place inside the park near East 67th Street and Fifth Avenue.

Reports say the woman was walking on a street when she was approached by a knife-wielding man.





He allegedly threatened her with the blade before forcing her into the park where the suspected attack occurred.

A passerby reportedly saw what was happening and called police.

New York locals were left horrified by the allegations.

News.title: Motorcyclist, 19, dies in horror high-speed crash after hitting safety barrier during police chase
News.content:

CRASH DEATH Motorcyclist, 19, dies in horror high-speed crash after hitting safety barrier during police chase







Next

A TEENAGE motorcyclist has died in a high-speed crash after a police pursuit on the A12.

Cops found the 19-year-old driving with no registration in Basildon yesterday sparking the deadly chase.

The boy crashed just before noon as the London Air Ambulance rushed to the scene.

The teen was pronounced dead by medics as they arrived.





Emergency services cordoned the surrounding roads for over seven hours following the crash.

His next-of-kin have been informed.

The Met’s Directorate of Professional Standards (DPS) and the Independent Office for Police Conduct (IOPC) have also been informed.

Road closures were in place between A12 Eastern Avenue northbound from Masefield Crescent to Gallows Corner.



Eastern Avenue East southbound was also closed from Gallows Corner to Heath Drive.

One eyewitness, who wishes to remain anonymous, said that he was driving on the A12 when a motorcyclist overtook his vehicle “at a very high speed”.

He said: “Just moments later, the motorcyclist crashed into a metal safety barrier.”

“I also witnessed police officers performing CPR on the motorcyclist at the scene in an attempt to save his life.”



The Metropolitan Police confirmed that the chase only occurred after they found the motorbike travelling with no registration plate.

A Metropolitan Police spokesperson said: “Police indicated for the motorcycle to pull over, but it failed to stop

“Shortly afterward, the motorcycle collided with street furniture at Gallows Corner.”

News.title: Pest exterminator shoots wife, 54, in head with rifle after ‘mistaking her for rat’ – as she is left fighting for life
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

GUN HORROR Pest exterminator shoots wife, 54, in head with rifle after ‘mistaking her for rat’ – as she is left fighting for life







Next

A PEST exterminator has allegedly shot his wife in the head after mistaking her for a rat.

The victim, 54, was left fighting for her life following the botched rodent culling operation at a refrigerated warehouse in France.

Emergency services rushed to the scene in Bondoufle, Essonne, after receiving reports that a woman had been hit by a bullet.

Firefighters and response teams arrived at 10pm local time on Saturday night.





The woman was found with a serious head injury and rushed to hospital.

Her condition is understood to have rapidly deteriorated after she arrived at the medical centre.

Police arrested an agitated man at the scene who said he was the victim’s husband.

He allegedly explained he had shot her during a rat control operation.



The couple were both professional exterminators who had been called to a food storage site to eliminate rodents.

They were carrying out a “sanitary culling” of the animals – where experts use air rifles or shotguns to kill targets.

Lead pellets are used in these operations – the same type used in Saturday’s shooting, according to reports.

The exterminator claims he heard a noise in the dark before pulling the trigger.



He claims he shot his partner by mistake.

A source close to the probe told Le Parisien: “He claims he mistook her for a rodent.”

The pellet hit the woman between her eyes, causing serious wounds, according to local media.

An investigation into attempted homicide of a spouse is underway.

The exterminator was quizzed by cops after being cuffed.



He will face court on Monday.

News.title: Paris gunman ‘targeted black people & Arabs to get revenge over French riots’ as cops continue to probe ‘terror attack’
News.content:
Next

A GUNMAN in Paris allegedly targeted black people and Arabs to get revenge over the spiralling French riots.

One person was killed and five others were injured on Friday in a terrifying drive-by shooting which cops are treating as a suspected terror attack.



The main suspect, Kevin T, claimed he targeted black and Arab people specifically because he was “fed up with them”, according to Le Monde.

He cited looted and destroyed shops in the French capital – some of the worst the country has seen in years.



Cops arrested the suspect while he was driving to La Verrière.

He then allegedly confessed to having a racist ideology.



A sub-machine gun and tear gas canisters were seized from his car, as well as cocaine.

His blood tested positive for cannabis and cocaine, Le Parisien reported.



Police sources told the outlet the man maintained a “stoic” and unbothered attitude while he was being cuffed.

Minesweepers were called in before a police raid of the suspect’s home in Plaisir.

The property had been booby-trapped with gas cylinders and electrical wires connected to a timer, according to authorities.



A copy of Adolf Hitler’s Nazi manifesto Mein Kampf was found inside, along with a Bible and Koran.

The suspect was released from police custody to undergo a psychiatric assessment on Sunday.

The family of the tragic victim in the attack Pengo Bossio Wangi, 26, hit out at the decision.



Their lawyer said: “When the attack comes from the far-Right, the psychiatric issue is raised very quickly.

“The perpetrator is ‘necessarily a deranged individual’. This question, however, is almost never raised with the same insistence when the attack is Islamist-motivated.”

Ritsia Wangi, the victim’s sister, said she and her family had learned of her brother’s death from a journalist.

She claimed the reporter told her dad his son had been shot dead in a racist attack.

“He died a terrible death. He died all alone,” she told Blast.



“It really was a barrage of relentless gunfire.”

France has suffered weeks of explosive riots organised by students and the Yellow Vest movement.

Fiery demonstrations have even spread throughout Europe, with crowds clashing with cops in Belgium, Spain, and Italy over a range of different issues.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Over 1,000 people were arrested in France this weekend while dozens of people were left injured.

News.title: Teen, 17, arrested over death of boy in fatal car crash and three rushed to hospital after 4am police pursuit
News.content:
CRASH ARREST Teen, 17, arrested over death of boy in fatal car crash and three rushed to hospital after 4am police pursuit







Next

A TEEN has been arrested after a horror smash killed a boy and left three injured following a police car chase.

The 17-year-old is being held on suspicion of causing death by dangerous driving.

According to cops, a white Nissan Juke was in a collision with a black Audi S3 in south Bristol just after 4am this morning.

The boy who tragically died was a passenger in the Nissan.





The smash happened on the A37 Wells Road at its junction with Airport Road and Wootton Park, said police.

The force said: “It followed a short police pursuit involving an unmarked police vehicle and the white Nissan Juke.

“Sadly, one person – a teenage boy who was a passenger in the white Nissan Juke – died at the scene.”

Two other teenage children from the Nissan were taken to hospital with injuries not thought to be life-threatening, along with the man driving the Audi.



A mandatory referral has been made to the Independent Office for Police Conduct (IOPC) as a death following police contact, and Avon and Somerset’s Professional Standards Unit has been informed.

The road was closed for collision investigation and vehicle recovery and reopened just after 4pm on Sunday.

A detective inspector from the force major crime investigation unit is currently leading the inquiry into the collision, pending any decision by the IOPC.

News.title: Man, 35, becomes second person charged after police officer shot with ‘sawn-off shotgun’ in Nottingham city centre
News.content:
SHOOTING HORROR Man, 35, becomes second person charged after police officer shot with ‘sawn-off shotgun’ in Nottingham city centre







Next

A SECOND person has been charged after a police officer was reportedly shot by a sawn-off shotgun in a city centre last week.

PC Lee Lane is still in hospital a week on from the horror shooting in Nottingham with a 35-year-old man charged today.



The on-duty officer was shot at a bus stop on Angel Row at around 4.50am on October 18 after approaching two people acting suspiciously.

The suspects fled the scene and the injured cop was rushed to hospital, where he remains receiving treatment.



The force then launched a major hunt for the suspects.

A firearm – believed to be a sawn-off shotgun – was recovered from the scene as detectives launched their major investigation.

Just days ago, Aisha Zaman, 27, was charged with possession of a prohibited firearm and possession of a firearm with intent to commit an indictable offence.

The woman has been remanded in custody and faced court on Friday, October 23.



Now a 35-year-old man has been charged with assisting an offender.

Jahmal Ruddock-Senior is due to appear at Nottingham Magistrates’ Court tomorrow.

Several others have been arrested in connection with the incident.

This includes two men, aged 24 and 30, and two women, aged 25 and 21, who have been arrested on suspicion of assisting an offender.

A 35-year-old man and a 33-year-old woman have also been arrested on suspicion of possession of a firearm with intent to endanger life and assisting an offender – both remain in police custody.



Terrifying images from the site of the shooting show what appears to be a sawn-off shotgun discarded on the street.

Footage later emerged showing the aftermath of the shooting with members of the public spotted rushing to assist the wounded cop.

Anyone with information that could help police with their inquiry is urged to get in touch quoting incident 106 of October 18, 2026.

News.title: Two rushed to hospital after being crushed by falling scaffolding that collapsed during Storm Boelo
News.content:
WIND CHAOS Two rushed to hospital after being crushed by falling scaffolding that collapsed during Storm Boelo







Next

TWO people have been hospitalised after being crushed by scaffolding swept over by Storm Boelo.

The pedestrians became trapped after winds knocked the structure down at around 1.30pm today.



The pedestrians were walking in Streatham High Road, south west London, when the incident unfolded.

People passing the scene managed to pull the pair out of the wreckage.



Pictures show firefighters at the scene of a crumbled metal and wooden structure along the high street.

The area was taped off as emergency services attended the incident and took the two away in ambulances.

It is understood their injuries are not serious.

A London Fire Brigade spokesperson said: “Firefighters are responding to an incident involving collapsed scaffolding on High Road, Streatham.



“Two people were trapped under the scaffolding and rescued before the Brigade arrived. Both people were taken to hospital by London Ambulance Service.

“The Brigade’s Control Officers received the first of five calls at 1331 and have mobilised crews from Tooting, Lewisham, West Norwood and surrounding fire stations to the scene.”

A London Ambulance Service spokesperson said: “We sent resources to the scene including ambulance crews, an incident response officer and paramedics from our hazardous area response team (HART) to the scene.

“We treated two patients at the scene and took both of them to a hospital.”

This comes as the country faces nation-wide chaos from Storm Boelo, leaving tens of thousands without power and flooding towns.



A 60-year-old man was tragically killed by a falling tree in Dumfries, Scotland, earlier this morning.

Met Office warnings are in place across the UK for high winds – with gusts of up to 84mph in parts of the country.

An amber alert for wind is in place until 9pm tonight.

Brits have been warned not to travel if possible, as severe disruption hits all modes of transport.

Trees have blocked roads and smashed into cars and homes from the gusts of up to 84mph today.



Tens of thousands have been left without power, with the Energy Networks Association reporting that 83,000 homes have been cut off.

It said: “The networks have been focussed on reconnecting customers this morning, though the continuing severe weather in some regions is limiting network engineers’ opportunities to safely start the work of restoring customers’ power today and access to certain areas remains difficult.”

The Met Office added: “Injuries and danger to life are likely from large waves and beach material being thrown onto coastal roads, sea fronts and properties.”

News.title: At least 41 injured with 20 in serious condition after bus crashes into car and plunges 65ft down slope in Barcelona
News.content:
Next

AT least 41 people have been injured with 20 in a serious condition after a bus crashed into a car in Barcelona.

The passenger bus veered off the road after the collision and plunged 65ft down a steep slope sparking an emergency rescue operation.



The terrifying ordeal unfolded on the BV-5144 road in Fogars de Montclús in the Barcelona province.

Authorities say 20 of the 41 wounded passengers are in serious condition.



A major emergency response team including firefighters, 15 ambulances and two helicopters rushed to the scene to help injured passengers.

Reports say some of the wounded people were able to walk back up to the road without support.

Local authorities said the bus plunged 65ft down a slope moments after the initial impact.

The President of the Generalitat of Catalonia, Salvador Illa, said he was monitoring the situation “with great concern”.

He said he remains in contact with local authorities to stay informed of the case.

Illa said: “All my support to the people affected and my gratitude to the emergency services for their work.”



Authorities were first alerted to the crash at 4.23pm local time.

The road has been closed in both directions as the recovery operation continues.

It is currently unclear what caused the two vehicles to crash into each other.

It comes after nearly 50 people were injured in a horror bus crash in Spain this summer.

A coach carrying 55 passengers smashed into a council office on Rambla Ferran in Lleida.



The city’s mayor Fèlix Larrosa said: “This is the most serious accident that has occurred in the city of Lleida”.

The bus was travelling through the city centre from Lleida to the historic village of la Granja d’Escarp when it suddenly veered off course.

News.title: Man killed by falling tree as Storm Boelo leaves 160,000 properties without power
News.content:
A 60-year-old man has died after being hit by a falling tree in southern Scotland as Storm Boelo continues to bring severe weather to the UK.

Police Scotland said the man was pronounced dead at the scene following the incident near Castle Douglas in Dumfries and Galloway at about 10:30 on Sunday.

The harsh weather battering the UK had left 161,400 properties without power as of 15:00 GMT on Sunday afternoon, the Energy Networks Association (ENA) said.

Those still without electricity have faced delays as the dangerous conditions were "limiting network engineers' opportunities to safely start the work", the ENA added.

During Storm Boelo and the earlier Storm Austen, which hit the UK on Friday, 838,700 properties across the country faced power cuts, according to the ENA.

Wind gusts peaked on Sunday morning at 85mph in Machrihanish, in Argyll and Bute, and 84mph in both Stornoway in the Outer Hebrides, and Capel Curig in north Wales.

An amber wind warning issued by the Met Office will remain in place until 21:00 on Sunday across Scotland and parts of northern England.

A yellow warning that also covers other areas of the north of England, including Liverpool, Manchester, Leeds, Sheffield and Newcastle-upon-Tyne, as well as parts of the East and West Midlands and North Wales, is in place until 21:00 on Sunday.

The Met Office has urged people to "stay indoors as much as possible", adding: "If you do go out, try not to walk, or shelter, close to buildings and trees."

The strongest gusts have continued to spread eastwards across the UK on Sunday.

News.title: Burnham open to 'honest discussion' on EU free movement
News.content:
The prime minister says he would welcome an "honest discussion" about the prospect of returning to free movement between the UK and European Union.

Speaking to the Sunday Times, Andy Burnham said a new relationship with Brussels could include full EU membership or joining the single market, requiring free movement.

Asked about Burnham's remarks, Angela Rayner told the BBC's Sunday with Laura Kuenssberg "you can't take anything off the table", adding the prime minister was saying "we've got to be pragmatic to get the best deal for Britain and he wants to have the conversation."

Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch responded that the prime minister "hasn't thought this through", while Reform UK's Robert Jenrick dismissed the idea as "mad".

Migration dominated debate during the 2016 Brexit campaign, with the Leave campaign raising issues about rules allowing any EU citizen to move to the UK.

Burnham has previously committed to Labour's 2024 election manifesto which ruled out a return of free movement, single market membership or a customs union.

He has said that any changes would require a mandate at a general election, would is due by 2029.

"I think you have to have a very factual, quite evidence-based debate about this," he told the Sunday Times, external, adding he believed the type of migration had changed from revolving door movement of young people.

"Revolving door migration where people would come and then go back is different," he said. "The balance of migration has changed, hasn't it, since then? I think we've just got to have an honest discussion about those things."

But he stressed: "I can't see myself ever recommending anything that would involve joining the euro or Schengen."

The Schengen Agreement allows passport-free travel across EU countries. The UK was able to keep the pound when it was an EU member, but the bloc has pushed new members to adopt the Euro.

His remarks were made ahead of an EU summit on 20 November in Brussels, where the prime minister is expected to pitch options for a reset of relations with the bloc.

On Sunday with Laura Kuenssberg, Rayner said she wanted to see the best possible deal with the European Union, which may well involve concessions.

"What the prime minister is saying now, and what I want, is that we have an honest conversation about the facts of what the trade-offs are to get the best deal for Britain going forward," she said.

"The frustration for me in the previous debate we had when we had the referendum is that a lot of those facts didn't get the airtime... So I would like us to have an honest conversation about what the trade-offs could be and then put that to the people at a general election."

Writing on X, Badenoch dismissed it as "yet another example of Burnham's foot in mouth syndrome".

She added: "Most people who voted for Brexit did so because they didn't want free movement. Too many politicians have failed to understand the significance and impact of immigration on communities."

Conservative MP and former chancellor Jeremy Hunt, who backed Remain, warned the Brexit debate was "incredibly divisive" and insisted the current Brexit deal can still be made to work.

"I was at the top of a government that was paralysed for several years while we were trying to wrestle with the implications of that vote and I think, having made the decision, we should stick with it and make the most of it - I think we can make it a success," he told Kuenssberg.

Pointing to the one million young people not in work or training, he added: "Surely our priority in that situation is to get those jobs filled by the young people we have here instead of parking them on welfare.

"Which is why I think it's astonishing to lead on the issue of free movement... Something that is actually going to stop young people here getting jobs."

But Liberal Democrat deputy leader Daisy Cooper told Kuenssberg she believed allowing freedom of movement would be "a really good thing for growth" and pushed for the UK to rejoin the single market, the customs union, and also be involved in the bloc's defence pact.

The UK currently has "the worst of both worlds" on immigration, she said, as it was excluded from the EU's "new asylum pact with biometric data" that could be used to "tackle the small boats crisis".

Reform UK's economy spokesperson Robert Jenrick told Kuenssberg he had never believed freedom of movement "was a good thing", despite supporting the Remain position before the 2016 referendum when he was a Conservative MP.

"I think it's completely mad, the idea that this country needs more immigration," he said, claiming data shows mass migration "has been a disaster for working people, for Brits".

"The last thing they want is their wages being undercut by a load of low wage, low-skilled migrants from overseas," he added.

News.title: Letter making claims about Meghan's father written by his first wife, BBC understands
News.content:
A letter sent to the Metropolitan Police making a number of claims relating to the Duchess of Sussex's father was written by his ex-wife Roslyn Loveless, the BBC understands.

Meghan confirmed on Friday she had previously been informed about "disturbing allegations" about her estranged father, Thomas Markle.

On Saturday, the Met confirmed it received a letter relating to Markle in 2019, and it was shared with the Duke and Duchess of Sussex at the time.

It has been reported that images of child sexual abuse allegedly belonging to Markle, 82, had been found in his former home in the Philippines. Markle, who is based in the US, denies all such allegations.

Loveless, who has since died, is the mother of Meghan's half-siblings Samantha Markle and Thomas Markle Jr. Loveless divorced Markle in 1975 before he married the Duchess' mother Doria Ragland in 1979.

Meghan was born in 1981 and is the only daughter of Markle and Ragland.

In a statement shared on Friday, Meghan confirmed the existence of the letter and wrote: "I am deeply distressed... my thoughts are with any children who may have been harmed."

She said she hoped it could be understood why she had largely cut off contact from her father and did "not allow him to have contact with our children".

Meghan has been estranged from her father since 2018. The BBC understands she broke contact with him last year, telling him she and the authorities knew he had abused young girls.

Sources close to the duchess said Meghan warned Markle in a letter - sent while he was in hospital in the Philippines after having his leg amputated - that he would never meet his grandchildren.

News.title: Board of Deputies of British Jews declares Greens to be racist party
News.content:
The Green Party of England and Wales has been declared a racist organisation by the Board of Deputies of British Jews.

The Jewish body, which is the largest in the UK, was responding to the "Zionism is racism" policy motion passed at the Green Party's conference earlier this month.

Board of Deputies president Phil Rosenberg said a vote passed by 118 votes to one to declare that the Greens had, "by adopting an antisemitic platform, become a racist party".

A spokesman for the Greens insisted the party does not discriminate against people who hold Zionist views and said it rejected the Board of Deputies' "characterisation of this motion and our party".

They added the decision "will not stop us from speaking out against the genocide in Gaza and pushing for stronger sanctions against the Israeli government and its leaders". Israel has repeatedly denied its actions in Gaza amount to genocide.

The motion passed by the Board of Deputies urged other parties not to do deals with the Greens unless they rejected the policy.

Forming coalition deals with Greens at local or national level would be "failing to take antisemitism with the requisite seriousness", it said, unless the party's local leadership have rejected the policy and committed to overturn it.

Labour has already issued an ultimatum to local Green groups it is currently in coalition with, telling them to disown the motion or lose the party's support.

Rosenberg said: "By adopting an antisemitic platform, the Green Party of England and Wales has become a racist party. We will treat it accordingly.

"No political party has the right to tell Jews that a central part of our identity, rooted in thousands of years of history, faith and peoplehood, is racist.

"The Green Party's policy brands much of our community, including our synagogues and communal organisations, with that slur. It gives prejudice against Jews a political licence.

"The Green Party's leadership must now take responsibility for reversing this policy and confronting the antisemitism it has legitimised."

The motion backed by Green members at its party conference earlier this month said Zionism was an ideology supporting "an ethnonationalist Jewish state in historic Palestine to the exclusion and/ or domination of the non-Jewish population".

It was criticised by Jewish groups, as well as four Green MPs and two former leaders, and opposition political parties.

Responding when the Green motion was passed, the Board of Deputies and Jewish Leadership Council said in a joint statement that "Zionism is anti-racism, creating a refuge for Jews in their ancient homeland after millennia of persecution outside it".

Green Party leader Zack Polanski, who is Jewish, did not take part in the vote on the motion as he left the conference early to campaign in the Holborn and St Pancras by-election which was held days later.

He has since told the BBC's Sunday with Laura Kuenssberg that, while he would like to make amendments, he would not overturn the motion, which would be party policy until 2028.

He said both boys had been so excited and been snorkelling in shallow water as they sorted out their towels and bags on the beach when the boys got into difficulties.

News.title: Carrick future under major threat - can he survive?
News.content:
Michael Carrick's future as Manchester United manager is under major threat following the home loss to Bournemouth on Sunday.

The Red Devils lost 3-0 as their poor start to the season continued - they have won just one of their eight Premier League matches so far and sit 16th - 14 points off the top.

Carrick, 45, took interim charge in January following Ruben Amorim's departure and he was rewarded with the permanent job in May after securing Champions League qualification with an impressive run that resulted in them finishing third.

But United have not won in the top flight since 30 August, when they defeated newly promoted Ipswich 5-2.

"See what happens," Carrick told BBC Sport when asked if he was expecting any conversations on his future.

"I'm not expecting anything. It's just digesting today - we knew it was an important day to try and get us moving forward and we haven't done that.

"For me it's just digesting that and the emotions at the end of the game is something I've not really had before."

Carrick made a big call on Sunday by dropping his captain Bruno Fernandes to the bench.

That decision came after the Portugal midfielder questioned Carrick's tactics in Wednesday's 4-1 loss at Como in the Champions League.

The comments from Fernandes came in the wake of defender Lisandro Martinez issuing an apology following his controversial remarks criticising the club's hierarchy.

Martinez said he had expected more investment in the Manchester United squad and "more from our technical director [Jason Wilcox]".

News.title: Long queues after power surge at Stansted Airport
News.content:
Passengers arriving at Stansted Airport have described waiting in long queues to reach immigration control after a power surge shut down its systems.

Traveller Jill Stakem reported the airport's internal tram system had failed earlier and people were "being held in a corridor for over 90 minutes".

Stakem added: "It's horrendous. No communication, no seating for people, no-one offering watering."

In a statement, a spokesperson for Stansted Airport said: "Due to a power surge earlier today that affected the airport and local area, a number of airport systems were temporarily impacted."

They added: "All systems are now back in service with operational teams working hard to provide support to passengers on their journeys through the airport."

Another airport spokesperson confirmed the shuttle service "remained out-of-service due to a technical fault and contingency bussing is in operation to transfer passengers between the terminal and gates".

News.title: Russia to host first Olympic federation world event since Ukraine invasion
News.content:
Moscow will host the 2030 World Weightlifting Championships - the first time an Olympic federation has chosen to stage a global event in Russia since the country's full-scale invasion of Ukraine began in 2022.

The International Weightlifting Federation (IWF) announced its decision on Sunday, four months after confirming Russian athletes would again be eligible to compete in its events.

In July, the International Olympic Committee (IOC) provisionally lifted a suspension on the Russian Olympic Committee.

That suspension had been imposed following the country's invasion of Ukraine.

The IOC's subsequent decision potentially opened the way for Russian athletes to compete for their country at the 2028 Olympic Games in Los Angeles.

The IWF announced the host cities of four world championships at junior, youth and senior levels, awarding the 2029 senior event to Ahmedabad in India.

"All the bids we received were excellent and we are sure that the championships in your respective countries will be a huge success," said IWF general secretary Jose Quinones.

No world championships in an Olympic sport, summer or winter, have been held in Russia since the start of the war in Ukraine.

The 2025 World Aquatics Championships, initially awarded to the Russian city of Kazan, were instead moved to Singapore.

Moscow has not held the World Weightlifting Championships since 1983.

The Russian Weightlifting Federation said: "[We are] the first Olympic sports federation to succeed in bringing a top-level official competition back to the country in many years."

Federation president Aleksandr Vinokurov thanked the IWF in a post on Telegram "for their trust", with the championships also serving as a qualifying event for the 2032 Olympic Games in Brisbane, Australia.

"Russia has all the necessary experience and capabilities to host competitions of the highest level," he said.

"Moscow has repeatedly staged major international sporting events and has modern infrastructure."

In announcing its decision in July to provisionally lift Russia's suspension, the IOC said that no decision had been taken on whether Russia could display their flag, colours and anthem at the Olympic âGames.

The IOC said it would continue to "not organise IOC events in Russia or invite Russian government or state officials to its events".

Some Russian athletes competed at the 2024 Paris Olympic Games and this year's Winter Olympics in Milan as neutrals.

Ukraine filed an appeal to the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) requesting that the IOC decision to lift its suspension of the Russian Olympic Committee be annulled.

The IOC's move decision came after the International Paralympic Committee had already ended Russia's exile from global sports events, with the country's athletes allowed to compete under their national flag at the Winter Paralympics.

Five Ukrainian athletes are listed to compete in the 2026 IWF World Championships in Ningbo, China, which are scheduled to take place from 27 October to 8 November.

News.title: Budget to include £1bn for social and affordable housing
News.content:
Under the plans for the regions, an initial Â£285m in transitional seed funding will be allocated by the government next year to support mayors and local leaders - and reduce reliance on "fragmented bidding pots" in Whitehall, the Treasury said.

The government will also confirm that it will work with mayors to design a new Â£1.5bn borrowing facility from 2028, which would allow them to access capital needed to support local priorities.

The Treasury said this could be put towards new homes, bringing High Streets back to life, or improving transport links.

Healey said: "Mayors and local leaders know what their communities need to grow, which is why we are giving them more money, more power and more capacity to get projects moving, build homes and make the right decisions for their areas."

Areas across the country which are not yet strategic authorities will be able to access a share of the Â£285m to "unlock projects which will contribute to growth in their areas".

The prime minister said: "I'm calling time on local leaders going cap in hand to Westminster. That is no way to run a country."

Claire Ward, chairwoman of the UK Mayors Network and Labour's East Midlands mayor, said that having the "right powers and resources through increased devolution" would help turn "ambitious plans into reality and deliver real, lasting change" for communities.

Lord Sadiq Khan, Labour's mayor of London, said greater ability to invest could "help unlock transformational infrastructure projects" including the West London Orbital route, the extension of the Bakerloo Underground line and Docklands Light Railway, and the development of Stratford International station.

Departing Treasury entrepreneurship adviser, Alex Depledge, has criticised the government's treatment of start-ups ahead of her last day on Thursday - the day after the Budget.

She told the Sunday Times, external, that start-ups were being treated as a "sideshow" and should not be pushed to the "margins of economic policy".

"Keeping scale-ups on the fringes underestimates the contribution of our greatest companies, and we need to support and develop them on British shores at all costs," she said.

Leading up to the Budget, defence has also remained a key talking point. Healey resigned in June from his role as defence secretary in the previous government over the defence investment plan, which he claimed fell "well short" of what was needed to fund the armed forces.

He had called for defence spending to rise to 3% of the country's GDP by 2030, on the way to reaching a Nato target of 3.5% in 2035.

But urging him to commit to setting out plans to spend 3% of GDP on defence, the shadow chancellor said: "We are living in an era of extraordinary threats, and yet the chancellor is dithering over finding the money to pay the country's insurance premium... you cannot have a strong economy without a strong defence".

Responding to Andrew Griffith's comments, Defence Secretary Wes Streeting said the Conservatives were to blame for failing to invest in the military while in office.

Streeting said the prime minister had made it clear that his government was "determined to give our armed forces the investment needed to keep us safe".

News.title: Why the King's Caribbean tour could be 'biggest risk of his reign'
News.content:
The King will make three significant speeches during the Caribbean trip and will follow government advice not to issue an official apology for Britain's role in the transatlantic slave trade.

A senior royal aide said that the King would "not shy away from the darkest days of our past" but stressed that decisions over apologies and reparations were matters for government.

The current Burnham administration, like those before it, will not pay reparations.

Buckingham Palace says that acknowledging the wrongs of the past will be built into the King's programme in all three countries.

But apologies, reparations, and republicanism are rich pickings for campaigners and protests are likely.

This is the reality for the King and Buckingham Palace, and they are accepting of it.

Those who've worked on the planning of the trip view protests as part of the open debate in the region and security preparations include their possibility.

Lurking in the back of Royal Household minds will also be memories of the last tour by senior royals to the Caribbean in the early part of 2022.

Then, as the Duke and Duchess of Cambridge, William and Catherine found themselves facing criticism over the optics of the trip - images of the royal couple reaching out to touch the outstretched hands of Jamaican children through a wire fence looked clumsy. Engagements designed as tributes to past royal visits appeared outdated. And protests also caused the cancellation of a small part of the schedule.

Everything will have been done to avoid those kinds of missteps on the 2026 Caribbean tour.

News.title: Four-year-old girl dies after fall from tower block
News.content:
A four-year-old girl has died after falling from a tower block in east London.

The Metropolitan Police said officers were called to the scene at an address in St Paul's Road, Barking, at about 11:00 BST on Saturday morning, following reports that a child had fallen from height.

Paramedics from the London Ambulance Service gave first aid and the child was taken to hospital, but later died from her injuries.

A Met spokesperson said the incident was not believed to be suspicious.

"Our thoughts and deepest sympathies are with the child's family and loved ones at this incredibly difficult time," they said.

"An investigation into the circumstances surrounding this tragic incident is ongoing. However, at this time, the incident is not believed to be suspicious.

"We urge anyone with information about the incident to contact police on 101, quoting CAD 2424/24OCT."

News.title: Plan for Northern Olympics to get £7m in Healey's Budget
News.content:
The report will look in closer detail at how hosting the games could work.

It will consider the kinds of venues and transport links required, how different cities could share the games, how communities could benefit.

Crucially it will also examine how much it could cost as well as assess the chances of a bid succeeding. The Conservative-Lib Dem coalition government said in 2013 it estimated hosting in London had cost Â£8.9bn.

A report in 2013 by the UK Trade and Investment, which has since been replaced by the Department for International Trade, said it had sparked a Â£9.9bn boost to the economy through new contracts, sales and foreign investments.

But the estimated amount was queried by some, including the Federation of Small Businesses and the National Institute of Economic and Social Research (NIESR).

Conservative shadow sports minister Louie French said that while hosting an Olympic Games would "likely provide a positive boost for the country", the cost of proposals would require "careful scrutiny".

He said the chancellor should use the Budget to bring down everyday costs before looking to "spend millions in taxpayer cash on reheated announcements made by his predecessor".

French added: "The irony is that Labour's new tourism tax will create a cost barrier for sports fans wanting to visit the North of England for an Olympic Games."

The new feasibility study for the Northern Games will be done by government, UK Sport, the Northern Mayors and include the British Olympic and Paralympic associations.

Healey said: "Olympic legacy lasts way beyond the celebration of sport over the summer. The North hosting an event as big as this would be truly unforgettable.

"Britain's experience of London 2012 is proof we can host the world. I'm picking up the pace on our work to potentially bid for these prestigious games. It will lift communities, create opportunities and give the UK a huge boost."

News of the funding for the study was welcomed by the British Olympic Association, ParalympicsGB and UK Sport.

"We welcome the government's continued support for exploring the potential of a future bid for the Olympic and Paralympic Games in the UK in the 2040s," they said in a joint statement.

"Building on the success and legacy of London 2012, we look forward to working in partnership to explore this exciting opportunity and the benefits it could deliver for the nation, and for the global Olympic and Paralympic movements."

News.title: Thousands of people gather in support of Drumcree Orangemen
News.content:
The first part of the parade was followed by a series of speeches, mainly from members of the Orange Order.

This was very much an Orange Order event and not a political rally but inevitably there was a political tone to many of the comments.

There was explicit criticism of the Police Service of Northern Ireland (PSNI) Chief Constable Jon Boutcher, the secretary of state and the first minister, but also implicit criticism of the leaders of the two biggest unionist parties - the DUP and Ulster Unionist Party.

Traditional Unionist Voice leader Jim Allister was applauded but by far the loudest cheers were for the Orange Order's legal adviser Jamie Bryson and the local MP Lockhart.

She was invited on to the stage and presented with a special gift for her support of the Orangemen.

Lockhart was the only politician to take to the stage, where she repeated her challenge to the DUP leadership: "Profound consequences must mean profound consequences. Michelle O'Neill must go.

"That's where I stand, and this lady is not for turning."

Portadown District Master Nigel Dawson warned politicians that they could face consequences at the next election over the Drumcree dispute.

"Politicians need to remember that we put them into office and we can take them out of office," he said.

He added that the Orange Order had won the right "to return home via our traditional route and Portadown District intends to exercise that right on a date and time of our choosing, and if necessary, without further recourse".

Orange Order Deputy District Master Alistair Power said Drumcree must not be allowed to divide unionism.

"It should not be used by parties to attack each other publicly over differences of opinion," he added. "We need to stand united."

News.title: Habitat destroyed by Cairngorms fire to be restored with government funding
News.content:
More than Â£1m is to be spent on nature recovery projects, including the restoration of habitats destroyed by a fire which ripped through a huge area of hillside in the Cairngorms.

The Scottish government funding will support habitat, species and river restoration, control of invasive non-native species and deer management across Scotland.

It includes Â£150,100 for recovery and nature restoration work following the Abernethy wildfire in the Cairngorms in July, to restore damaged habitats, help wildlife recover and reduce the risk of future wildfires.

Further funding will be provided to a range of other projects.

News.title: Reward offered over murder in flat used as brothel
News.content:
A Â£20,000 reward is being offered by Crimestoppers in connection with the murder of a man who was found dead in a Birmingham flat in 2022.

Jinming Zhang had been stabbed multiple times before he was found in the property, which police said was being used as a brothel, in Moseley Street in Digbeth.

West Midlands Police previously released CCTV of a suspect, while a DNA sample from the suspected killer found at the scene did not produce a match on the national database.

The case was featured in the BBC series of Forensics: The Real CSI last year, which revealed police believed the murder suspect may have sustained a hand injury in the frenzied attack.

Jenny Birch, who has been overseeing the investigation, urged anyone with information "no matter how small" to contact police.

"Someone out there knows something, and we won't give up until we have answers," she said.

News.title: Sam Fender calls out ticket prices ahead of tour
News.content:
Sam Fender has said he has removed a ticket category from sale after being unhappy with pricing for his upcoming tour.

The 32-year-old announced his Proper Massive Stadium Tour earlier this week, which will visit Newcastle, Cardiff, London, Edinburgh, Dublin and Manchester in summer 2027.

While tickets are yet to go on sale, Fender responded to a post on social media which claimed to outline the expected ticket prices.

The Geordie musician now appears to have lowered the prices and said the "costs are astronomical compared to two years ago" but he could not control the venue or ticketing fees.

Tickets are due to go on general sale at 09:30 GMT on Friday, with a pre-sale at the same time on Wednesday.

Fender initially said he was "not happy" with the reported prices.

"They're getting changed," he said on Instagram.

"It got inflated well more than I'd had in mind, it should only be inflated in relation to the cost of putting the show on."

News.title: F1 United States GP LIVE: Kimi Antonelli leads as Max Verstappen loses out at start in Austin
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Kimi Antonelli leads the race in Austin ( Reuters )

Formula 1 returns to the Circuit of the Americas this weekend for the United States Grand Prix - as Kimi Antonelli stands on the cusp of his first world championship.

The 20-year-old Italian holds a 102-point lead over Mercedes teammate George Russell and will win his first title if he wins this Sunday’s grand prix and Russell finishes ninth or lower. Antonelli, who starts on pole, also needs Ferrari’s Lewis Hamilton to finish fifth or lower.

A podium last time out in Singapore extended Antonelli’s lead, as Max Verstappen claimed his second victory in a row amid a Red Bull resurgence this season. Russell, meanwhile, only finished ninth and crashed out of the sprint race in Marina Bay.

The popular race in Austin is the start of another triple-header, with Mexico and Brazil to follow in the weeks ahead. Verstappen was victorious at COTA last year.

News.title: Trump demands metal detectors for Abdul El-Sayed at US capitol as he spew attacks at Democrat during rally
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

President Donald Trump has demanded that Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed go through metal detectors at the U.S. Capitol building if he were to get elected in November’s midterm elections.

“I’m here to keep a Jihadist Muslim Brotherhood member from becoming a United States senator,” Trump said at a rally in Port Huron, Michigan, Sunday afternoon as he spewed attacks at the Democrat. El-Sayed has vehemently denied any ties to the Islamist organization.

Trump said El-Sayed “should never be allowed inside the halls of our great, beautiful Capitol building in Washington, D.C.,” adding that his supporters will elect his pick, Mike Rogers, a former Republican congressman, to the U.S. Senate.

The president then accused El-Sayed’s family of having terrorist ties, without providing any evidence, and said, “Anyone with that record of support for jihadists would be screened and unable to get a seat on an airplane. They certainly should not give him a seat in the United States Senate.”

open image in gallery President Donald Trump has demanded that Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed go through metal detectors at the US Capitol building if he were to get elected in November’s midterm elections ( Getty )

“He would be the only senator that will have to go through a metal detector before he's allowed to go into the Senate. I want him to have a metal detector,” Trump said. “If Abdul gets to the Senate, he would have access to our nation's most closely guarded national security secrets, and his vote would wield power over our military, our borders, our homeland security, and much more than that.”

El-Sayed disavowed the Muslim Brotherhood at a recent town hall in Caro, Michigan, after being asked by an attendee if he would do so.

“You’re asking the question because implicitly you assume that I’ll have dual loyalties,” El-Sayed said to the attendee. “You assume that somehow I wouldn’t disavow. Or that I’ll have some higher order, allegiance than to the Constitution.”

“I’m gonna swear an oath to the Constitution of the United States. And that Constitution guarantees us all the right to practice whatever faith we want or no faith at all,” El-Sayed said.

The Senate race is tight, with El-Sayed leading Rogers 50 percent to 48 percent among Michigan likely voters in a new Marist poll.

open image in gallery Trump accused El-Sayed of being a part of the Islamist organization known as the Muslim Brotherhood, which the Democrat has vehemently denied ( Getty Images )

As Trump holds daily rallies to boost Republican candidates’ chances of winning November’s midterm elections, former Democratic President Barack Obama has hopped on the campaign trail. Obama was in Detroit Saturday to stump for El-Sayed, where he told supporters: “Abdul is fighting for change, real change, change that will bring an end to this war.”

Obama also railed against Trump’s unpopular war in Iran at a rally in Cleveland Saturday to support Democrat Amy Acton, who is running for Ohio governor against Republican Vivek Ramaswamy.

“Let’s think about this Iran war. The original rationale was, we’re going to go in there and get them to give up their nuclear program, their nuclear weapons,” the former president said. “Now, the thing was, Iran didn’t have nuclear weapons, because I put a deal in place that everybody acknowledged — kept them from getting nukes. And I didn’t have to fire a missile to do it; I just had to engage in diplomacy.”

Iran signed the Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action in 2015, a deal Obama brokered that restricted Iran’s nuclear program in exchange for sanctions relief. During his first term, Trump withdrew from the agreement, arguing that it “allowed Iran to continue enriching uranium and — over time — reach the brink of a nuclear breakout.”

Trump launched the Iran war, alongside Israel, in late February, and it has dragged on for nearly eight months. With no end in sight and the midterms less than two weeks away, it could spell a problem for Republicans.

open image in gallery Trump has been making stops across the country as he campaigns ahead of the midterm elections ( Reuters )

The president is facing dismal approval ratings as Americans struggle with high gas prices brought on by the war and stubborn inflation making everyday necessities more expensive.

A whopping 61 percent of Americans disapproved of Trump’s job as president, while just 39 percent approved, according to a new CBS News/YouGov poll.

When asked about specific issues, 67 percent of Americans disapproved of Trump’s handling of the economy, while just 33 percent approved. Another 67 percent disapproved of the Iran war, while 33 percent approved.

Eighty-three percent of registered voters said lowering the cost of living should be one of the highest priorities for the next Congress, and 72 percent said ending the Iran war should be another top concern, according to a recent Associated Press/NORC Center for Public Affairs Research poll.

News.title: Teenager arrested after boy dies in fatal Bristol police pursuit crash
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

A teenager was arrested after a boy died in a fatal collision following a police pursuit, Avon and Somerset Police has said.

The boy who died at the scene was a passenger in a white Nissan Juke which was in a collision with a black Audi S3 in south Bristol just after 4am on Sunday morning.

Avon and Somerset Police said it happened on the A37 Wells Road at its junction with Airport Road and Wootton Park.

The force said: “It followed a short police pursuit involving an unmarked police vehicle and the white Nissan Juke.

“Sadly, one person – a teenage boy who was a passenger in the white Nissan Juke – died at the scene.”

Two other teenage children from the Nissan were taken to hospital with injuries not thought to be life-threatening, along with the man driving the Audi.

“Officers later arrested a 17-year-old boy at a residential property on suspicion of causing death by dangerous driving,” police said.

“This young person was taken to hospital for assessment and discharged. He remains in police custody.

“Specialist officers have traced and informed the family of the boy who died and offered them support.”

A mandatory referral has been made to the Independent Office for Police Conduct (IOPC) as a death following police contact, and Avon and Somerset’s Professional Standards Unit has been informed.

The road was closed for collision investigation and vehicle recovery and reopened just after 4pm on Sunday.

A detective inspector from the force major crime investigation unit is currently leading the inquiry into the collision, pending any decision by the IOPC.

News.title: Audi boss forced to defend $4 billion Georgia plant amid German union anger
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

The top executive at German carmaker Audi defended on Sunday a proposed $4 billion investment in a new facility in the United States, following an announcement made by President Donald Trump during his campaign for the upcoming November midterm elections.

Audi Chief Executive Gernot Doellner appeared alongside Trump during a campaign event in Perry, close to Macon in central Georgia, on Saturday.

At the event, Trump stated that Audi, a brand under the Volkswagen Group, intends to construct a manufacturing facility in Georgia capable of producing 200,000 SUVs each year.

"This decision was preceded by many months of careful planning and intense negotiations," Doellner informed reporters on Sunday. "If the American president invites you, you accept the invitation. That is what respect for the office and for the country in which we invest demands."

Before the project can move forward, Volkswagen's supervisory board must grant final approval for the investment.

The state of Georgia features closely contested races for its governor and the U.S. Senate.

Trump and Gernot Dollner, CEO of Audi AG, attend a rally at Guardian Centers in Perry, Georgia ( Reuters )

Trump is seeking to demonstrate that his trade tariffs on foreign automobiles are strengthening the American economy and encouraging domestic manufacturing.

In Germany, those same trade tariffs have heightened strain across European industrial sectors while escalating tensions between Volkswagen executives and labor representatives concerned about potential plant closures and layoffs.

Audi previously stated that Trump's tariffs on automobiles, steel, aluminum, and components cost the business approximately €1.2 billion ($1.4 billion) over the past year, as all of its cars sold in the American market are currently imported from Mexico or Europe.

Opponents of the trade policies argue that the tariffs have likewise harmed the domestic economy in the US by raising vehicle prices for consumers and delaying investment plans across the auto industry.

A spokesperson for Germany's IG Metall union remarked that Doellner's choice to appear alongside Trump amidst the political campaign was "hard to understand.”

"Trump has never failed to make it clear what he is after: he wants to weaken our domestic economy, particularly the automotive sector," the spokesperson said.

Christiane Benner, head of the IG Metall union and Volkswagen's deputy supervisory board chair, noted that establishing a US manufacturing footprint was "right and necessary" to enhance the company's competitive standing. "However, firm prospects for workers at all sites, particularly those here in Germany, must be clearly defined and set out," she said.

Doellner refrained from disclosing full terms of the US investment agreement, declining to confirm whether the deal incorporates tariff relief for the automaker.

Olaf Lies, state premier of Lower Saxony—the German state holding Volkswagen's second-largest ownership stake—remarked that expanding operations in the United States presents a positive prospect only if German employees benefit as well.

"Growth in America must secure jobs and value creation here and must not displace them," he said.

According to Audi, the proposed manufacturing complex will generate around 4,500 jobs. Construction work is slated to begin next year, with vehicle production anticipated to start in the early 2030s.

The facility is expected to produce Audi's Q7, Q8, and Q9 SUV models, according to a US official who spoke to Reuters.

The US official added that Audi further intends to manufacture 25,000 vehicles annually in neighboring South Carolina, with a portion of those models—currently produced in Europe—earmarked for export.

Those additional vehicles are set to be manufactured at a $2 billion facility for Scout Motors, VW's off-road vehicle brand, which is under construction in Blythewood, near Columbia, the state capital, the official stated.

"We regard the region as a key market for profitable growth," Volkswagen CEO Oliver Blume said. "A potential Audi plant in the US would create further conditions for this."

During Saturday's campaign rally, a gold Audi displaying manufacturer license plates was parked outside the event location.
