News.title: Strictly Come Dancing announces surprise format change as fourth couple exits
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Shaun Wright-Phillips has become the fourth celebrity to exit this year's Strictly Come Dancing, leaving the competition with his professional partner Alexis Warr.

The former England footballer and Warr were defeated in the dance-off by actor Jaime Winstone and Carlos Gu.

Winstone and Gu had finished in the bottom two after the public vote, despite scoring 25 for their dance on Saturday's episode of the BBC show.

Sunday's results show also brought a surprise announcement: Strictly's first triple dance-off, which will take place during next week's Halloween episode.

The three couples with the lowest combined judges' scores and public votes will dance again next week, before the judges eliminate one pair.

open image in gallery Jaime Winstone and Carlos Gu with Shaun Wright-Phillips (right) and Alexis Warr, before the former footballer became the latest celebrity to be voted off ( PA )

Strictly will return to a two-couple dance-off for the rest of the series.

In the dance-off, Wright-Phillips and Warr reprised their jive to “Faith” by Stevie Wonder featuring Ariana Grande, while Winstone and Gu performed their foxtrot to “Man I Need” by Olivia Dean again.

Judges Craig Revel Horwood and Motsi Mabuse voted to save Gu and Winstone.

Head judge Shirley Ballas voted for Wright-Phillips and Warr, leaving Du Beke, who had this week's casting vote, to decide who remained on the show.

Du Beke voted to save Winstone and Gu.

open image in gallery Shaun Wright-Phillips and Alexis Warr danced to ‘Faith’ by Stevie Wonder ( PA )

The pair had ended up in the dance-off despite finishing above former Love Island star Cach Mercer and his professional partner Maddie Ingoldsby, who scored 24.

They also finished above Emmerdale star Lawrence Robb and Jowita Przystal, who scored just 19 on Saturday.

Robb and Przystal's performance was singled out for criticism from Revel Horwood on Saturday, who said that the soap star was “flat-footed and out of time”.

Elsewhere in this week's live show, Australian singer Delta Goodrem returned after her rib injury to score the first 10 of the series.

Her rumba to Celine Dion's “It's All Coming Back To Me Now” with professional partner Kai Widdrington scored 34.

Winter Olympic champion Tabby Stoecker topped the leaderboard on Saturday, following Goodrem by scoring two 10s for her couple's choice dance to “Stupid Song” by Olivia Rodrigo.

open image in gallery Tabby Stoecker and Mark Karmalita topped the leaderboard this week ( PA )

Her total of 37 was the highest of the series so far.

Her performance with professional partner Mark Karmalita was dedicated to her late father, and she appeared emotional after the dance.

Judge Shirley Ballas praised her as a “beautiful dancer” and called the performance “absolutely exquisite”.

The results show also featured Spice Girls star Melanie C joining the Strictly professional dancers for a fitness-inspired group dance.

The remaining couples will return to the dancefloor next week at 6.30pm on BBC One on Saturday October 31 for Strictly's Halloween special.

All episodes of the 2026 series so far are available to stream on BBC iPlayer.

News.title: Venezuelan opposition leader María Corina Machado returns after 10-month exile
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

After almost a year away, Venezuelan opposition figure Maria Corina Machado has returned to her home country following a series of unsuccessful attempts that strained her relationship with US President Donald Trump's administration.

"I'm here. With you all," the Nobel Peace Prize-winner posted on X on Sunday.

Footage shared by her press team showed her appearing at a church in the western state of Lara, where bystanders gathered to sing the national anthem and shout "liberty!" as she departed in an SUV, according to a Reuters witness.

Her staff stated she will travel overland to Caracas.

Her attempts to re-enter the country have tested relations with the Trump administration, which she sought to cultivate as an ally prior to the removal of President Nicolas Maduro from power in January.

U.S. officials had asked her at least once to postpone her return, Reuters reported in June, following several failed entry efforts. While her team did not reveal the details of her journey, two people with knowledge of the matter said she took a private flight from Panama to Colombia before crossing overland into Venezuela.

Trump has consistently backed interim President Delcy Rodriguez, the former deputy to ousted President Nicolas Maduro, while praising business ventures and oil production agreements made by US firms in the country.

In September, Trump remarked that it was too soon to discuss democratic elections in Venezuela.

At the White House on Sunday, Trump stated he was unaware of Machado's arrival and suggested Washington would maintain its support for Rodriguez.

"She's a very nice woman," he said of Machado. "But we're doing really well in Venezuela."

In a statement regarding her return, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said: "The conditions allowing for the safe return of Ms. Machado to Venezuela are the direct result of the US-supported reconciliation talks which have already seen hundreds of political prisoners freed and hundreds of political opposition figures return from exile."

Rubio added: "We expect all political actors to support these talks which represent the best chance Venezuela has had in thirty years to peacefully achieve not just a free and fair election but an enduring democracy."

( Reuters )

A faction of the opposition and the interim administration held their latest negotiation session this month to restructure the supreme court and electoral council ahead of future votes.

Machado's movement is not included in these talks. Venezuela's communications ministry did not immediately reply to requests for comment.

"Maria Corina Machado will achieve liberty and democracy in Venezuela," said 69-year-old Hernan Adames, who celebrated alongside other supporters in Barquisimeto.

Machado's top foreign affairs adviser, David Smolansky, told Reuters that she plans to meet with families of political prisoners, victims of the fatal earthquakes that struck Venezuela in June, international delegates, and leaders of the country's democratic movement.

"She will work proactively for a date for free and fair elections," Smolansky added.

International energy companies committed last month to expanding operations in Venezuela during a ceremony overseen by Rodriguez and US Energy Secretary Chris Wright. Machado has maintained that only a "serious, democratic government" can offer the stability required by investors.

Machado was previously banned from exiting Venezuela by Maduro's government but secretly left in late 2025 to collect the Nobel Peace Prize after over a year in hiding.

On Saturday, her Vente Venezuela movement launched a mobile application to gather voter registration details from Venezuelans living abroad. The team behind the app—built over 18 months by 15 staff members—hopes to share the data with a reformed electoral council to officially register users.

Edmundo Gonzalez, a former presidential candidate from Machado's movement currently living in Spain, stated on X that he would join her in Venezuela soon.

News.title: Hapless and hopeless Man Utd bring curtain down on out-of-depth Carrick
News.content:
Hapless, hopeless and utterly humiliated. And that has to be that for Michael Carrick. It is surely inconceivable that he will continue any longer as Manchester United’s head coach. A proud club on its knees and a favoured son on his way out.

The former midfielder will carry the can. As managers always do. Even if the fault lines run so deep at United that it feels like they are almost irreparable. Owners – the Glazers and Sir Jim Ratcliffe – executives, players. A collective failing of monumental proportions. Although, again, it will be the manager who goes. Carrick knows it and it looked like it at the end. He knows the score, especially after this score.

More than four years ago Ralf Rangnick, the then interim manager, declared that United needed “open heart surgery”. Now there is barely a pulse.

An announcement must be imminent, with United turning to someone else in the fight against Premier League relegation. A joke? No, this abject performance against Bournemouth leaves United in 16th place, just a point above the bottom three, so the priority for the new man will be clear. Save them from the drop. They are 14 points off the top already, but forget that. It is irrelevant given their plight.

News.title: Trafford shows England credentials to help Leeds take point from Sunderland
News.content:
The two moments of quality came for the Leeds goalkeeper. Brian Brobbey is such a key part of what Sunderland do and his return to lead the attack gave the Wearsiders the focal point up front that they sorely missed in recent games.

But the Netherlands international could not give his side the lead thanks to two pieces of excellent goalkeeping from Trafford.

The 24-year-old left Manchester City to play regularly and has arguably been the best goalkeeper in the Premier League so far this season.

The two saves he made to deny Brobbey were very different, but equally impressive. The first was deceptively hard. Although the connection on the shot from the edge of the area was not the cleanest, that almost made it harder as the ball’s flight was difficult to pick up. The bounce just in front of the goalkeeper meant he had to watch it all the way and keep a strong hand at full stretch.

The second was, arguably, even better. Trafford was in a really vulnerable position, well outside his six yard box in a one-on-one with the Netherlands international. The way he stood up and timed when to move for the ball was superb especially as an error could have led to a penalty.

He may have saved with his feet, but he cramped Brobbey for room and timed his moment to dive at his feet perfectly. That was elite-level goalkeeping in a really tricky situation that favoured the striker.

Trafford made another two fine stops in the second half too, both from Nilson Angulo. The first getting down low to tip another bouncing ball wide and the second punching another deflected effort away.

Sunderland will feel like they shaded the battle, but Robin Roefs also made two decent stops from long range shots in the second half while Lukas Nmecha had an injury-time effort cleared off the line.

News.title: England pay price for toothless bowling in astonishing defeat by Pakistan
News.content:
Hello and welcome to live, over-by-over coverage of Pakistan v England in Lahore. In the UK, the clocks went back an hour overnight; England would love to wind them back 72 hours and have another go at defending 429 against Sri Lanka. That unfathomable defeat in Rawalpindi has left them on the brink in this tri-series.

England won’t be mathematically eliminated if they lose to Pakistan today, but it would leave them needing snookers if they are to reach Saturday’s final. Realistically, they need to win the last two group games, and there’s a chance even that might not be enough.

“It’s my first tri-series and it replicates World Cup styles and pressures,” said the England all-rounder Will Jacks. “You can’t replicate that in training or a bilateral series. In World Cups you have to bounce back. I remember in 2019 when England lost a couple of games in the group and they had to win their last two and they were able to do that to take the momentum forward.

“I’m not saying it’s the same thing but it’s a mini version of that and hopefully we can win on Sunday and move on. We have the opportunity to play in two must-win fixtures. Sometimes you learn more in losses than you do in wins.”

Jacks’ Surrey team-mate Sam Curran suffered the most against Sri Lanka, conceding an eye-watering 103 from his nine overs.

“They were incredibly hard conditions to bowl in and he bowls a lot of pressure overs – that’s his role in the team,” said Jacks. “He’s been so successful with that for England over a number of years. There are some days where it doesn’t quite work.”

Curran has kept his place in the side – but Josh Tongue is replaced by Henry Crocombe, who makes his international debut. And there’s no recall for Adil Rashid. We’ll have the toss and full team news in a moment.

News.title: Most expensive goal in Liverpool history gives Iraola era lift-off
News.content:
This was an important afternoon for Liverpool’s head coach, a difficult assignment against high-flying, well-respected opponents in Brighton, who arrived on Merseyside having won their last four Premier League fixtures with a combined aggregate of 15-0, including a 3-0 thumping of reigning champions Arsenal.

But Liverpool rose impressively to the challenge and there are grounds for saying this was the most significant success to date for Iraola, whose team defended relentlessly to preserve a clean sheet. They are up to fourth now after this 2-0 success and deserve their position.

“I’m very happy,” Iraola said. “We faced a very good opponent, similar to Villarreal [in the Champions League]. It’s difficult to defend them a lot of times and it was key how we started. We needed to be aggressive, recover balls, win our duels, be dangerous in transitions: I think we’ve done it.”

And how. Iraola was able to march towards the Kop at the end, to clap the supporters and acknowledge only Liverpool’s fifth (and his first) Premier League win at Anfield in 2026, and it was evident he had a spring in his step from what he had seen.

Whether the game would have flowed in the direction it did had Brighton taken the lead can only be speculated but what a glorious chance they wasted for us to find out: in the 13th minute, five swift, one-touch passes bamboozled Liverpool’s defence and created space for Yasin Ayari.

With the goal at his mercy, Ayari could have made things exceptionally uncomfortable but he leant back and blazed over. He clasped his face and grimaced, knowing what had gone begging in front of the Kop; four minutes later, his misery was exacerbated.

News.title: Antonelli takes another step closer to F1 title with US GP pole position
News.content:
Welcome to our live coverage for qualifying for the 2026 United States Grand Prix at the Circuit of the Americas, just outside of Austin. This is one of the finest tracks that we have on the Formula One calendar and is a fitting place for the US Grand Prix. The races are usually entertaining, the drivers love the track (though have complained about the bumps this year) and it comfortably the best on-track action of the three races in the US.

What might we see this weekend? Well, Kimi Antonelli could be crowned world champion if results go his way. The way the results need to go make that fairly unlikely, but stranger things have happened in F1 and they often do. In any case, it would take a catastrophic implosion for Antonelli to lose the championship from here, so it is a case of when rather than if.

Who looks in good form? Well, Ferrari do. They have brought an updated car here this weekend it, so far, is paying off. Charles Leclerc had good pace yesterday and Lewis Hamilton, his team-mate, was fastest earlier today in final practice. Hamilton’s time of 1min34.893sec was a tenth or two quicker than the Red Bull of Max Verstappen, with Leclerc not too far behind. Then it was Antonelli, George Russell in the second Mercedes and Oscar Piastri making up the top six, though the Australian was nearly half a second off the ultimate pace of Hamilton.

Qualifying begins in about 50 minutes and we will be here with all the updates from that.

News.title: Sensational Spurs storm Stamford Bridge as Palmer loses his head
News.content:
Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso has told Cole Palmer he must learn from his red card that contributed to his team’s London derby defeat by Tottenham Hotspur.

Tottenham head coach Roberto De Zerbi insisted Palmer should have seen red for shoving his pelvis into the face of Mateus Fernandes. But, having got off with a yellow card, the Chelsea midfielder then fouled substitute Conor Gallagher.

“I haven’t seen them [the yellow cards] on TV, but as far as I have been told, he [the referee] probably got it right,” Alonso said. “So, for sure for Cole, but for everyone. We think [up until] now we haven’t received any red cards [this season] and we need to continue that way because we need to have this maturity to deal with difficult moments, when you have conceded 1-0, there was still 15-20 minutes to go, so we have to be calm. I need to check the action to talk with Cole, but it is one to learn for the future for sure.”

Asked if he thought Palmer should have been sent off for the first yellow card, De Zerbi, who was booked for his protests, replied: “Yep.”

Jordan Henderson had spoken to Palmer at the end of the previous week’s victory over Everton in which the forward could also have been booked for a second time and sent off.

But Alonso claimed he does not have any wider concerns about Palmer’s character. He said: “Today, for sure, yes, but it is not a [wider] concern. I think that Cole when he is focused on the game, when he is enjoying and today after the 1-0, it is a moment to keep calm, a moment to keep mature and for everyone.”

De Zerbi hailed his side’s character and claimed that Tottenham have “suffered enough” after two 17th-placed finishes and a slow start to the season until successive victories over Coventry City and Chelsea.

“We want to improve, improve and improve, to be better game by game, week by week. I think we have suffered enough,” De Zerbi said. “Changing the spirit of the group, changing the performance of the players, especially the more fragile players, maybe the younger players. We played very well. Great individual performances, great collective performance because we played very well. And then we put something different than Tottenham, I think, in the last period. Different attitude, different relationships with the players, different group.”

Chelsea were without João Pedro because of an injury and Alonso is waiting to find out how long the striker will be out.

“We don’t know yet because he has a lot of fluid,” Alonso said. “So he felt it yesterday [Friday] and we need to wait probably until tomorrow [Sunday] to do the test and to know the whole situation and the whole seriousness of the injury. We will know soon enough.”

News.title: Pollock at heart of scuffle that inspires Leicester to thumping win in feisty derby
News.content:
Hello and welcome to our live coverage of Leicester Tigers v Northampton Saints.

The Prem’s derby weekend continues today at Mattioli Woods Welford Road, where Geoff Parling’s side go head-to-head in with their East Midlands rivals.

Both Leicester and Northampton have two wins from the opening three rounds of the season and with both sides involved in a number of high-scoring encounters already in the new campaign, we could be in for a real treat.

Tigers started the season with a 38-40 loss at home to Saracens, but bounced back quickly with wins over Gloucester and Newcastle Red Bulls. They will be itching to right a few wrongs after suffering a chastening Champions Cup defeat in Pau last week.

Northampton, meanwhile, have notched up wins over Newcastle Red Bulls and Bath either side of loss to Bristol Bears.

A win today for Saints would be their first on the road since defeating Exeter Chiefs at Sandy Park in April.

“It (the East Midlands derby) means a lot to everyone, we know it will be a great atmosphere at Mattioli Woods Welford Road,” said Parling.

“I don’t think with this sort of game either team has to build it up too much emotionally because that just comes, so I think it’s actually about being really really calm in the moment.”

“Hopefully we can put the best of ourselves out there and I’m sure Saints will be able to do exactly the same.”

Saints are without a victory in Leicester since January 2023, when a single point decided the 18-19 result.

Since then, the last five meetings between the sides have been won by the hosts on the day – with Saints last taking home the bragging rights when a Tom Litchfield hat-trick helped Northampton to a 45-31 win on home soil in last season’s league play-off.

Kick-off gets underway at 3.05pm. Stay with us here for all the latest updates.

News.title: Saliba has fight on his hands to usurp ‘unbelievable’ Konsa
News.content:
From the moment Ezri Konsa pulled on an Arsenal shirt, he has moved with all the composure of a man who knows exactly where to be and when. The centre-back has required no adaptation period in north London, where he has filled the considerable shoes of William Saliba with such class that Arsenal have hardly missed the Frenchman at all.

The loss of Saliba to a long-term back injury was supposed to be a major problem for Arsenal. Instead, the situation has now reached a point where some fans are wondering how Saliba will get back into the side. That may prove a little extreme, but the fact there is even a discussion is proof of Konsa’s superb impact at the Emirates Stadium.

“Unbelievable,” Mikel Arteta, the Arsenal manager, said of his £55m signing. “He’s come to a huge club and to position yourself in that manner, and to perform at the level he is, it is very difficult to do. We are really lucky to have him.”

In Arsenal’s latest victory, their seventh from eight matches in the Premier League this season, Konsa offered all of his usual defensive security and calmness in possession. Even more excitingly, he also scored his first goal for the club, smashed in from close range after a corner had caused chaos in Everton’s penalty area. It was Arsenal’s first set-piece goal of the season.

Sports.title: Gary Neville blasts Man Utd ‘bluffers’ who downed tools on doomed Michael Carrick in Bournemouth horror show
Sports.content:
Next

GARY NEVILLE slammed Manchester United’s “bluffers” who simply gave up on a tearful Michael Carrick.

The former defender and noisy pundit believes the writing is on the wall for his “hurt” ex-team-mate, who appears aware of his impending doom.



Few managers could mitigate the shambolic defending on display during United’s 3-0 defeat to Bournemouth at Old Trafford.

Carrick appeared glossy-eyed as he thanked the Stretford End while they sang his chant, perhaps for the final time.



But those same fans immediately turned on the rudderless players, unleashing a brutal chorus of boos on the sorry squad after Carrick was out of sight down the tunnel.

Neville said: “Michael will be hurting badly. The Manchester United fans are singing the Michael Carrick song because I think they know what’s going to happen here.



“They’ve seen this before. He’s one of their own and he’s popular.

“But the owners, the sporting department and the players are not popular and they’ve badly let this football club down.

“Omar Berrada and Jason Wilcox are probably going to make a decision that will disgust United fans, but it’s probably necessary. It’s just an absolute mess.”

The home support vented unprecedented, blood-letting abuse at Wilcox and the Ineos-appointed board after Evanilson secured a third 3-0 win for Bournemouth at Old Trafford in four years.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Untied fans chanted for Carrick in-between spells of “Jason Wilcox you’re a w**r”, “Sell United and f*** off home” and bonfire threats at the MIA Glazers family, who have saddled the club with £1.1billion debt.

Carrick said: “It’s really mixed emotions, I didn’t really expect that of the supporters, if I’m honest, but I’ve always felt the support and always felt that connection with them anyway.

“Probably sick of me saying all the times I’ve sat here and said it, the respect that I have for them and for them to kind of show that back meant an awful lot.”

Dreadful individual errors from the young defensive duo Leny Yoro and Ayden Heaven compounded another lifeless performance from the side Carrick tried to inspire during Friday’s press conference.



Carrick had recalled unselfish United legends of the past to inspire a response after United’s 4-1 Como capitulation in the Champions League on Wednesday.

Neville added: “They’ve downed tools this lot. I’ve been watching United for 40 years and I know what I’m seeing.

“Roy Keane has said these players are ‘bluffers’ in the past and he’s absolutely right. They’re bluffers.

“They pick and choose when they want to run and fight and put in the effort required. They’ve completely stopped trying for Carrick.

“It is going to get ridiculously difficult for Michael Carrick to be Manchester United manager moving forward. That’s the problem the club have got.”



Defeat leaves United 16th in the table with seven points after eight Premier League games, while the Cherries climb to 13th.

The pre-match narrative surrounded Bruno Fernandes, with the United captain dropped to the bench after he blamed Carrick’s tactics for their 4-1 defeat by Como on Wednesday – though the manager said it was a “football decision”.

But despite trailing 2-0 at half-time, Fernandes, so often United’s talisman, was not brought on. The reigning player of the year, so often the hero, is now grouped with the pathetic rest.

Sky pundit Jaime Carragher said: “Carrick was never going to bring him on. It was a deliberate decision to leave him on the bench to try and almost embarrass him.

“It’s a rancid dressing room. There is obviously a massive friction between the manager and United’s best player.



“It’s become untenable. Carrick wants to be changed. He doesn’t want to be sat in the dugout with those players.

“Can you imagine going into the training ground tomorrow with Bruno Fernandes after not bringing him on? He wants to be put out of his misery.”

Carrick looks set to leave with his head held high. The fans know the rot stops way above the dugout, and Carrick himself has earned respect by refusing to throw the board and players under the bus.

In what could be his final press conference, the United head coach failed to concede that fans need to hear more from Wilcox and Co after admitting he “felt” for most of the players.

Quizzed if he expects the chop, Carrick said: “It wasn’t farewell from me. I totally understand the situation. I am not expecting anything, I am carrying on as normal, I love this place, always carrying on doing what I think is the best for the football club.”



United have not won a game of football in 45 days, since the 4-0 win over Azerbaijani minnows Sabah on September 10.

The club, which finished third last season, has suffered six defeats in 12 games with Chelsea up next.

Carrick was set up to fail after the club spent just £163m on four new players, the bulk of it on £155m midfield trio Carlos Baleba, Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos.

United were outspent by Ipswich and Hull, while Carrick was left with the same back line that got two managers sacked before him.

RHODRI GIGGS has launched a stunning X-rated attack on Gary Neville amid Manchester United’s growing crisis.

The brother of Red Devils legend Ryan Giggs took aim at the former United captain following Sunday’s humiliating 3-0 defeat to Bournemouth.



Michael Carrick’s struggling side were booed off at Old Trafford after extending their winless run to eight matches in all competitions.

Sports.title: Sunderland 0 Leeds 0: Black Cats still rooted to bottom of Premier League table as poor start to season rages on
Sports.content:
Next

SUPER SUNDAY turned into a goalless snoozefest as toothless Sunderland continue to sleepwalk towards trouble.

Given the bad blood between the two goes way back to 1973 when the then Second Division Black Cats beat Don Revie’s star-studded side to lift the FA Cup, fans expected a thriller.



Instead they were served up a dour stalemate that left Regis Le Bris’ team rooted to the foot of the table.

Even the return of Brian Brobbey failed to provide any inspiration as Sunderland’s winless run in the top-flight extended to six,



Following an outstanding display against Arsenal’s physical backline, the Dutchman was unstoppable last month when firing a hat-trick past Manchester City.

Unfortunately for the Black Cats, that momentum came to an abrupt end when he picked up a hamstring injury on September 24 against Germany.



Without him, Sunderland failed to land a glove on either Brighton or Bournemouth, each time slipping to 2-0 defeats, as their losing run stretched to four as they sank to the bottom of the table.

But Brobbey did not take long to get back in the swing of it as he returned to lead the attack here.

Only eight minutes were on the clock when he had James Trafford scrambling to his right to save his first effort.

Though the powerhouse wasted the best chance of the game midway through the opening period as those watching struggled to keep their eyes open in the borefest.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

Captain Granit Xhaka nicked it off Harry Wilson, Jaka Bijol underhit the looseball back to his goalie under pressure from the striker, who charged on to it only to shoot right at the rapid Trafford’s midriff.

That was about as good as it got for either side.

High-flying Leeds barely laid a glove on the hosts despite Luke O’Nien’s vulnerability at the back.

The centre-half was twice caught off-guard by a ball over the top by Dominic Calvert-Lewin but escaped by the skin of his teeth both times.



O’Nien brought the proceedings to halt moments after the break when his inadvertent elbow left partner Nordi Mukiele seeing stars.

Following a lengthy delay, the Frenchman was forced off and replaced by Omar Alderete, the Paraguayan axed after a disastrous showing last week at Bournemouth, but still Daniel Farke’s side failed to take advantage.

Tarik Muharemovic headed straight at Robin Roefs in the 56th minute with their first effort on target.

Brobbey was in the thick of it again, holding off his marker to lay it to Xhaka to slip it wide for Nilson Angulo to whack one from the left, Trafford getting down low to his left to save.



Next it was Sunderland’s magician Enzo Le Fee turning provider for the Ecuadorian winger, though Leeds’ stopper palmed away.

Le Bris’ decision to replace Brobbey with Timur Tutierov just after the hour did not go down well.

The Ukrainian was his Crimean Cannonball on Thursday, scoring in the Europa League at Lech Poznan, but he made little impact here.

And it was thanks to Roefs down the opposite end that they emerged with a point. First he lunged to keep out Ao Tanaka’s turn and shot.



Then ex-Newcastle star Sean Longstaff with his first touch after coming off the bench pulled the trigger from 20 yards but the flying Dutchman tipped wide to leave Leeds sitting seventh.

MANCHESTER UNITED are yet to tell Michael Carrick whether he will be sacked after the feeble 3-0 home defeat to Bournemouth.

Carrick spoke with chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox post-match, but the pair tend to visit the dressing room after games.



United supporters aired sinister songs about former Leeds winger Wilcox and the club’s owners, the Glazer family and Sir Jim Ratcliffe.

Carrick was serenaded throughout the humbling and was applauded as he headed down the tunnel at full-time.



After Carrick vanished from view, the United players were booed at the end of a week that captain Bruno Fernandes publicly questioned Carrick’s tactics in the 4-1 reverse at Como.

United are now eight games without a win and have lost six in 12. A change of head coach is expected in a week where the club do not have a midweek fixture.

Antonio Conte, Eddie Howe and Julian Nagelsmann are all out of work and in the running to replace Carrick. Brighton coach Fabian Hurzeler is considered the outstanding Premier League candidate but would command a hefty fee.

MANCHESTER UNITED’S under-fire boss Michael Carrick “deliberately” dumped captain Bruno Fernandes on the bench during the Bournemouth mauling to “embarrass” him after his tantrum at Como, Jamie Carragher has claimed.

Carrick’s position at United is now in severe peril after a miserable 3-0 loss to the Cherries at Old Trafford, which marked his sixth loss out of 13 matches – of which he only won three – across all competitions this season.



Man Utd‘s legendary midfielder is overseeing his beloved club’s worst start to a campaign in 40 years and an eight-game winless run.

Rumours of an imminent sacking gained momentum after another heavy Champions League loss on Wednesday when Como beat the Red Devils 4-1 in Italy.

The 45-year-old tactician went on to drop the playmaker to the bench for the first time in five years against Bournemouth and never brought him on, even though his side were trailing by two goals at half-time.

Sports.title: Harry Kane set for tasty prize if he wins Ballon d’Or with the whole of Germany cheering on England star
Sports.content:
Next

IN GERMANY, we show our love with beer and food.

If we like you, we give you beer and if we really like you, we give you lots of beer.



If we love you, we give you schnitzel.

There is a country pub near the house of Harry Kane south of Munich, and the owner delivers him and his family a schnitzel for every goal he scores.



As you can imagine, that’s a lot of schnitzels since Harry moved to Bayern from Tottenham three years ago.

This schnitzel story tells a lot about the relationship between Kane and Germany — since he arrived almost everybody has fallen in love with him.



And that is not just because of all the goals he scores and the great passes he plays.

It’s foremost because of the way he adapted to Germany and German football, how nice and humble he is, and how much respect he shows to everyone.

In Germany, we like the ‘normal’ football players, the guys who seem to be like you and me.

Sports.title: Michael Carrick admits ‘there’s no hiding from it’ as he risks sack after Man Utd’s woeful defeat to Bournemouth

MICHAEL CARRICK has admitted he does not know what comes next as his Manchester United future hangs in the balance.

The under-fire boss was left reeling after United were taken apart for the second time in a week, with Bournemouth running out 3-0 winners at Old Trafford for the third time in four seasons.



Carrick, 45, offered little reassurance over his position when speaking to Sky Sports after the final whistle.

He told Sky Sports: “It’s a tough situation. There’s no hiding from it. What it looks like, what’s next, I really don’t know.



“I always do what’s best for this football club. I’ve said it all along and I don’t change that now.

“I love what I do. I love the position I’m in. I feel the responsibility.”



The defeat followed Wednesday’s humiliating 4-1 loss to Cesc Fabregas‘ Como, piling further pressure on a manager who had enjoyed a promising spell in charge in the second half of last season.

Today, United were rocked by goals from Rayan and Marcus Tavernier before half-time, leaving the hosts with a mountain to climb.

Evanilson then struck in the second half to compound the misery and leave Carrick facing fresh questions over his team’s direction.

The manager admitted his players had been hurting after another damaging afternoon.

“We are disappointed and hurt in there. The players, or the ones I have spoken to, are feeling it.”

Carrick also acknowledged the difficult circumstances surrounding his team, with injuries and selection decisions adding to the challenge.

Asked about the hand of cards he had been dealt, including the recent comments made by Lisandro Martinez and Bruno Fernandes, he said: “It’s really difficult for me to have a day like this at this football club, to feel this emotion and dynamics of what it felt like – not for me personally, but for Man Utd.

“It was really mixed today, and I feel a lot of responsibility. It hurts a lot seeing us go through like this at this moment in time.



“There’s always times in games where you’re trying to make decisions to try and change the course of play. They were decisions we made today.”

The comments come after a turbulent couple of weeks behind the scenes at Old Trafford.

Martinez questioned the club’s hierarchy following the 2-0 defeat away to Atletico Madrid, and a week later Fernandes raised concerns over Carrick’s tactics after the Como thrashing.

Harry Maguire has voiced his support for Michael Carrick amid mounting calls for the Manchester United manager to be sacked. The Red Devils fell to yet another Premier League defeat at the hands of Bournemouth, with their last win in the league coming in August against Ipswich Town.

Despite this representing Carrick's third Premier League defeat in eight games, Maguire remains firmly in his manager's corner and believes the players themselves must shoulder the blame for their recent poor form.

‌



Reacting to the game on BBC MOTD, he said: "We're fully behind Michael [Carrick], coming into the team last season he turned things around and got Champions League football this season. As individuals, we're not playing well enough."

Maguire also gave a scathing overview of their Old Trafford display, stating that there was a crisis of confidence within the dressing room. He said: "Very disappointed. Coming to the game we wanted to get a win for our fans and to concede another set play for the first goal is not good enough.

There's a lack of confidence at the moment - the results, the performances we have to look at ourselves and find something within ourselves to bring more to the team.

‌



"That's every player that I'm talking about. When things aren't going your way you have to do the basics well and conceding set plays, a simple set play is just nowhere near good enough.

"It's an individual thing - we have to stick together as a team. So early on in the season - we can still have a good season but something has got to change quick. It's been disappointing, that has to change."

Carrick shouldered his share of the blame for the woeful result, conceding he feels a sense of "responsibility" for the way things are currently unfolding at United. He told Sky Sports: "It was a strange, mixed of emotions at the end of the game. It wasn't a nice way to end the game.

Gary Neville sends blunt Michael Carrick sack message and points finger of blame at Man Utd

Michael Carrick could be about to lose his job as Manchester United manager following their 3-0 thrashing by Bournemouth and Gary Neville has given his take on the situation

View 3 Images Gary Neville thinks Michael Carrick will be sacked (Image: Sky Sports)

Gary Neville says Michael Carrick won't last 24 hours as Manchester United manager after they were thrashed by Bournemouth, but believes the blame lies elsewhere.

‌



‌



United dropped to 16th place in the Premier League after their 3-0 defeat at Old Trafford on Sunday. Carrick was only appointed permanent boss in the summer, but could already be sacked just 12 games into the 2026/27 season.

‌



The 45-year-old has overseen just two wins all season, with their seven points from eight league games representing the club's worst start to campaign since 1986/87. United executives have already reportedly been sounding out replacements and key figures Jason Wilcox and Omar Berrada were inside Old Trafford to witness another miserable defeat on Sunday.

‌



Neville was on co-commentary for the match and let rip at the two club chiefs post-match, claiming his former team-mate was a "dead man walking" before the match even kicked off.

Sports.title: The game is up for Michael Carrick - but Man Utd are a shambles of a football club
Sports.content:
The game is up for Michael Carrick - but Man Utd are a shambles of a football club

MANCHESTER UNITED 0-3 BOURNEMOUTH: Michael Carrick will be the fall guy but Red Devils fans know where the blame lies for this latest malaise

View 2 Images Carrick appeared to wave goodbye to United fans after the game (Image: Manchester United via Getty Images)

A huge banner unfurled in the Stretford End said it all in one word. The message simply said: “Standards” written alongside pictures of Bryan Robson, Roy Keane and Eric Cantona.

‌



‌



How this great club has fallen. From the glory days of those Manchester United legends to this utter shambles at Old Trafford. Sadly, this must be the last rites for Michael Carrick’s reign because there is simply no way that he can survive this abject humiliation.

‌



At the final whistle, Carrick went to each corner of the ground as if he was saying goodbye. The game is up. It is always the manager who ends up paying.

‌



This will go down as one of the worst, most damaging and shocking defeats United have ever suffered at Old Trafford. You actually felt sorry for Carrick as he looked lost on the touchline.

‌



Carrick’s attempt to stir some of reaction with his emotional, heartfelt five-minute and 25 second monologue followed by the bold decision to drop Bruno Fernandes did not work.

Instead, yet another manager has been left heading for the scrapheap as Old Trafford should be renamed the Theatre of Nightmares.

‌



Carrick was clearly calling out United’s current generation when he said they should follow the example of there likes of Wayne Rooney and Sir Bobby Charlton by showing “sacrifice and hard work.”

But United were meek, spineless and pathetic. They showed no fight for the manager, no passion for the fans and were an absolute disorganised mess.

‌



Bournemouth played United off the pitch. They were sensational. But United were as bad as Bournemouth were good. By the end, Old Trafford had turned toxic.

The Stretford End was chanting: “Sell United, now f*** off home.” They turned on the Glazers and Sir Jim Ratcliffe. Then they saved the encore with a chorus of abuse for director of football Jason Wilcox.

‌



View 2 Images Omar Berrada and Jason Wilcox watch on at Old Trafford (Image: Getty Images)

Old Trafford was half empty by the final whistle and when United fans - some of the best and most loyal in the country - have given up then you know it is all over.

‌



This has descended into an ugly civil war. The club has lost its way thanks to bad ownership, bad recruitment and too many players who are not fit to wear this famous old shirt.

These days, the loudest rumbling from the Old Trafford crowd comes when Harry Maguire ventures forward. At least he showed some heart. But that is not enough.

‌



The real surprise was that it took Bournemouth so long to score. Ayden Heaven was booked for a mindless two-footed challenge. Justin Kluivert swung over a free kick and there was Brazil star Rayan completely unmarked to fire home at the back post after 38 minutes.

The second goal was comically bad. Lenny Yoro chased down a long ball, slipped and let in Adrien Truffert. His cross was turned home by Marcus Tavernier. That is when the United fans unfurled their Standards banner.

‌



United were just lucky that Bournemouth were so wasteful. It could have been five or six. The third goal came after 71 minutes.

Man Utd next manager odds as clear favourite emerges to replace Michael Carrick READ MORE :

‌



Lewis Cook’s long ball forward was chased down by Evanilson. The Bournemouth striker rounded keeper Senne Lammens and then showed fabulous skill to curl a shot into the top corner.

We used to expect those sort of great moments of magic from United. Now the opponents come to Old Trafford to showcase their talent and humiliate this once great club.

‌



Tellingly, Fernandes - the player dropped days after questioning Carrick’s tactics - never came off the bench. But no-one could really question that decision. He has been so poor this season. Yet another player blaming everyone but himself.

Even more revealing, the United fans chanted Carrick’s name just before the final whistle. At the end, Carrick was actually cheered as he went round the ground to thank the fans while thumping his chest to show the club is in his heart.

Article continues below

But those same fans let Carrick leave the pitch - and then turn their anger on the players who were roundly booed as they went down the tunnel. The Old Trafford faithful have decided who is to blame. And it is certainly not Carrick.

Michael Carrick is on the brink of being sacked after Manchester United were thrashed 3-0 by Bournemouth, but the real culprits for the club's mess were sat in the stands at Old Trafford

Sports.title: Liverpool blunt free-scoring Brighton as star man proves his worth in impressive win
Sports.content:
Liverpool produced a clinical first-half display to see off high-flying Brighton at a breezy Anfield.

Pascal Gross inadvertently turned into his own net to give the Reds the lead before Alexander Isak doubled their advantage in a four-minute burst to clip the Seagulls' wins.

Brighton huffed and puffed but could not find their scoring boots despite plundering 23 goals in their previous seven Premier League matches.

It was the visitors who had the first big chance as Yasin Arayi squandered a golden opportunity. Diego Gomez played in Pascal Gross whose pull-back fell perfectly into the path of Ayari, but he blazed over the bar with the goal at his mercy.

‌



Liverpool hit the front just three minutes later. Ronald Araujo showed grit and tenacity to jump up after being fouled, then fed Florian Wirtz whose wayward strike hit Gross and deflected past Bart Verbruggen.

The lead was soon doubled as Bradley Barcola pressed full-back Olivier Boscagli to win the ball high up the pitch. He crossed to Alexander Isak who finished exquisitely.

Alisson was almost punished for a careless pass out from the back 10 minutes before the break, Ayari striking the post. Araujo then went close for Liverpool but was thwarted by Verbruggen.

Brighton had the better of the second half but couldn't find a way through as Liverpool saw out the closing stages with relative ease.

‌



It's a result that takes the Reds back into the top four, a point behind the Seagulls and six off pace setters Manchester City and Arsenal.

Ron they got right

Some of Liverpool's recruitment has been questioned in the last couple of seasons, but Ronald Araujo has had an immediate positive impact at Anfield.

‌



The 27-year-old arrived from Barcelona in the summer on an initial season-long loan deal with an option to buy next summer for around £47million. On current form, that looks a bargain.

He was imperious here, especially in the first half. Araujo played a pivotal role in the first goal, driving forward and refusing to be stopped despite being fouled to provide Wirtz whose drive was deflected into the Brighton net.

And he could have had his first Premier League goal just before the break, bursting on to the ball and striking crisply on the angle, only to see his effort saved by Verbruggen.

While eyebrows have been raised in other quarters, Araujo is definitely one Liverpool got right.

‌



The Holy Trinity Version 2.0

View 2 Images Barcola set Isak up for Liverpool's second (Image: ADAM VAUGHAN/EPA/Shutterstock)

Barcola was always likely to prove himself a pivotal signing for Liverpool for years to come, and there are already signs of a new, exciting front three emerging at Anfield.

Mohamed Salah, Sadio Mane and Roberto Firmino established themselves as the Reds' holy trinity and fired them to success at home and on the continent.

Now Cody Gakpo, Isak and Barcola are bidding to follow in their footsteps. It's early days and, let's face it, they're unlikely to reach the heights of their predecessors.

‌



But there were encouraging moments from all three here, with Barcola setting up Isak for Liverpool's second goal and Gakpo a constant threat on the left.

Gakpo, of course, was the subject of interest from Manchester City in the summer and things could have worked out very differently. Now he looks a key cog in Andoni Iraola's side.

The Hurz could be yet to come

While this was a disappointing afternoon for Brighton, more pressing developments for their future might just have taken place 30 miles along the East Lancs Road.

Manchester United were humbled 3-0 by Bournemouth in a result that piles the pressure on Michael Carrick and may well see him sacked as Red Devils boss.

‌



There will of course be a clutch of candidates to succeed him if he does depart Old Trafford, and one of those looks likely to be Fabian Hurzeler.

The 33-year-old has made a huge impact at Brighton and they are still the division's top scorers despite failing to find the net today. The Seagulls sit third and this result in isolation will not worry them.

But an approach from United, despite their problems, would surely be difficult for Hurzeler to ignore. Brighton are experts in succession planning, but it would doubtless be a huge blow if the German was to jump ship.

Sports.title: Michael Carrick on brink as Man Utd fans make voices heard in Bournemouth hammering
Sports.content:
Manchester United's season plumbed new depths on Saturday as Bournemouth secured a comfortable victory on an afternoon where Old Trafford turned toxic.

A Bruno Fernandes-less Red Devils side lacked any spark with Michael Carrick now surely on the brink of losing his job as the Cherries won 3-0 at United for the third time in four years.

The hosts were two goals down by half-time with Rayan and Marcus Tavernier putting the Cherries on course for another success in Manchester. Evanilson capped the afternoon with a sensational third 20 minutes from time.

The two opening goals coming inside five minutes of the first half - Rayan finishing from a free-kick before Tavernier benefited from a defensive slip.

‌



United showed nothing by way of a fightback in the second-half and Evanilson was able to round Senne Lammens before finishing brilliant from out wide in front of the travelling fans.

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Bournemouth had the better of the early exchanges and found themselves bearing down on goal, but Rayan could not make the most of a three-on-one opportunity as his effort was blocked. United gradually got themselves back into the contest without posing any major threat.

‌



The deadlock was finally broken come the 37th minute as Rayan's side-footed finish at the back post opened the scoring. His goal coming from a free-kick that owed to a poor Ayden Heaven two-footed challenge, which only earned him a yellow card.

The travelling faithful quickly erupted into chants of 'you're getting sacked in the morning' as Carrick watched his side fall behind yet again. But things would get worse before the interval as Leny Yoro, being chased down by Adrien Truffert, slipped and that allowed the left-back to square the ball for Tavernier, who slotted into an empty net.

View 5 Images Michael Carrick is now without a win in eight with his job in major doubt

Matheus Cunha, not Fernandes, was the man called upon to change United's direction of travel as the hosts ran out for the second half, but only the offside flag prevented Bournemouth from going three goals up inside 30 seconds of the restart.

‌



Evanilson was deserving of his strike after 70 minutes as he curled home from far out after rounding the United goalkeeper, but come the dying stages Old Trafford had rafts of empty seats. The home fans had seen enough.

Those that remained at the Theatre of Dreams defiantly sung Carrick's name at full-time, instead reserving their ire for the players and ownership.

IS CARRICK'S BRUNO STATEMENT FINAL ACT?

With Fernandes, without Fernandes. There doesn't seem to be much of a difference when it comes to this United side. Carrick had little option but to drop his captain in light of the comments he made during the week. Was that going to be an example of self harm? Or did he have to show some authority?

In all honesty it probably didn't make much difference. United were seven games without a win with Fernandes in the team. That was extended to eight without him, and even with the Red Devils three goals down and needing a goal, the Portugal international remained glued to the bench with Carrick happy to go down without him. Cunha, Joshua Zirkzee and Shea Lacey all called upon instead.

‌



View 5 Images Bruno Fernandes was dropped to the bench and was forced to watch on

It would be remiss to claim that having Fernandes in the team would've changed the course of the afternoon. The Portuguese playmaker has not been replicating the form that made him the PFA Player of the Year last season.

His recent demise has mirrored that of his team, who were on a wave of momentum under Carrick last season as they rose up to third. This result now leaves them one point off being third from bottom as the Bournemouth fans sang that United were going down with City.

It isn't that bed, yet, but Carrick's latest and boldest roll of the dice has done nothing to change his fortunes, with time desperately running out.

‌



OLD TRAFFORD'S SEEN ENOUGH

When fans walk out before the half-time whistle you know you're in the midst of a low ebb. For all the dire afternoons at Old Trafford since 2013, the fans have showed more patience and staying power than the players, the managers and the hierarchy have deserved.

View 5 Images Evanilson capped Bournemouth's stellar outing with a third goal in the second-half (Image: Getty Images)

But in the midst of a seven game winless run, which was extended to eight, it was after Tavernier's goal that doubled Bournemouth lead that the camera panned to fans walking up the concourse and for the exit. That was only 42 minutes in, but they'd seen enough.

Even the boos, which have been more regular than ever this season, have been kept under wraps for the last decade considering the results and performances, but this feels like a real tipping point, and one that could see a major change, likely in the dugout.

‌



There was a huge black banner in the stands that read "standards". It had a images of those from yesteryear, when United were the dominant force. Nowadays they're a million miles from that, and things only seem to be getting worse.

View 5 Images Ayden Heaven was lucky to avoid a red card in the first-half

HEAVEN DODGES RED, BUT PAYS PRICE

Gary Neville remarked that we "don't see tackles like that anymore", half joking that the last time he saw a player fly in with two feet was in the 1980s when United great Bryan Robson was still playing.

The young defender is still very much a player learning his trade, but his poor tackle was lucky to escape a dismissal. VAR checked the challenge and claimed he stayed on the pitch only because he made no contact with Evanilson, who himself looked stunned that Heaven had even attempted such a tackle.

‌



To add insult to injury, it was from the resulting free-kick that Bournemouth scored their opening goal as Rayan volleyed home at the back post. Heaven himself was complaining for a foul as the delivery came in, but his complaint was surely born out of hope and not expectation. He and United simply got what they deserved.

Sports.title: Sheffield Wednesday SACK boss Henrik Pedersen after 11 games of League One season
Sports.content:
Sheffield Wednesday SACK boss Henrik Pedersen after 11 games of League One season

Following back-to-back defeats by Notts County and Doncaster, Sheffield Wednesday have sacked Henrik Pedersen as manager

View 2 Images Sheffield Wednesday have sacked Henrik Pedersen (Image: Greig Cowie/Shutterstock)

Sheffield Wednesday have sacked manager Henrik Pedersen. The Owls sit eighth in League One after back-to-back defeats by Notts County and Doncaster.

‌



‌



Pedersen took over as Wednesday boss before the start of last season, stepping up having been assistant manager to Danny Rohl.

‌



What followed was the worst season of any team in Football League history as the Owls amassed just 18 points over the course of the Championship campaign amid a backdrop of chaos.

‌



Wednesday were left with a skeleton squad of misfits and kids following the neglect of ex-owner Dejphon Chansiri. He was forced out and administration followed.

The club was deducted 18 points meaning they only reached zero on the final day of the season with their first home win of the season against West Brom.

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Wednesday's takeover by US-based consortium Arise was finalised on the same day, and after giving Pedersen a chance with a squad containing 18 new players for League One, they have now opted to make a change.

‌



Former Owls player and Rotherham manager Matt Hamshaw, part of Pedersen's coaching staff, will step up as interim boss until a new manager is named.

Sporting Director Simon Wilson said: “First and foremost, I want to thank Henrik for his professionalism, commitment and contribution during an exceptionally challenging period for Sheffield Wednesday.

‌



“We knew the start of this season would be difficult due to the scale of change across the club, but our expectation was always that we would develop as the season progressed, establishing a recognisable style of play and greater consistency in our performances.

“Although we have accumulated points, we haven’t seen enough progress in those areas. We believe making a change now gives us the best opportunity to establish those foundations and build towards the second half of the season and beyond.

‌



View 2 Images Former Rotherham boss Matt Hamshaw has taken caretaker charge of Wednesday (Image: CameraSport via Getty Images)

“We remain ambitious about what we can achieve this campaign, and our focus remains on building a Sheffield Wednesday team with a clear identity, capable of delivering sustained improvement and long-term success.”

‌



Wednesday started the season in positive fashion, winning four of their opening five fixtures. But home goalless draws against Wigan and Stockport followed.

The Owls beat AFC Wimbledon 5-0 on Saturday but the reverses at Meadow Lane and in a South Yorkshire derby at Doncaster have proved the tipping point for Pedersen.

Article continues below

Fans angrily chanted for him to be removed as boss and they have got their wish. Wednesday face Cambridge at Hillsborough on Tuesday night.

Sports.title: Rodgers backs 16-game 'NFL International week' after Paris history
Sports.content:
Aaron Rodgers endorsed the introduction of an international week to the NFL season as he led the Pittsburgh Steelers to victory over the New Orleans Saints at the Stade de France in Paris on Sunday.

Rodgers and the Steelers made history last year when they beat the Minnesota Vikings in the NFL's Dublin debut at Croke Park, before travelling overseas again this week to deliver another milestone moment for the league in the French capital.

NFL Commissioner Roger Goodell revealed on Friday that the league has plans to play a game in Tokyo, Japan in either 2027 or 2028, with wider ambitions of reaching 16 international games per season.

"I really look forward to that. We know that soccer worldwide probably has the most amount of fans. If you watch the World Cup at all, you know how fanatical the people for their country teams are. But the NFL is still shown in a number of countries, the Super Bowl is shown in over 100 countries; the reach of the league is fantastic," said Rodgers.

"I think I always wanted to be a part of it. I remember the 2011 CBA, there was talk about expanding the amount of international games, didn't really a whole lot until the second CBA.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player NFL commissioner Roger Goodell explains how the league is following Formula 1's model with international games, but adds that they may explore creating an international franchise or division.

"And there was talk about doing an international week, where you had games in 16 different places and you just added an extra bye week. I think it would have been phenomenal for the game.

"Now that the owners want to push for 17 games for the extra revenue and because they care so much about player safety. But it would have been nice."

Sunday's game in Paris featured as part of a record nine international games being played during the 2026 campaign, joining Melbourne and Rio de Janeiro as the league's newest host territories.

The NFL will now head to Madrid, Munich and Mexico City over the next month amid what has taken shape as a Formula 1-style format.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Aaron Rodgers passed Peyton Manning for the third-most touchdown passes in NFL history

"You could do obviously Canada, you could do Mexico," Rodgers continued. "There's been games in Brazil. You could probably open up another country in South America. Obviously there's a lot of opportunities in Europe, Ireland is fantastic, France, Spain, Germany, multiple games in England. And then who knows?

"There's Dubai, those areas really got into the sporting world in a number of ways, you got boxing and UFC, so I think there's great opportunities for expansion in those.

"It'd be awesome to see them have an international week because I think it's great for the game and the expansion of the game."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Rodgers gives his reaction after his side beat the New Orleans Saints

The Steelers arrived late into Paris this week as they landed on Friday morning before heading straight into media availability at their hotel. Rodgers said at the time he wished the team had flown in at the beginning of the week as the Saints had.

Arrival time has become a prominent talking point surrounding the NFL's international games, the Rams landing in Melbourne just a day before their defeat to the San Francisco 49ers. It came a year after Sean McVay's side dominated the Jacksonville Jaguars at Wembley Stadium having flown in on the eve of the game, a strategy that did not work in Australia.

"I wish there was a mandate from the league and they would have to open up their pocketbooks, too, which, you know, maybe a little tight on money and stuff," said Rodgers.

"But I think they should mandate every team coming over Sunday or Monday to really enjoy the culture and the place you're going. And you can do events in those cities and outreach stuff and community work. But they won't because they're a little tight."

Sports.title: Carrick future in huge doubt as Man Utd consider alternatives
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick's future as Manchester United head coach is hanging by a thread.

United plunged to a new low on Sunday as they were beaten 3-0 at Old Trafford by Bournemouth. The defeat extends their winless run to eight matches and leaves United just above the Premier League relegation zone.

Sky Sports News understands that United's bosses were already considering alternatives for the head coach role even before the defeat to Bournemouth amid the club's worst-ever start to a Premier League season.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Michael Carrick was applauded off the Old Trafford pitch following defeat to Bournemouth, but the same couldn't be said about the Manchester United players

The United hierachy will now accelerate that process, with an expectation from insiders at the club that Carrick will be relieved of his duties.

That decision will ultimately come down to director of football Jason Wilcox and chief executive Omar Berrada, who will make a recommendation to co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe.

Carragher calls for quick decision as fearful Neville predicts sacking

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player FREE TO WATCH: Highlights from Manchester United’s match against Bournemouth in the Premier League

Carrick's position looked to have become untenable as Bournemouth stormed to a deserved victory on Sunday in which United were a distant second-best. With captain Bruno Fernandes benched for the duration of the game following his midweek criticism of Carrick's tactics, United were fortunate to only lose by three goals.

"It is going to get ridiculously difficult for Michael Carrick to be Manchester United manager moving forward. That's the problem the club have got," said Neville during Sky Sports' match commentary. On his podcast, Neville concluded: "They are probably going to sack him. Tomorrow, they will probably make a decision that will disgust Manchester United fans but it is probably necessary."

"Michael Carrick needs to be relieved of his duties tonight," added Jamie Carragher. "Not just for the good of Manchester United but also for the good of Michael Carrick. It has become untenable."

Who are the contenders to replace Carrick?

Image: Eddie Howe, Julian Nagelsmann, Unai Emery and Antonio Conte

Sky Sports News' Rob Dorsett and Dan Khan:

If Carrick is to depart, Julian Nagelsmann and Eddie Howe are the two front runners to take over at Old Trafford. Both are available to start quickly, and neither would require any compensation to be paid. Howe, when he resigned as Newcastle manager in July, said he wanted to take a break from football to recharge his batteries. But Sky Sports News has been told he would be interested in talking to United, should a vacancy become available.

Howe was recommended by United's former sporting director Dan Ashworth as a suitable candidate in the past, having got to know him well during his time at Newcastle. Wilcox, United's current director of football, is thought to favour hiring a coach with Premier League experience.

Nagelsmann is well known to United's head of recruitment, Christopher Vivell, after the two men worked closely together at RB Leipzig. The former Bayern Munich boss has been out of work since stepping down as Germany head coach following a disastrous World Cup which saw the side knocked out by Paraguay in the round of 32 in the summer.

Unai Emery and Antonio Conte have also been considered by United as possible replacements, but they aren't thought to be among the current favourites. Emery, we have been told, remains committed to the project at Aston Villa.

But Carragher backing Emery candidature

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jamie Carragher reacts to Man Utd's 3-0 defeat at home to Bournemouth and criticises all aspects of the club

However, Carragher believes Aston Villa's Unai Emery should be United's first target.

"He is a manager I look at when I think about Manchester United," said Carragher. "I think Emery is the best manager in the Premier League. But I've got this thing with him. Yes, his record in the Europa League is amazing, but surely somebody who is that successful wants to be known in the Champions League.

"He wants to win the Champions League. He's not going to do that at Aston Villa.

"He's had two experiences that haven't gone particularly well for him, Paris Saint-Germain and Arsenal. And I just think surely he would want that opportunity to prove himself at an absolute giant of a football club. Sorry, Villa fans."

Sports.title: Neville fears Carrick set to be sacked as Carra calls for decision tonight
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick looks poised to lose his job as Manchester United head coach following their 3-0 defeat at Old Trafford to Bournemouth, according to Gary Neville and Jamie Carragher.

The humbling defeat leaves United just above the relegation zone following their worst-ever start to a Premier League season.

"It is going to get ridiculously difficult for Michael Carrick to be Manchester United manager moving forward. That's the problem the club have got," said Neville during Sky Sports' match commentary.

On his podcast, Neville concluded: "They are probably going to sack him."

Carrick struck a defiant tone after the game but his lengthy applause towards the United fans after the final whistle was immediately interpreted as a farewell gesture.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Carrick was applauded off the Old Trafford pitch following defeat to Bournemouth, but the same couldn't be said about the Manchester United players

"Michael Carrick needs to be relieved of his duties tonight," added Jamie Carragher. "Not just for the good of Manchester United but also for the good of Michael Carrick.

"Manchester United need to make that decision tonight."

Carrick led United to Champions League football after taking over from Ruben Amorim in mid-season last year, but United are winless in their last eight matches amid a wretched start to the current campaign.

"I did think last season that the club should have gone for the best manager they could have got and not given the job to Michael Carrick because I felt this might happen. But this has gone very, very sour very quickly and the club is a mess," said Neville.

Carrick's name was chanted loudly by the Old Trafford faithful following Bournemouth's game-sealing third goal but Neville fears that time may already be up for his former team-mate.

"Carrick is popular. But the owners, the sporting department and the players are not popular. They have badly let the club down.

"Tomorrow, they will probably make a decision that will disgust Manchester United fans but it is probably necessary.

"The Manchester United fans are singing Carrick's name because the reality tomorrow is: will he be the manager?

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Michael Carrick explains why he dropped captain Bruno Fernandes

Bruno Fernandes was dropped from the match on Sunday after he criticised Carrick's tactics in the wake of Wednesday's 4-1 thrashing at Como in the Champions League. Surprisingly, the United captain stayed on the bench for the entirety of the defeat to Bournemouth.

It's become untenable," summarised Carragher. "Carrick wants to be changed. He doesn't want to be sat in the dugout with those players.

"Can you imagine going into the training ground tomorrow with Bruno Fernandes after not bringing him on? It's a rancid dressing room. He wants to be put out of his misery tonight."

Sports.title: Isak on target again as Liverpool beat Brighton
Sports.content:
Alexander Isak scored for a third straight Premier League game as Liverpool inflicted only Brighton's second loss of the season.

Isak's goal, finished emphatically from Bradley Barcola's right-wing cut-back, came four first-half minutes after Pascal Gross had diverted a Florian Wirtz shot into his own net.

Brighton arrived at Anfield having scored 23 goals in their first seven games of the season but lacked a clinical edge, with Yasin Ayari blazing a golden chance over moments before the opener.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Pascal Gross deflected in Florian Wirtz's shot for the opener

Ayari later struck the post with a curling effort from outside the box as Brighton finished the game with only one shot on target despite having 64 per cent of the possession.

Trey Nyoni, a second-half substitute for Wirtz, who went down the tunnel after taking a knock to his ankle, also made a crucial, last-ditch tackle to deny Maxim De Cuyper in the Liverpool box.

The hosts had chances to add to their lead, wasting several counter-attacks and drawing Bart Verbruggen saves from Ronald Araujo and Cody Gakpo. But their first-half flurry proved sufficient to secure a first Premier League home win under Andoni Iraola.

The result takes them above Chelsea into fourth in the Premier League, only a point behind Brighton, who taste defeat for the first time since August. Liverpool's fourth win in a row in all competitions also provides further evidence of their attack finally clicking.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Alexander Isak buried Bradley Barcola's cut-back for the second goal

Isak's goal, his sixth of the season in the Premier League, came after fine work by summer signing Barcola, who stole possession high up the pitch before driving forward and picking out his team-mate.

Iraola starting to put his stamp on Liverpool

Momentum is building for Liverpool under Iraola. It's four wins in a row now and eight in 10 going back to the start of September.

They had to ride their luck at times. Brighton should have been in front before their opener. But the hosts were rewarded for attacking quickly and directly, in the style of their head coach.

Liverpool won possession in the final third five times - their second-highest total in the Premier League this season. Iraola values speed and incisiveness above possession, so the fact they had a meagre share of the ball is unlikely to concern him.

Image: Ferdi Kadioglu and Ryan Gravenberch battle for possession early on at Anfield

Instead, he will take satisfaction from the contributions of his attacking players. Barcola provided an assist for a second straight Premier League game, this time having been swapped to the right flank. Isak led the line with another clinical display.

Wirtz had bright moments too, taking the shot that forced the opening goal before coming off in the second half, while Rio Ngumoha, their star man in the midweek win over Villarreal, was only needed for a quarter of an hour with Gakpo also impressing.

Wirtz downplays injury fears Florian Wirtz insisted the injury that forced him off against Brighton is not serious.



The Liverpool playmaker had be be replaced by Trey Nyoni after appearing to hurt his ankle.



"I think it will be alright, it's not too bad," he said. "I don't know much yet. We still have to check it but I think it's not going to take long."

Iraola: We are playing with collective spirit

Liverpool head coach Andoni Iraola speaking to Sky Sports:

"Very happy. We needed this win at home and to celebrate with the supporters. A really good performance.

"We started really aggressively and needed this start because we had been coming from behind lately. Especially against a team full of confidence like Brighton, we were very focused on starting well, scoring first and, luckily for us, we did it.

"This is the fourth win in a row, it feels good. We have to keep going, we still have points to recover but I'm liking a lot of things.

"Good performances from the players, they are helping each other, we are playing together with collectiveness. Some of the players will have better or worse performances, but today it was a team that you can trust."

On Wirtz's injury: "He had to leave the pitch with a small twist of the ankle. It doesn't look very big but we're playing every three days so we have to see what it is.

"I don't know if it is even an injury. He twisted his ankle and it's painful in the moment and he didn't feel 100 per cent. We decided to put on Trey and he played a good performance."

Hurzeler: Only one team was playing to win

Brighton head coach Fabian Hurzeler speaking to Sky Sports:

"It was a missed opportunity.

"Everyone felt we could definitely take something away from this game. We came here to play our way. We made two easy mistakes to give them a present to score two goals.

"We had plenty of chances to score. We kept trying. They defended well in the box and have individual quality. We did everything. We have to avoid easy mistakes. We had chances but didn't have luck on our side today.

"We had a big chance with Yasin. If that goes in, the game is completely different. We have to learn we don't have to chase the game.

"We lost our structure a little bit at 2-0 down. We wanted to come back as quickly as possible and lost our structure. That's what we have to analyse and do better.

"In the second half, and also a lot of phases in the first-half, only one team was playing and trying to win."

Liverpool's low possession - Opta stats

Liverpool's possession of 35.6 per cent was their second lowest on record (since 2003/04) in a Premier League home win, and their lowest in an Anfield league victory since November 2010.

Only Erling Haaland (nine) has scored more Premier League goals this season than Liverpool's Alexander Isak (six), who has scored in three consecutive appearances in the competition for the first time since January 2025.

Liverpool have now benefitted from 80 own goals in the Premier League, the joint-most alongside Manchester United.

Sports.title: Cunningham-South out of three-day England training squad due to injury
Sports.content:
England will be without Chandler Cunningham-South and Benhard Janse van Rensburg for their upcoming three-day training camp ahead of the Autumn Nations Series due to injury.

Head coach Steve Borthwick named his 36-player squad for a three-day training camp on Sunday. The team is due to gather at England's Performance Centre at Pennyhill Park later today.

Image: Steve Borthwick's side will start their Autumn Nations campaign against Australia on November 8

Uncapped forward Kepueli Tuipulotu and scrum-half Archie McParland have both been named in the squad.

Harlequins prop Fin Baxter also returns to the England squad following a 10-month injury lay-off.

Sale Sharks' Joe Marchant has also received a call-up for the first time since the 2023 World Cup after the winger returned to the Gallagher Prem following a two-year stint with Top 14 side Stade Francais at the start of the 2026-27 season.

Seb Atkinson, Immanuel Feyi-Waboso and Guy Pepper were all included in the squad and were listed as being in injury rehabilitation.

Sports.title: Drumbeat adds to O'Brien's two-year-old roll of honour
Sports.content:
Drumbeat added further depth to Aidan O'Brien's Classic battalion for next year in earning quotes of 14-1 for the Derby after landing the Criterium de Saint-Cloud at the Paris track.

The Wootton Bassett colt - wide-margin winner of the Zetland Stakes at Newmarket last time out - looked short of room at a crucial stage of the race under Ryan Moore, but burst through a gap to lead approaching a furlong and a half out.

From there he stayed on too strongly for stablemate Shakespeare and Christophe Soumillon, the pair two lengths back in second with Joseph O'Brien's Jesus Green a further length away in third.

The 9-10 favourite was delivering a seventh win in the race for O'Brien, but a first for Moore after wins for Soumillon aboard Pierre Bonnard 12 months ago and Los Angeles in 2023.

"He showed a lot of quality and is a very straightforward horse," Moore told Sky Sports Racing.

"He had the pace to go and take the gap and he quickened up well."
