Sports.title: Manchester United board hold crisis talks over Carrick’s future and Howe approach
Sports.content:
Manchester United’s hierarchy are in crisis talks over whether or not to sack Michael Carrick as manager after he oversaw another torrid defeat, to Bournemouth at Old Trafford on Sunday, that appeared to leave his job in the balance.

Carrick was defiant after the 3-0 humbling, insisting he was not expecting to be removed from his post, but the United executive were actively considering doing so, the Guardian understands. Eddie Howe remains the preferred candidate of Jason Wilcox, United’s director of football, should there be a change in the dugout, with the former Newcastle manager’s extensive Premier League experience placing him ahead of other potential targets. Howe would be less expensive to bring in than Unai Emery, another admired candidate, given Aston Villa would demand about £20m in compensation for the Spaniard.

Julian Nagelsmann, the former Germany and Bayern Munich head coach, is highly regarded by Christopher Vivell, United’s head of recruitment, but Wilcox’s view may hold more sway with Sir Jim Ratcliffe, who controls football policy at United. Antonio Conte is another who may be in the frame.

Carrick left Bruno Fernandes out of his starting lineup against Bournemouth, insisting before kick-off that he did so for football reasons and not because of the captain’s comments regarding his tactics following the midweek Champions League loss to Como. He subsequently saw his side suffer a sixth defeat in 12 games in all competitions as Rayan, Marcus Tavernier and Evanilson scored for Marco Rose’s side. United have won only once in the league this season and sit in 16th. Their last victory was on 10 September against Sabah in the Champions League.

“I totally understand the situation [regarding his job],” Carrick said. “I’m not expecting anything in particular, to be honest. [I’m] carrying on as normal, and I love this place. I’ll always do what I feel is going to be the best for the football club, whatever decision is made on anything really. So that’s kind of it. I’m not expecting anything either way.

“It’s a tough situation, there’s no hiding from it. What it looks like and what’s next I really don’t know. I will always do my best for the football club and I won’t change that now. I love what I do and I feel the responsibility – we’ll have to wait and see.”

Carrick made a point of applauding the home supporters at the end, pumping his hand to his chest as he walked past a supportive Stretford End. As soon as he disappeared down the tunnel, boos met Fernandes, who was following in the manager’s footsteps, alongside other United players.

“It wasn’t a farewell from me,” Carrick said. “I’m feeling it for my players, they’re going through a tough spell. Some of it we can help, some of it the situation unravels and the boys are feeling it at the moment. Mixed emotions for the supporters to respond in that way. To have that connection with the supporters it’s mixed emotions, it’ll take a bit of time to digest but I certainly appreciate their support. The situation is where we are and we haven’t had results or performances that have been good enough.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Speaking after the final whistle about his decision to leave out Fernandes, who was an unused substitute on Sunday, Carrick said: “There’s always times when you’re trying to make decisions that are to change the course of play and made a difference, but those are the decisions we made today.”

Harry Maguire, United’s captain in Fernandes’ absence, insisted the squad were “fully behind” Carrick. He said: “Coming into the team last season he turned things around and got Champions League football this season. As individuals, we’re not playing well enough. We have to look at ourselves and find something within ourselves to bring more to the team. That’s every player that I’m talking about. When things aren’t going your way you have to do the basics well.”

Sports.title: Roefs and Trafford stand firm as Sunderland and Leeds battle for point
Sports.content:
Régis Le Bris can usually do impassive to perfection but, by the final whistle, even Sunderland’s ultra balanced manager was looking more than a little fed up and frustrated.

His bottom-placed team had probably just about deserved a second Premier League win of the season but instead had to settle for a draw on an afternoon when the hugely disruptive Storm Boelo proved the enemy of good football.

While Daniel Farke will doubtless regard this as a decent point on the road for his steadily improving Leeds, much now hinges on Sunderland’s visit to Coventry on Saturday.

The wind was strong and capricious enough to bend the corner flags out of shape, send pieces of rubbish swirling around the pitch and passing calibration horribly awry, but it would take a hurricane to throw Brian Brobbey off balance.

The good news for Sunderland was that their formidable centre-forward had recovered from a hamstring injury and seemed to be relishing the physicality of his duel with Jaka Bijol.

Along the way Brobbey had a couple of first-half chances. These was the connection with the Enzo Le Fée cross and slightly deflected shot that prompted a decent save from James Trafford,

Then came the moment when Brobbey bullied Bijol into attempting a short back pass before charging after it and getting there before Trafford. Hats off to Farke’s England goalkeeper for keeping his cool, bravely standing his ground and eventually saving cleverly with a leg.

Leeds possess a not too shabby centre-forward of their own in Dominic Calvert-Lewin. He passed a late fitness test on a bruised foot and although initially less involved than Brobbey, seemed on a mission to engage Luke O’Nien in a personal subplot.

View image in fullscreen James Trafford denies Brian Brobbey from close range. Photograph: Owen Humphreys/PA

It soon became clear that Calvert-Lewin had little enthusiasm for being marked by O’Nien’s central defensive partner Nordi Mukiele and duly manoeuvred himself into cameos against the former at every opportunity.

Yet although O’Nien endured a couple of wobbles he also made a vital 11th hour quite possibly goal preventing tackle on Calvert-Lewin as half-time beckoned.

The second half had barely begun before fortune frowned on Sunderland. An attempted clearance concluded with O’Nien throwing out an elbow and accidentally catching Mukiele in the throat. The former Paris Saint-Germain defender required lengthy treatment as Le Bris looked on anxiously.

Eventually it became apparent a distressed Mukiele could not continue and the recently erratic Omar Alderete stepped off the bench.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

By now a second best Leeds were renascent and it took important interceptions from Alderete and Le Fee to break the dangerous stride of Jayden Bogle and Ao Tanaka respectively.

Undeterred, Sunderland rallied. Nilson Angulo was in encouraging form on the left-wing and two shots from the Ecuadorian forced Trafford into a couple of smart saves.

Shortly after the hour mark the by now fading Brobbey was replaced by the inexperienced Ukrainian striker Timur Tutyerov but, at the same time, Farke introduced fresh attacking legs of his own.

They belonged to Noah Okafor and Anton Stach who filled the spaces behind Calvert-Lewin from where Harry Wilson and Brenden Aaronson had struggled to destabilise Le Bris’s backline.

The game remained in the balance. Trafford did well to somehow scramble the ball to safety as Granit Xhaka’s corner very nearly curved beyond him but Robin Roefs was required to dive at Calvert-Lewin’s feet after spilling Tanaka’s shot. Calvert-Lewin wanted a penalty but Stuart Attwell, the referee, disagreed and a video assistant referee check endorsed that viewpoint.

When the former Newcastle midfielder Sean Longstaff, on as a Leeds substitute, unleashed a dangerous low 20 yard shot, Stadium of Light regulars feared the worst but Roefs made a superb one-handed save to turn it around a post.

Sports.title: Isak applies finishing touch as Liverpool bring Brighton’s winning run to an end
Sports.content:
Brighton’s impressive run was blown off course at Anfield where Liverpool performed with an appetite and urgency at both ends of the pitch that showed Andoni Iraola’s methods taking root. It was Liverpool, deserving winners on home soil for the first time in the Premier League this season, who looked upwardly mobile.

There was more evidence of the expensive trio of Florian Wirtz, Alexander Isak and Bradley Barcola feeling at home and adapting to Iraola’s demands. Wirtz was instrumental in an opening goal officially credited to Brighton’s Pascal Gross and Isak scored for the sixth time in six Premier League appearances to shatter the visitors’ sequence of four successive league wins. The sight of Barcola sprinting back to help his defence and Ronald Araújo smashing into challenges, as Liverpool stubbornly defended their lead and their box in the second half, satisfied Iraola just as much as his side’s incisiveness before the break.

Fabian Hürzeler praised the Brighton performance and the self-belief necessary to take the game to Liverpool when trailing to two quickfire goals. But he exaggerated the threat they displayed. Yasin Ayari missed a glorious chance to open the scoring and also struck a post, but Alisson was troubled more by his own distribution after Liverpool’s second goal than by anything the visitors engineered.

“I think everyone in the stadium saw there was one team who really tried to create and tried to win this game and therefore I have to praise my players,” claimed the Brighton head coach, prompting a mass raising of eyebrows in the post-match press conference. “The difference was that they scored and we didn’t. They blocked a lot of shots and defended the box well. We didn’t have that efficiency. We couldn’t keep the clean sheet because we made easy mistakes and lost some important personal duels but overall I saw a team with a lot of good things. It is very frustrating because we all have the feeling that there is a missed opportunity here today.”

Storm Boelo raged outside the stadium but inside it was relatively calm, vindicating the decision to proceed with the game. But not for Brighton. Liverpool’s attacking force devastated the visitors’ hopes of a fifth straight win and clean sheet in succession in the Premier League. The hosts were aggressive and sharp from the start, in contrast to their opening against Villarreal in the Champions League, and opened the scoring just as Brighton were beginning to exert their first serious spell of pressure.

There was an element of good fortune about the breakthrough but it also encapsulated the differing intensity between the teams when Wirtz held off Lewis Dunk and Araújo beat the Brighton captain and Olivier Boscagli to the loose ball. His low cross rebounded off two Brighton players before going to Wirtz, whose first-time shot deceived Bart Verbruggen via another deflection off Gross. Wirtz’s low-key celebration hinted at what was to come. It was not his first league goal of the campaign and second goal in successive games after all. The breakthrough was officially credited as an own goal from the Brighton midfielder.

View image in fullscreen Florian Wirtz’s shot was credited as an own goal by his fellow German, Pascal Gross. Photograph: Adam Vaughan/EPA

It should also have been a Liverpool equaliser rather than the opener. Diego Gómez and Gross combined to pierce Liverpool’s left flank and present Ayari with a free sight of goal with Alisson dragged across to his left. The Brighton forward blazed high into the Kop and would soon have added reason to rue the miscue.

Liverpool soon doubled their lead when capitalising on more casual Brighton defending. Boscagli was again found wanting when attempting to deal with Alisson’s clearance. The left-back struck a clearance straight at Barcola and was left floundering as the France international, deployed on the right, brushed aside his efforts to recover possession. Isak steered Barcola’s delivery inside the far corner with a deft, side-foot finish to score in three consecutive league games for the first time since January 2025. There was no surprise whatsoever when Boscagli was withdrawn at half-time.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Brighton attacked with greater conviction than they defended but with Araújo, Jérémy Jacquet and Virgil van Dijk making telling interventions, and receiving impressive support from all quarters, Alisson was not seriously extended. The visitors’ best hope of a recovery stemmed from the Liverpool keeper’s own risky pass to Alexis Mac Allister, which gifted possession back to Brighton and resulted in Ayari striking a post from 20 yards out.

Jack Hinshelwood, Boscagli’s replacement, and fellow substitute Malick Yalcouyé injected more energy and bite into Brighton’s second-half display but an end product from the visitors remained lacking. Too many overhit crosses and poor final balls enabled Liverpool to protect their lead in comfort.

Iraola said: “It is a very valuable win. The key was how we started. We needed a strong start, to be aggressive, recover balls, win our duels, be dangerous in transitions, and we’ve done it and it has been a different game from the last ones when we’ve conceded first.”

Sports.title: Osula and Barnes strike as Newcastle pile pressure on lacklustre Palace
Sports.content:
The first half was dreadful. The pass completion rate was a meagre 72.8%, although it felt lower. There were only two shots on target. The sun kept popping out from behind the clouds to take a look, and then going back in again, appalled. And the really bad news for Crystal Palace is that, for them, that was the good bit.

Newcastle were much improved after the break. Will Osula touched in a Jacob Murphy cross two minutes after half-time, Joe Willock had an effort ruled out for a marginal offside five minutes later, and Harvey Barnes completed a slick passing move six minutes after that. A smattering of boos from the home fans made clear what everybody already knew. Quarter of an hour of proper football had been enough to win the game, and that leaves Pierre Sage under significant pressure.

To an extent he is a victim of circumstance; a falling tide lowers all boats. The decline at Palace is evident everywhere from the shabby stadium to the summer sales, Maxence Lacroix and Daniel Muñoz joining the familiar exodus. Two wins in eight league games is troubling, particularly when one of them was as freakish as the previous home game against Nottingham Forest, when they were outplayed for much of the first half and inexplicably went in ahead at half-time. Nobody could have drawn much confidence from that, and the shellacking they sustained at Brighton last week is the kind of thing that might have got a manager more than a few weeks in the job the sack. Patience, though, can only be extended so long.

There were a couple of early chances. Daichi Kamada sliced his finish after a promising run by Dwight McNeil. Jean-Philippe Mateta, so devastating when Palace beat Newcastle in April, dragged a shot wide. McNeil rolled a low pass through a vacant six-yard box after good work from Yéremy Pino. But that golden age of incident soon passed.

By the quarter-hour an eerie silence had already fallen over Selhurst Park. It was not just that nothing was happening, it was that there was no expectation of anything happening. In part it was the blustery wind on a chilly autumnal afternoon, but there was also the sense that these are two fundamentally ordinary sides, low on confidence, coming to terms with new managers, neither of whom can have a huge amount of confidence that they will still be in their roles in a couple of months.

No weather conditions can explain why so many basic passes were misplaced, why the ball spent so much time bouncing aimlessly around the centre circle, or why shots kept being struck into players a couple of feet away.

View image in fullscreen Pierre Sage has struggled since taking over as Crystal Palace manager from Oliver Glasner. Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The Guardian

And that is the other worry for Palace. This was not a defeat against a high-flyer or a team in form. After a mildly promising start to the season, anxiety has begun to set in for Newcastle. They were booed off last week after losing at home against Aston Villa, their third defeat in four. Losing against an improving Villa in itself is no disgrace; the issue was more the manner of it. Had it worked, the deployment of Dan Burn as an emergency centre‑forward would have been hailed as inspired thinking outside the box; but it did not work – and, really, how likely was it to? – and so it looked like desperation.

The appeals for patience are reasonable enough: Matthias Jaissle has been in charge for only three months and replacing a manager who had been in charge for five years is rarely a straightforward process, even if the squad has not lost its three best players. But at the same time £260m was spent on eight signings, of whom only Nico González has made much of an impact so far, although Amar Dedic was solid enough here.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Burn, restored to the back four alongside Fabian Schär ahead of Sven Botman and Malick Thiaw, was immense, untroubled by the physicality of Mateta, of whom it may charitably be said that he is not back to his best after injury. The defence generally looked assured, while González was pretty much the only player in that chaotic first half who had any sense that some semblance of shape may be desirable. This is a squad still taking shape, with the new signings presumably to be introduced gradually but, ultimately, Newcastle should be comfortably mid-table.

It’s hard to have such confidence in Palace. Lukas Hornicek did have to make two saves around the midpoint of the second half, first from an Adam Wharton curler and then a long-range drive from Darío Osorio, but there was very little threat, very little imagination and very little quality from them.

Newcastle were far from brilliant, but that 15-minute spell after half‑time was more than enough for them to win the game comfortably. There is discontent at Palace, and it is justified.

Sports.title: Ouattara rescues point for Brentford as Hull maintain unbeaten home record
Sports.content:
Hull’s unbeaten home record remains intact but the Tigers have not tasted victory for seven games after this draw with Brentford.

The opening goal came courtesy of a 24th-minute Oli McBurnie penalty, awarded when Aaron Hickey flattened Tim Iroegbunam while trying to hook the ball away.

Although Brentford’s Caoimhín Kelleher guessed right, he could not stop McBurnie scoring his first Premier League goal for more than 900 days.

After the break, Hull were left to rue some inattentive defending as Igor Thiago found his way to Dango Ouattara, who slotted the ball home under very little pressure to make it 1-1 in the 63rd minute.

Jaidon Anthony pushed for a second Brentford goal and saw a shot land just wide before getting a second chance, which forced a save from Konstantinos Tzolakis, but there was a quick counter as Mohamed Belloumi raced in the other direction before firing over from distance.

An 88th-minute chance was Hull’s last to find the winning goal, but Mohamed-Ali Cho’s cross to Joe Gelhardt resulted in an off-target shot that ensured the Tigers took no more than a point.

Hull’s manager, Sergej Jakirovic, was pleased with the improved efforts of his side after last weekend’s defeat by Fulham. “I think we played a good game, especially in the first half,” he said. “We were much more aggressive in duels, we won a lot of first and second balls. Maybe there were some cheap mistakes, bad passing, bad receiving, but you see how fast they are – in five seconds they were in our box. We should have scored one or maybe two more with better decisions.”

Both clubs were required to pick through the detritus of the pre-match display in the opening minutes as balloons and litter were carried by the strong winds of Storm Boelo on to the pitch.

The first chance of note fell to the visitors, with Hull faltering in midfield after 11 minutes and allowing Hickey to unleash a shot that was comfortably dealt with by Tzolakis.

Ten minutes later, Belloumi found McBurnie inside the box, but as the Scot was preparing to strike, Mathias Jensen rushed in to foil the attempt.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

View image in fullscreen Oli McBurnie (left) hugs Mohamed Belloumi after putting Hull ahead from the penalty spot. Photograph: Mike Egerton/PA

After 22 minutes the visitors offered their hosts a golden chance when Hickey, having failed to collect a ball from Kelleher, lunged at the legs of Iroegbunam and floored him to give away a penalty. McBurnie stepped up and made no mistake.

Brentford had to wait until the 63rd minute to equalise, Ouattara made the most of lax Hull defending to collect an Igor Thiago ball and tap home.

Belloumi then reacted with a sprint towards the Brentford goal with substitute Cho in pursuit as back up, but the long-range shot was too high and flew into the stand.

The final roll of the dice was Cho’s cross in to Gelhardt, but he was wide of the mark and the whistle blew on a 1-1 draw that maintains unbeaten records home and away. Jakirovic added: “I can regret the chance we had through Mohamed-Ali Cho and Gelhardt, maybe it should have been 2-1, but in the end I think it’s a fair result.”

Brentford’s head coach, Keith Andrews, who had a spell at Hull as a player, was happy to see the response from the players who were brought off the bench during the second half in the lead up to their equaliser. He said: “It was a tough game and it was always going to be a tough game. I’ve got a lot of respect for Sergej and the journey he’s taken this team on – I think it’s been remarkable. We reacted well at half-time, the impact from the bench was pretty good but it was a tough game.”

Sports.title: Scottish Premiership: Durán caps Celtic’s comeback win over Hibernian
Sports.content:
Camilo Durán moved into double figures for the season as Celtic reasserted themselves at the top of the Premiership by coming from behind to defeat beleaguered Hibernian 2-1 at windy Easter Road.

After another Europa League setback at home to Celta Vigo on Thursday, the champions bounced back with a victory that restored their four-point cushion over Rangers at the top. The home side, who are bottom, took an early lead through Owen Elding but it was swiftly cancelled out by a Jason Kerr own goal before Duran’s 10th of the season edged the visitors ahead just before the break.

It proved enough to secure a ninth win in 10 league games and ensure the recently appointed home boss, Marink Reedijk, suffered a third straight defeat since succeeding David Gray.

There were a couple of blemishes for Celtic, however, as substitute Alistair Johnston’s return from injury lasted barely 20 minutes before he had to go off, while £11million forward Kasper Hogh – restored to the starting line-up after notching in just one of his 13 previous matches for the Hoops – again drew a blank before being replaced in the 64th minute.

Derek McInnes asked his Rangers side to be “brilliant” against St Johnstone and was rewarded with a 4-0 win at Ibrox on Saturday. After dropping two points at Dundee, the Light Blues dominated the first half but only led at the interval through a goal in the 29th minute from the Venezuela forward Kevin Kelsy.

Saints started the second half brightly but goals from the Gers striker Ryan Naderi in the 61st minute and Kelsy again five minutes later had the home side cruising. The Saints substitute Kai Fotheringham was shown a straight red card by Chris Graham in the 74th minute for his high challenge on the midfielder Nico Raskin, before the substitute Tochi Chukwuani added a fourth for the hosts with three minutes remaining.

View image in fullscreen Rangers’ Kevin Kelsy scores the third goal against St Johnstone. Photograph: Steve Welsh/PA

McInnes said: “It’s quite ironic in the sense that we were so good and so brilliant at times in the first half and create so many opportunities, that we were only a goal to the good at half-time. And obviously, we don’t want to let the frustration of those missed opportunities and dominance filter into the second half.

“I think half-time came at a bad time for us because, despite the conditions, some of the play was really good. I asked the players to be brilliant today, not just win the game, can we really commit to being the best we can be, as good as we can be? And I thought we were in the first half. Everything was brilliant except the result at half-time because we should have been more in in front.”

Cláudio Braga and Calvin Miller scored to help Hearts secure a 2-0 win over Motherwell at Fir Park on Sunday. A return to winning ways after last weekend’s humbling 7-1 defeat by Celtic leaves Hearts four points behind second-placed Rangers and eight off the leaders. Motherwell sit 10th after this sixth straight defeat, equalling a record from 2003. They were booed off the pitch at the interval and at full time.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Dundee United won a rollercoaster game 3-2 against Aberdeen at Tannadice on Saturday. Zidane Iqbal scored for the hosts before the visitors equalised through Nesta Guinness-Walker – both players scoring their first goals for their clubs.

United took the lead once more thanks to a Dylan Tait strike, with Connor Ronan drawing Aberdeen level after the break. Zac Sapsford secured all three points for his side, with the win moving United up to fourth – one point behind Hearts, who are at Motherwell on Sunday – while Aberdeen dropped to ninth.

Two own goals helped Falkirk climb to seventh with a 3-0 victory over Kilmarnock. Centre-backs Cathal McCarthy and George Stanger scored past their own goalkeeper either side of a Jacob Murrell header. St Mirren ended their losing streak with a 2-1 victory over Dundee with goals from Calvin Ramsay and Eseosa Sule before Bradley Fink pulled one back for the visitors.

Sports.title: Ian Holloway’s circus: why the manager’s antics are no laughing matter for fans
Sports.content:
In Ian Holloway’s often madcap managerial orbit, this was simply the latest in a steady succession of eccentric outbursts. Eyes bulging as he spoke, he boomed the letter “D” and promptly stabbed himself in the chest with an imaginary dagger. Next came the letter “M” alongside a blow from another invisible knife. Finally, a “W” followed by a jab to the heart. “Dead. Man. Walking,” he declared, pausing for effect between words and briefly falling into an Oscar-worthy zombie stupor. “That’s how it feels.”

To an offbeat press conference genre containing seagulls following trawlers and self-proclaimed special ones, it was a crazy new entry worthy of its subsequent viral nature. Holloway at his finest.

The clip was widely shared, there is every chance you saw it this month. The general perception, from those of a neutral stance, was that one of football’s great characters had lost the plot. To those in the room, there was a sense that it was merely the exuberant mannerisms of a quirky manager during a tricky period. But for a large section of Swindon fans, it prompted an unamused eye roll. Here we go again. The circus tent is pitched firmly in town.

Supporting a Holloway-led club is an interesting assignment. Within weeks of taking the Swindon job two years ago on Sunday, he began constructing a hostile wall towards fans by reminding them that they could “go bowling” if they did not like his methods. Last December, he had to be restrained by his players during an altercation with a fan, while he has made a habit of telling them to “jog on” if overly vocal in their criticism.

When his side picked up a much-needed point against Walsall last week, the goalkeeping coach held him back from another confrontation with supporters. Asked about it, he goaded reporters into putting his address online so that disgruntled fans could have it out with him: “I don’t really care anymore.” So, when season‑ticket holders found their phones pinging with amused messages containing the same viral Holloway zombie clip, their lack of laughter could be forgiven.

“When you get these soundbites from Ian Holloway, outside the Swindon Town world it’s all about what a great character he is, how he says it like it is, and how it must be great to have him as manager,” says Rich Pullen, founder and co-host of the largest Swindon podcast, Loathed Strangers. “But, to a growing percentage of the Swindon community, it’s exhausting and it takes away from any of the good.

“If Swindon win, post-match he often uses it as an opportunity to have a go at the fans. It’s got to the stage where you can’t even enjoy a win without Ian Holloway being unable to hold himself from criticising fans. The easy thing to do is ignore him, but it’s almost impossible because he is everywhere. He goes viral and everyone always thinks: ‘Oh, isn’t that funny.’ Well, no. People are tired of the excess noise.”

View image in fullscreen Disheartened Swindon fans stand solemnly in the pouring rain at the Memorial Stadium. Photograph: Jeremy Landey/Focus Images Ltd/Shutterstock

This time last week, there was a thought that the M4 derby homecoming trip to Bristol Rovers on Saturday might hasten a possible end to Holloway’s Swindon tenure. Winless in eight games in all competitions, the discontent was not expected to abate on the preceding midweek trip to high-flying Barnet. The 3-1 victory that followed – Barnet’s first league defeat of the season – was a huge shock, thanks in no small part to the heroics of the goalkeeper, Connor Ripley, who recently declared the whole squad would “run through a brick wall” for Holloway.

Swindon might have followed it with another win, at Rovers’ Memorial Stadium, only for Matty Virtue to miss an open goal 90 seconds into the match. The forgettable goalless draw that played out at least extended Swindon’s unbeaten run to three games and kept them safely mid-table in League Two. Holloway was right to savour the improved performances, but the malaise runs deeper.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

The manager had said something far more significant immediately after his viral soundbite when he continued: “The owner’s a dead man walking as well and that over‑complicates everything here.”

Even those seeking a more composed figure in Holloway’s place agree the manager is just one cog in a machine many argue has been misfiring for some time. Days after the zombie rant, the Swindon Town Supporters Trust declared the club had “lost our soul, our hope, our passion”, and urged Holloway’s comments about the Australian owner, Clem Morfuni, to “be a wake-up call”.

Since saving the club from probable administration in 2021, Morfuni has become a target of increasing fan indignation, failing to sell up and adding millions to the club’s debt. “Whilst the short-term focus may be on Ian Holloway, the bigger picture is above the role of the manager,” concluded the Trust, pointing to “a wedge with supporters so obvious that even the manager openly talks about it”.

In such a context, the uptick in form is merely one – albeit very welcome – aspect among wider misgivings. Because what fans really want is a united club and manager they can get behind; not to go jogging on.

Sports.title: Crystal Palace consider moves for three ex-Premier League managers as pressure grows on Pierre Sage
Sports.content:
Crystal Palace consider moves for three ex-Premier League managers as pressure grows on Pierre Sage

Crystal Palace are looking at potential options to replace Pierre Sage as the team's manager, talkSPORT understands.

The Eagles are sitting in 17th place after a 2-0 defeat at home to Newcastle United, where they were booed off.

4 Sage's start to life in England has been underwhelming Credit: Getty

Palace have won twice so far in the top-flight but have lost five of their first eight.

As a result, contingency plans are being made with Sean Dyche, Thomas Frank and Vitor Pereira all appreciated.

Another candidate is former Premier League striker Robbie Keane should Eagles chairman Steve Parish decide to move on from Sage.

The Frenchman arrived at Selhurst Park after a sublime season with Lens, where they finished second in Ligue 1, just six points behind champions Paris Saint-Germain.

However, the players appear to be struggling to adapt to what he wants from them, and when coupled with European football, it is a bad combination.

Palace have conceded the most goals in the league, 19 so far, and that has been their biggest issue with the nine goals they have scored not even close to being the worst in the division.

But after Newcastle walked away with three points, Sage insists he still has backing from the Palace top brass.

He said: "Yes. I think they do [believe in me].

"It's normal [to be under pressure] because we don't have the results. The noise is a consequence of the team and we don't have [the points] we expect.

"Inside, we just are really focused on the solutions, how to be better and how to create the conditions to compete. I don't have to convince people around the club, I just have to convince the players to do their best and continue their improvement.

4 Dyche hasn't managed since being sacked by Nottingham Forest in January Credit: Getty

4 Frank's standing in the game remains high despite his stint at Tottenham Hotspur not working out Credit: Getty

"After that, this kind of decision of what we are speaking about is to the chairman and owners. For me, the noise around the team and club is only noise.

"I spoke with the chairman this week, but I didn't speak about this subject.

"We spoke about the game, the condition of the team and how we build our game plan to compete today. We didn't speak about this subject. I share my strategy with him and the technical staff. It's normal."

The options

Frank made it clear that he was in no rush to take a new job.

In fact in the summer, he insisted that he wouldn't be rushing into a new job.

He said in a statement: "There have been conversations and opportunities since leaving Spurs, but I have decided not to rush into the next role. For me, this summer is not the right time to go back into management.

"When the time is right, I will look forward to my return as a manager, ready to embrace the job with great energy and dedication."

The same is true of Dyche, who revealed exclusively to talkSPORT that he's waiting for the right opportunity.

He said: "We'll see. First thing's first, it's not easy to get any jobs in football. So you've got to first of all, get a job.

"But it's also got to be one that you want. The last few have been tough going. It's been heavy lifting when you're at clubs that need almost bailing out, and sort of stripping back and getting going again.

"It's enjoyable. Very enjoyable in one way, but it is heavy lifting. So we'll see. But at the moment, I'm quite enjoying doing all kinds of different things.

"That includes talkSPORT. There's so much out there now involving football, not just Premier League football."

4 Palace are embroiled in an early season relegation battle Credit: Getty

Story of the game

Palace started the match against Newcastle with the same XI that played in Thursday against Besiktas.

But it was they who made the brighter start with a succession of shots fired in at Lukas Hornicek's goal.

Daichi Kamada and Jean-Philippe Mateta pulled efforts wide of the near post, but the teams went in level at half time.

However, Newcastle immediately scored at the start of the second half.

Amar Dedic played a pass into Jacob Murphy on the right, and he swung a delightful cross into the box.

It was begging to be put away, and William Osula obliged touching home.

The Magpies thought they'd doubled their lead soon after as Joelinton played Joe Willock in.

He controlled and finished into the far corner only for VAR to confirm he was offside.

But the Toon made it 2-0 shortly after as Nico Gonzalez shoved off Adam Wharton and found Murphy, Amar Dedic made an overlapping run and pulled the ball back for Harvey Barnes to lash into the net.

From there, Palace had a few effort from range that Hornicek dealt with while Joelinton came close to a third for Newcastle before the home side were booed off.

Sports.title: Furious Man United fan says he wants them to be RELEGATED in shock claim after latest humiliation
Sports.content:
Furious Man United fan says he wants them to be RELEGATED in shock claim after latest humiliation

Manchester United can only return to their former glories if they are relegated from the Premier League.

That is according to one disgruntled supporter following Sunday's chastening defeat at home to Bournemouth.

3 United are just a point above the relegation zone after losing to Bournemouth Credit: Getty

The Red Devils were beaten 3-0 at Old Trafford as their winless run in all competitions extended to eight matches.

Michael Carrick's side now sit just a point above the relegation zone in 16th place.

A toxic atmosphere inside the stadium saw the players booed off at full-time as they were beaten by the Cherries.

Meanwhile, opposition to the Glazer family and INEOS' ownership has now seen one United fan make a surprising admission over their top-flight status.

United fan wants club relegated

Following their latest defeat, Red Devils supporter Chris spoke to talkSPORT's Sam Matterface on GameDay Live.

Expressing his frustration with the running of the club, Chris revealed: "I won’t be bothered if we get relegated.

"Literally, the only way the Glazers are going to go is if we stop making money.

"All these money men who are only involved in Man United because of the money, if you get rid of all of that, strip it back down to what actual proper United fans want, where we’re proud of the Busby Babes, Class of ‘92, Mancunians or young lads coming and playing for our team.

"All we get is has-beens coming to our team getting paid too much money. They’re not bothered. It’s like a place you come for two or three years, get paid and then just go wherever you want to go.

"The only way you get rid of all that is, and I won’t be bothered, if we went down. Scrap the new stadium, we’ll stay here.

3 United fan Chris fears relegation is needed to solve the club's issues Credit: Getty

"The plastic fans who don’t want to be United fans, let them go and then we’ll start again, like (Matt) Busby did. That’s my view anyway."

As for whether there is anything the fans can do to get their message across to the owners, he added: "I don’t know what the answer is because the problem is as well, do you know any other brand in the world where if all of us stop going now, all season ticket holders stop going, there would be other people who just go and queue up and go.

"It’s madness. It’s like we’re all intoxicated and we’re just going for it because we love the club and we want it back to what we wanted.

"There’s no perfect remedy, but I get what you’re saying. Something needs to happen. That’s why I’m saying something extreme where I won’t be bothered if we get relegated.

"I genuinely won’t be bothered because I’m sick of this. All the things I love about Man United or did, we’re starting to become a club I can’t stand.

"The morals of it, sacking decent people who have been at the club for years, all these little things now.

3 Carrick's side have failed to win any of their last eight matches in all competitions Credit: Getty

"They make me cringe and that’s the club I go (to watch). My kids are now supporters."

When were Man United last relegated?

United have not tasted relegation for 52 years having last dropped out of the top-flight in 1974.

On that occasion, the club secured an immediate return to the First Division and have remained at the same level since.

They came closest to dropping out of the Premier League as recently as two seasons ago, though.

The Red Devils finished 15th on 42 points in the 2024/25 campaign, their lowest top-flight points tally since the previous relegation.

Meanwhile, 102 of the 140 seasons in the club's history have been spent at the highest level of English football.

Sports.title: Michael Carrick accused of trying to embarrass Bruno Fernandes as Man United boss insists horror defeat is not a farewell
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick accused of trying to embarrass Bruno Fernandes as Man United boss insists horror defeat is not a farewell

Jamie Carragher believes Michael Carrick deliberately kept Bruno Fernandes benched for Manchester United in the 3-0 defeat to Bournemouth.

Club captain Fernandes did not appear in the starting XI for United at Old Trafford on Sunday following his shock rant about their tactics in the 4-1 defeat to Como earlier in the week.

3 Carrick flexed his authority as United head coach by leaving his captain Fernandes out of the United team Credit: AFP

The 32-year-old sat on the bench for the entirety of the match, even when they found themselves two goals down by half time.

Carrick was bold to leave Fernandes out of the team, and Carragher reckons he never intended to give the Portuguese an appearance despite attacking quality being scarce on Sunday.

"I don't think he was ever going to bring him on," he told Sky Sports. "I think it was a deliberate decision to leave him on the bench, and almost try and embarrass him a little bit in front of the supporters, I don't know.

"He brought him off midweek, and I think what Bruno did after the game in Como was off the back of him getting brought off.

"I think Michael Carrick never had any intention of bringing him on at all, that sub was never going to happen."

Before the match, the Liverpool legend said: "There's probably two reasons why he's done it. Number one, he's sending a message to the rest of the dressing room, 'You don't take on me as the manager'.

"Or, he thinks, 'I haven't got long left, so I'm going to give him one back for what he did to me midweek', basically, show he's got a bit of strength, a bit of power.

"I think most people in the country will be quite pleased with Michael Carrick for putting him on the bench."

Carrick confirmed after the game that Fernandes was 'fit and available'.

Carrick shuts down United farewell talk

The biggest talking point from the defeat is not United's display, with talkSPORT's Alex Crook giving every player a 0/10, but the future of head coach Carrick.

3 Fernandes warmed up for United but didn't come on, and Carragher feels Carrick wanted to embarrass him Credit: Getty

United fans showed their support for the ex-midfielder at full-time as he walked down the tunnel, and then booed the players as they went on the same route.

There is a sense that they feel as though Carrick has been dealt a bad hand at the club, with many chants being aimed at technical director Jason Wilcox and the owners, including Sir Jim Ratcliffe.

However, he has dismissed any speculation that he has waved bye to the fans for the final time in his role.

"What is your feeling about your situation at this moment? It felt like a farewell from you, not a farewell from the club," Carrick was asked by Sky Sports on his post-match applause.

"It wasn't from me," he insisted in his response. "I had really mixed emotions, I'm feeling it for the players, for my group of players, I'm really feeling it for them because they're going through a tough spell.

"Some of it we can help ourselves, some of it the situation unravels. The boys are feeling at the moment.

3 Carrick was serenaded by United fans despite the defeat and does not think that he has bid farewell to them Credit: Getty

"Mixed emotions for the supporters to respond in that way, and to have that connection with the supporters in the moment that we're in, is really mixed emotions.

"A little bit of time to digest that, really, but I certainly appreciate their support.

"But the situation is where we're at, we haven't had results and we haven't had performances that have been good enough."

However, didn't rule out him being out the door at Old Trafford, as he said later on Sunday: "I take the responsibility, of course.

"I accept the responsibility. I respect the position I am in. The responsibility is mine. What else can I say right now?

"I totally understand the situation. I am not expecting anything in particular, to be honest.

"I am carrying on as normal. I love this place. I always do what I feel is best for this football club. Whatever decision is made on anything really, that's kind of it. I am not expecting anything."

Eddie Howe is understood to be the preferred option for Wilcox if United dismiss Carrick, and Julian Nagelsmann has been sounded out.

Antonio Conte would be open to taking the job, although he stressed he is not in any advanced negotiations with clubs.

Sports.title: Every diabolical Man United player was a 0/10 and they revel in finding new ways to disgrace the badge
Sports.content:
Every diabolical Man United player was a 0/10 and they revel in finding new ways to disgrace the badge

A banner with Bryan Robson, Roy Keane and Eric Cantona on it unfurled after Bournemouth scored their abomination of a second goal said it all.

‘Standards’ it screamed in big red letters on a black background. The problem for Michael Carrick is that standards at Old Trafford have slipped so dramatically that nobody is remotely surprised to see Bournemouth come away with the points in a 3-0 victory.



5 Another week, another defeat for United as they extended their winless run to eight in all competitions Credit: AFP

In fact, the Cherries have now avoided defeat in their last seven meetings with United.

Like many of the so-called 'lesser teams' in the Premier League, the ground that Sir Alex Ferguson made a fortress has become the Cherries' playground.

Carrick looks certain now to pay the price for United's terrible run of form with his job and must be at a loss to explain how his team have regressed so quickly from the performances in the second half of last season that got him the gig in the first place.



Carrick made the bold call to drop captain Bruno Fernandes to the bench as punishment for his astonishing attack on his head coach in the wake of the mid-week drubbing at Como.

5 The United fans made a point of booing the players after Carrick went down the tunnel ahead of them Credit: AFP



Fernandes was joined among the subs by fellow bad boy Lisandro Martinez and Matheus Cunha, whose body language in recent weeks has done Carrick no favours.

But if Carrick was hoping his emotional pre-match press conference address would have a stirring impact on his players, he was sadly mistaken.



In the five-minute monologue, Carrick spoke about values and humility and claimed there was a ‘a resilience in this football club.’

Sadly, for the 2008 Champions League winner, his monstrosity of a team showed none of those qualities and produced a performance that would get most managers fired.

The simple fact is that these United players do not appear to hurt anywhere near as much as Carrick when they lose games or concede cheap goals.

If I didn’t know better, I would say they revel in finding new ways to humiliate themselves and to disgrace the badge that was once the pride of English football.



5 Carrick looks to be on his way out as United head coach, and none of his players did anything to help him Credit: Getty

How else do you explain the diabolical defending that allowed Rayan to ghost in at the far post and guide Justin Kluivert's free-kick into the bottom corner?

The immediate reaction laid bare the problem whoever replaces Carrick will have to solve.

There were no angry recriminations, no words exchanged, just a simple collective shrug of the shoulders. Even stand-in captain Harry Maguire had a look of resignation in his eyes.



If that wasn’t bad enough, there are almost no words to describe the lapse in concentration that saw Leny Yoro caught in possession and sent tumbling by Adrian Truffert in the lead up to Marcus Tavernier's tap-in second goal.

Yoro was regarded as one of the best up-and-coming players in Europe when United prised him away from French club Lille a couple of summers ago.

However, the 20-year-old has been dragged down to the same pitiful levels of most of his teammates.

5 Club captain Fernandes didn't even make it off the bench as United hit a new low just two months into the season Credit: AFP



Yoro is still on the radar of French giants Paris Saint-Germain and would be advised to ask his agent to get him as far away from United as quickly as possible.

Carrick is understood to have been enthused by the midfield rebuild United underwent in the summer, and particularly the arrival of £70million Carlos Baleba.

Baleba still looks some way short of full match sharpness but is far from the biggest problem when it comes to the middle of the park.

Carrick's faith in Baleba’s fellow summer signing Youri Tielemans has been misguided, and the Belgian was hooked at half-time after another shockingly abject performance.



How Chelsea persuaded United technical director Jason Wilcox to part with £50m for Andrey Santos is one of life’s mysteries. If United were operating as a serious football club they would not have gone near a cast-off from Stamford Bridge.

Carrick has undoubtedly been set up to fail by Wilcox and co. Not having a fit striker nor left-back for a game he simply to had to win is evidence of that.

5

Evanilson’s third goal after more criminal defending from a combination of Martinez and Harry Maguire was the final nail in Carrick’s coffin.



Whoever replaces him will be inheriting the most poisoned chalice in the Premier League. United are a club with no standards.

Sports.title: Manchester United relax controversial Old Trafford rule for one game only
Sports.content:
Manchester United relax controversial Old Trafford rule for one game only

Manchester United relaxed their rules on season ticket holders attending fixtures for the visit of Bournemouth on Sunday.

A change was confirmed prior to the match due to weather conditions in the North West amid Storm Boelo.



3 United relaxed rules on season ticket holders for the visit of Bournemouth Credit: Getty

The fixture took place during an amber weather warning for strong winds, with disruption to public transport and road closures expected.

As a result, longer journey times were anticipated in the area, causing some fans not to attend the match.

Red Devils relax rules

United subsequently will not count those absences against minimum usage figures for season ticket holders.



Failing to attend the match against the Cherries will also not affect fans' season ticket renewals.

The move was confirmed on social media by an independent supporter liaison officer.



Fans were also given the opportunity to transfer their ticket to the match to another official United member.

In a post on X, the independent supporter liaison officer said: "Following contact from supporters affected by travel disruption, we raised this with the club this morning and have received reassurance that missing today’s game because of weather-related cancellations will not count against minimum usage or affect season ticket renewal."



The forecasted windy conditions would remain beyond the start of the match at 2pm on Sunday afternoon.

First half goals from Rayan and Marcus Tavernier put the visitors in front as United fell 2-0 behind before the interval.

Evanilson later added a third for Bournemouth inside the final 20 minutes.

3 An amber weather warning caused disruption for those attending Old Trafford on Sunday Credit: Getty



The result sees United slip to 16th in the Premier League, just a point above the relegation zone.

Michael Carrick's side have now failed to win any of their last eight matches in all competitions.

United season ticket holders

United's move to relax rules on season ticket holders follows their controversial treatment of fans earlier this year.

The club were publicly criticised by multiple supporter groups in the summer.



It came after fans had their season ticket accounts restricted by the Red Devils.

Accounts were targeted where usernames and logins had been shared with more than six people.

3 Season ticket holders who missed the loss to Bournemouth will not have their accounts affected Credit: Getty

Meanwhile, United announced last month they had banned 685 season ticket holders.



The process was part of a club investigation into ticket touting.

Sports.title: Florian Wirtz has first Premier League goal of season taken off him as update on injury given
Sports.content:
Florian Wirtz has first Premier League goal of season taken off him as update on injury given

Florian Wirtz thought he opened his Premier League account for the season, but his wait goes on.

Liverpool beat Brighton 2-0 on Sunday, breaking the deadlock on 17 minutes as Wirtz hit a first-time effort inside the area.

2 Wirtz appeared to have smashed in the opener for Liverpool, but his shot went off Gross for an own goal Credit: Getty

The Germany international, signed for a then club-record £116.5million transfer fee in 2025, has had a difficult second season with the Reds and already been linked with a move away from Anfield.

However, he remains without a goal in the English top flight for the 2026/27 campaign.

Minutes after the opener, the Premier League revealed that the goal has been accredited to someone else.

"The goal accreditation panel has adjudged Liverpool's 17th minute goal as a Gross own goal."

Liverpool netted a second moments later as Alexander Isak found the target from a Bradley Barcola cross to seal the three points.

Wirtz appeared to pick up an injury shortly before the hour mark, but he was able to return to play.

However, he was substituted swiftly after and went straight down the tunnel.

Iraola gives update on Wirtz injury

Fortunately for Wirtz and Liverpool, it appears the knock is not as bad as first feared.

Reds boss Andoni Iraola couldn't say if Wirtz would be available for Liverpool's next outing against Chelsea in the Carabao Cup on Wednesday night.

2 Wirtz picked up an injury as he tried to make a tackle, and was eventually brought off for Liverpool Credit: AFP

"Unfortunately, he had to leave the pitch with a small twist of the ankle," Iraola said.

"It doesn't look very big but we are playing every three days so we need to see where he is."

Brighton had conceded just five goals and kept four clean sheets in the league before Sunday.

However, their defence was breached on two occasions in a matter of minutes and they no longer have the joint-best defence with Arsenal.

Sports.title: Man United ‘humiliate themselves’ as Michael Carrick told he’ll be sacked at full-time
Sports.content:
Man United ‘humiliate themselves’ as Michael Carrick told he’ll be sacked at full-time

Michael Carrick and his Manchester United team were booed off at half-time at Old Trafford.

The Red Devils were 2-0 down to Bournemouth in another embarrassing performance that they went on to lose 3-0.

2 Tavernier scored Bournemouth's second against Man United Credit: AFP

A comeback would have been a tall order seeing as the Cherries had never lost a Premier League game while two goals up at the break.

The under-pressure Carrick, who dropped captain Bruno Fernandes for the match, was told he was likely to be out of work come Monday morning.

talkSPORT's Micky Gray said: "Michael Carrick has 45 minutes to save his job."

But chief football correspondent Alex Crook surmised: “They find new ways to dishonour the badge, honestly from one to 11. They're not fit for purpose and Michael Carrick's got no chance. Micky says he's got 45 minutes to save his job. I think he's done."

Later in the second half, he said: "This could be a relegation battle for Man United. They are not just losing games, they are getting battered."

At the end of the game, Carrick completed a lap of Old Trafford before disappearing down the tunnel.

Once he had gone, the boos from the home fans towards the players were very loud.

Bournemouth at the triple

Ayden Heaven gave the ball away with a sloppy pass and then jumped in two-footed with a rash challenge to try and win it back.

He was saved by Evanilson pulling out of the duel, which means Heaven is only given a yellow, but his reprieve was short-lived.

The resulting free-kick was floated to the back post, and Rayan clinically finished past Senne Lammens inside his near post.

The worst was yet to come as Leny Yoro slipped while trying to play the ball on the edge of his own box.

Adrien Truffert ruthlessly punished him by taking over and squaring it for Tavernier to roll into an empty net.

In the second half, Evanilson made it 3-0 as he raced on to a long ball forward.

Senne Lammens came off his line, but he was too slow as the striker touched it past him and scored from a tight angle.

Fernandes dropped

Carrick made the bold call ahead of the match to drop Fernandes following his comments about Man United's tactics in midweek.

The Red Devils were crushed by Como 4-1 in the Champions League, and after the game, the captain questioned the idea not to press the Italian side.

Fernandes then trained as normal on Friday and Saturday before being left on the bench.

Speaking ahead of the match, Carrick revealed that he'd dropped the skipper for footballing reasons.

In his pre-match Sky Sports interview, he said: “Pure football.

"When you have options it's always a difficult decision.

“We have to make the right one for today and the team to get that performance we want."

2 Fernandes was left on the bench for the first time since 2021 against Villarreal Credit: Getty

Carrick even refused to rule out taking the captaincy off the Portuguese international.

He said: "The most important thing for me is the team, first and foremost, the squad and the dynamics in the squad.

"Again, it's about the football club, I'll always do what's best for the football club."

And he remained on the bench throughout.

Dreadful form

With Bournemouth's win, Man United are sitting in 16th place in the Premier League.

They are just one point above the drop zone and have won one game all season.

That was a 5-2 victory over Ipswich Town, and they haven't won since.

In all competitions, they only have one other victory that came against Sabah in the Champions League.

Sports.title: New footage shows Chelsea fans rowing with Levi Colwill moments after Tottenham loss
Sports.content:
New footage shows Chelsea fans rowing with Levi Colwill moments after Tottenham loss

Chelsea fans were spotted venting their frustrations with Levi Colwill following the shock 2-0 defeat to Tottenham.

Cole Palmer was sent off as the Blues suffered a third Premier League loss of the season at home against their bitter rivals.

2 Chelsea fans fumed as they watch their team lose at home to Spurs for the first time in eight years Credit: Getty

Spurs, who picked up their first win days before, were the better side throughout and scored via a Mike Penders own goal and Mathys Tel.

Chelsea had not lost to the north Londoners at their Stamford Bridge home in the Premier League since 2018.

Fans have become accustomed to beating Spurs, so Saturday's result came as a real shock.

A couple of supporters in particular were livid with the performance and made it clear to Colwill at full-time in a video on social media.

Chelsea fans clash with Colwill

As the centre-back applauded towards the West Lower, one fan was heard shouting: "Colwill, don't you f****** clap!"

"F*** off!" a furious second added, before crying out: "Shame on you!"

Colwill was led away by Danny Welbeck, before completing his round of applause to the Matthew Harding and East stands.

Chelsea were dealt a blow ahead of kick-off as Joao Pedro missed out on the squad.

The striker picked up an injury during training on Friday, according to manager Xabi Alonso.

Geovany Quenda was chosen over Danny Welbeck to join Palmer and Morgan Rogers in attack.

WARNING: STRONG LANGUAGE

2 Colwill was on the receiving end of fury from Chelsea fans in the West Lower as he applauded them Credit: Getty

Penders started in goal for the hosts as Emi Martinez remains out of action following jaw surgery.

The Argentina international was knocked out cold during the 2-0 win at Everton last weekend.

Chelsea are fourth in the Premier League, but could drop out of the top four by the end of Sunday.

They will travel to Liverpool on Wednesday night for a Carabao Cup last 16 clash, live on talkSPORT.

However, Chelsea then host Manchester United in the league just two-and-half days later, a match that will also be live on talkSPORT.

A trip to Sunderland on November 8 caps off their schedule before the international break.
