Sports.title: Michael Carrick insists he was NOT waving an emotional farewell to fans after Man United's humiliating 3-0 thrashing by Bournemouth - but admits he is unsure about his future
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick's future as Manchester United head coach is hanging by a thread after defeat to Bournemouth at Old Trafford pushed him closer to the brink.

It was the sixth time Carrick’s team have lost in 12 games this season as United sank to 16th place in the Premier League table, piling more pressure on the club to appoint a third manager this year.

Asked if he expects to be sacked, Carrick said: ‘I totally understand the situation. I'm not expecting anything either way.

‘I’m carrying on as normal. I love this place. I'll always do what I feel is going to be the best for the football club and I won’t change that now, whatever decision is made.

‘It's a tough situation, there's no hiding from it. What it looks like and what's next I really don't know. I love what I do and I feel the responsibility. We'll have to wait and see.

‘Of course, I take responsibility. I respect the position that I'm in, and the responsibility is mine. What else can I say really right now?

‘I've tried to do everything I can to not be in this position, of course I have. For a number of reasons, we've not been able to stop that happening to the position we're in right now.

Michael Carrick insists he was not saying farewell to Manchester United fans as he did a lap of Old Trafford after their 3-0 defeat by Bournemouth

‘I've been at the club a long time. It hurts an awful to see us going through this at this moment in time. The situation is where we are and we haven't had results or performances that have been good enough.’

Some bookmakers last night suspended betting on Carrick being sacked with Eddie Howe and Julian Nagelsmann - both currently out of work – among the frontrunners to replace him.

Carrick said he had not spoken to chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox over his future. ‘No, just briefly they came down like they always do after a game, but nothing out of the ordinary,’ he added.

The United fans showed their support for Carrick, while turning on the club’s ownership, Wilcox and the players as United sank to a 3-0 defeat.

The 45-year-old looked visibly emotional as he walked around the pitch at the end thanking the fans and placing a hand over his heart.

‘It wasn't a farewell from me,’ Carrick insisted. ‘I probably didn't really expect that off the supporters, if I'm honest, but I've always felt the support and that connection with them.

‘It will take a bit of time to digest, but I certainly appreciate their support. It's difficult for me to have a day like this at this club and feel the emotion.

‘I'm feeling it for my players, they're going through a tough spell. There's a lot of emotion in the changing room right now, there's a lot of the boys quite hurt, to be fair.

‘It's not like they don't care or they want to be in this position. The ones I've spoken to, it’s affecting them a lot.’

Former United defender Gary Neville had a different view, however, telling Sky Sports: ‘They’ve downed tools and they’ve done this a number of times,’ said Neville. ‘They decide when to switch it on and off like a tap.’

Defender Harry Maguire - standing in as captain with Bruno Fernandes dropped following his criticism of the manager's tactics - spoke out in defence of Carrick at full time, saying: 'At the moment we're not doing enough as players. Michael turned our season on its head last year and we played brilliant football and got brilliant results. This season we haven't performed well enough as individuals.

'We have got to find something, question yourself, look in the mirror, that's the most important thing - think what you can do more and contribute to the team and if we do that we'll get somewhere.'

Former United defender Ashley Young, who won the 2012-13 Premier League title with the club, accused the players of 'giving up'.

'There have been different managers [in recent seasons] but it's the same players,' he said on Sky Sports. 'There have been a few changes in players but they're just not showing anything. You could tell today that it was like they'd given up - they're not running for this manager and they're not wanting to fight.

'The fans deserve so much more, you can tell they want more and they know he's been let down by those players.'

Jamie Carragher said that Carrick's position was 'untenable' at full time but he has also received widespread sympathy, with many considering the owners and top brass at the club to be culpable.

They recruited no defenders over the summer and are now shipping goals for fun - the only clean sheet they have kept all season was against Azerbaijani minnows Sabah.

Bournemouth's Evanilson curled in from long range to complete an afternoon of humiliation

The long-term decision-making of owners Sir Jim Ratcliffe and the Glazer family - as well as Berrada and Wilcox - has been called into question.

That was the subject of an explosive rant by Lisandro Martinez after the recent 2-0 loss to Atletico Madrid. The defender said earlier this month: 'I expect more (investment) 100 per cent. I expect more from our technical director. I have to be honest.

'As players we have to do more but it is also important when you make a strong squad to be ready for this kind of night.

'I have to control myself a lot but sometimes it's a reflection of the mirror of how our club is at the moment.

'We did a fantastic season last season and now we expect more from the top; more players to compete because many teams bring many players as well.'

But Carrick's authority over the players has been called into question after that swipe and the invective by Fernandes this week.

Club captain Fernandes was dropped after saying in the aftermatch of the Como drubbing: 'It's a decision from the staff to not press man to man and sometimes leave space behind and try to get the ball, wait for them, but sometimes when you give space to these teams they get confidence.'

Asked if he meant that Carrick got his tactics wrong, Fernandes added: ‘That's on the manager and staff to say, not me.

‘Sometimes you have to be more brave under pressure, take the risk of pressing high and making them uncomfortable. As you saw with Como, the centre back was coming to mark me in my own half. We need to do that as a team but we were unable to.'

Wayne Rooney lambasted Manchester United's players in the wake of such comments, describing the group as 'selfish' and 'like babies' amid a dismal run of form.

He told the United Stand podcast: 'These players, they're selfish. They don't care about their team-mates, don't care about the manager, the staff or the fans, they care about themselves. If they're not getting what's right for them, they're like babies and just throw their toys out of the pram and go and deflect the blame on to anyone else but themselves.'

Carrick admitted ahead of the Bournemouth match that the club has 'lost our way' in a five-minute speech.

He took over from Ruben Amorim on an interim basis last season, steering the club to third and Champions League qualification, but has won just two of 12 games this campaign.

Sports.title: Marcus Smith's magic moment set the tone for Harlequins' derby day win over Saracens - and was finely timed before England's autumn camp, writes NIK SIMON
Sports.content:
Marcus Smith's magic moment set the tone for Harlequins' derby day win over Saracens - and was finely timed before England's autumn camp, writes NIK SIMON

Of all the 200 games in Marcus Smith’s highlight reel, none have delivered a moment quite like this.

Since he was a teenager, the Harlequins No 10 has wowed the Stoop with his box of tricks in attack.

Yet the moment that epitomised Harlequins’ derby day victory came in defence – at the expense of Saracens full-back Max Malins. Midway through the first-half, Malins was nonchalantly coasting under the posts to score.

Smith arrived from the blindside and whacked the ball out of his grasp. No try. It was reminiscent of the showboating blooper that stalked Freddie Burns through the latter half of his career and it will leave a similar knot in Malins’ stomach.

‘They’re statements, aren’t they?’ said Harlequins coach Jason Gilmore. Everyone knows Harlequins, when they’re at their best, can play a really free-flowing rugby but we’ve got to have grit on the other side of the ball. Credit to Jordan Turner Hall who is doing a great job with our defence.

That moment just sets a standard for the boys. If Smithy’s not going to die on plays then we’re in the contest. I thought that was a really big statement for our boys.’

Marcus Smith (left) took advantage of Max Malins' nonchalance to tackle him and stop what should have been a certain try for the Saracens man

Saracens head coach Joe Shaw added: ‘Max could have got that 99 times out of 100. Of course it is frustrating. We weren’t playing our best but we were still in touching distance. Max is 30 years old. We have all messed up. But we lost the game as a collective not because Max did not put the ball down.’

This was Smith at his fiery best, finely timed before England gather for their autumn camp on Monday morning.

He linked up with Cadan Murley, his old housemate, to score the first try after three minutes. Harlequins never relinquished their lead.

‘I think Danny Care is the quintessential Harlequin but Smithy’s number two,’ added Gilmore, whose side lost their opening three games of the season.

‘The work that Smithy puts in, the care that he has for the club… he’s only 27 and he’s played 200 games for us. He’s come back from a broken finger and led us around the park really well.’

On paper, George Martin and Maro Itoje looked like they would bully the Harlequins pack. This was their first start together at club level and they lacked cohesion.

Instead, it was the likes of Fin Baxter – making his first appearance for 10 months - and Seb Driscoll who dominated the collisions. They forced errors in the tackle and won key turnovers in defence. It was a day when the hosts delivered both style and substance.

The hosts beat defenders in the tackle, providing the go-forward that allowed Smith to cut open the Saracens defence.

Fin Baxter (ball carrier) made his first appearance for 10 months and impressed

Ben Earl and Fergus Burke were sin-binned in the first-half as Saracens’ discipline slipped. They conceded nine penalties in the opening 27 minutes, helping Harlequins rack up the bonus-point try before half time, when Baxter was withdrawn early.

‘We were looking at giving Fin 40 to 50 minutes,’ revealed Gilmore, who expected Steve Borthwick to pick Baxter against Australia next month. ‘We don’t want to be too greedy. We haven’t had him for a while. Having our top props on the radar will be massive for us.

‘I thought he came back and played really strongly. You bang another game into him against a big Exeter pack next week – hopefully push him to 50 or 60 minutes. Then it’s up to Steve. We’ve just got to make sure we don’t overload him too early but I’d certainly back him.’

Harlequins described this game as their ‘cup final’. They beat Saracens at home last season – before winning just one league game in the following five months. Their challenge now is to prove this performance was not an anomaly.

Saracens have lost three games from five this season and they too are left searching for consistency. They have committed to a policy to rotate their team for the first nine games of the season and the lack of cohesion is beginning to cost them.

Smith was at his fiery best for Harlequins in their victory over Saracens at The Stoop

Noah Caluori, Alfie Barbeary, Owen Farrell and Charlie Bracken were all rested this weekend but Shaw defended his team’s policy: ‘We have chopped and changed, so I understand why people are asking. That’s how it was a decade ago.

‘It's not some random thing we're trying to be quirky with. We believe there is merit in what we're doing. We know our cohesion numbers aren’t as high as somebody like Gloucester.

'Our strategy is to have a strong group, with depth, but you have to perform to keep your seat in the latter half of the season. That’s harder to say on days like this. You can’t sugar coat it. It was a disappointing day at the office for us.’

Sports.title: Michael Carrick 'deliberately tried to EMBARRASS' Bruno Fernandes by dropping him against Bournemouth, claims Jamie Carragher - as Man United boss explains why he dropped his captain after midweek outburst
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick 'deliberately tried to EMBARRASS' Bruno Fernandes by dropping him against Bournemouth, claims Jamie Carragher - as Man United boss explains why he dropped his captain after midweek outburst

Jamie Carragher has claimed Michael Carrick left Bruno Fernandes on the bench during Man United's defeat by Bournemouth to 'embarrass him in front of the supporters'.

Fernandes, 32, was dropped from the starting XI by the under pressure Carrick after his explosive outburst following United's shambolic 4-1 defeat away to Como in the Champions League on Wednesday.

That represented the first time Fernandes has been pulled from the line-up for non-fitness reasons since Carrick, again, took him out against Villarreal in November 2021.

The move didn't have the desired impact though as United were dominated by Bournemouth, yet Carrick refused to turn to his club captain.

Lisandro Martinez and Matheus Cunha were initially summoned from the bench, and even when United went 3-0 down after 71 minutes, Carrick brought on Joshua Zirkzee and youngster Shea Lacey instead as he only used four of his permitted five substitutes.

Fernandes looked subdued on the bench throughout the game, and Carragher felt Carrick never had any intention of using him.

Jamie Carragher claimed Michael Carrick 'tried to embarrass' Bruno Fernandes by leaving him on the bench against Bournemouth

Carrick dropped Fernandes after his midweek outburst in the media and refused to turn to him

'I don't think he was ever going to bring him on,' Carragher said on Sky Sports. 'It was a decision to just leave him on the bench and almost try and embarrass him a little bit in front of the supporters, I don't know.

'He brought him off in midweek and that's where the... what Bruno did after the game was on the back of him getting brought off.

'And I think Michael Carrick never had any intention of bringing him on at all today - that sub was never going to happen.'

Speaking after the defeat, which left Carrick on the brink of losing his job, the former midfielder refused to be drawn too much on the issue.

'He's fit and available but we decided to pick the team we did,' he said. 'Unfortunately for everyone, we didn't manage to get the right result.

'There's always times when you're trying to make decisions that make a difference.'

When the team news was announced earlier on Sunday, Carragher had claimed Fernandes' absence could be a positive for the side and also benefit several individual players.

Carragher explained: 'He's Man United's best player, PFA Player of the Year, but Michael Carrick had to make the stand. But, once you've put him there (on the bench) you need a result.

'You're hoping, could this (the benching) bring us together as a group because there's no doubt about it, even though he's the best player there will be a lot of people who don't like playing with him at Man United because he's permanently throwing his arms up at people.

'He's basically saying "you lot aren't good enough to play with me". That's what we see from Fernandes a lot when things aren't going right for Man United, so hopefully the players in the dressing room will stick together and that's what they'll need today.'

Pre-match, Carrick had said: 'When you're picking the starting XI and you've got options to choose from, it's always a difficult decision. We've got to make what we feel is the right one for today and the team to get the performance that we want.'

On whether Fernandes was dropped after his explosive outburst, he replied: '(The decision was for) pure footballing reasons.'

Carragher claimed that Carrick never had any intention of using Fernandes in Sunday's defeat

Fernandes, who is usually very deliberate in what he says in the media, was scathing in his criticism of coaches after the Como debacle.

'It's a decision from the staff to not press man-to-man and sometimes leave a little space in behind and try to get the ball in the first moment, to wait for them, to give them the ball,' he said.

'But sometimes when you give too much the ball to these teams they get confident, they have so many bodies behind the ball that make you run a lot, make people get frustrated, and then obviously when you recover the ball the legs are, and the brain, much more difficult to make it work.'

Sports.title: Pierre Sage's days at Crystal Palace feel numbered as clinical Newcastle triumph 2-0 to ease pressure on Matthias Jaissle, writes BOBBI MANZI
Sports.content:
Pierre Sage's days at Crystal Palace feel numbered as clinical Newcastle triumph 2-0 to ease pressure on Matthias Jaissle, writes BOBBI MANZI

Two managers were desperate to alleviate the pressure on their jobs at Selhurst Park on Sunday.

For 45 minutes, it looked as though both Matthias Jaissle and Pierre Sage would achieve that - with defences on top in a tame affair.

But an 11-minute Magpies masterclass saw Palace implode, leaving the Newcastle boss in a much more secure job than the man in the opposite dugout.

Newcastle sliced through Palace as William Osula roamed free of Chris Richards to poke Jacob Murphy’s cross home from close range. Harvey Barnes added the second, capping off a slick passing move with a neat finish inside the box.

Daily Mail Sport’s Bobby Manzi unpacks a consequential afternoon in south London.

Harvey Barnes and William Osula scored within 11 minutes of each other as Newcastle climbed to seventh in the Premier League

Defensive improvement

This was a monumental defensive performance from Jaissle’s side, who kept only their second clean sheet of the season.

Confidence in the Newcastle backline was low after conceding eight goals in their previous two away matches.

But a change in personnel at centre-back, bringing experienced heads Dan Burn and Fabian Schar in from the start, gave Newcastle much more stability.

Schar made 15 defensive contributions, 10 clearances and was not dribbled past once. Similar can be said of Burn alongside him.

Besides a good chance inside the six-yard box for Jean-Philippe Mateta inside the first five minutes, Palace did not create much of note.

There were some scruffy penalty area scrambles in the first half but Burn and Schar consistently found ways to deal with it.

Newcastle had greater defensive organisation, giving a stable platform to win for the first time since mid-September.

‘It’s important to mention Sven Botman and Malick Thiaw have done a good job in the last weeks,’ Jaissle said. ‘But we went for more experience and leadership to give stability to a young group who have been shaking a bit with the defeats. We’re really glad it worked out.’

The midfield pair were pivotal, too. Nico Gonzalez and Joelinton grafted defensively.

Every player knew their role in a dogged showing, and that will encourage Jaissle moving forward.

Matthias Jaissle's side were better at both ends of the pitch against struggling Crystal Palace

MATCH FACTS Crystal Palace (3-4-3): Benitez 5; Richards 4, Disasi 6, Canvot 6; Khalaili 6, Wharton 4, Kamada 6, Mitchell 6; McNeil 6 (Osorio 62min 6), Mateta 5 (Nketiah 62min 6), Pino 6 Booked: Canvot, Khalaili, Pino Manager: Pierre Sage 5 Newcastle United (4-2-3-1): Hornicek 8; Dedic 7 (Thiaw 90min), Schar 8, Burn 7, Hall 7; Gonzalez 8, Joelinton 7 (Steur 85min); Murphy 7, Willock 6 (Ramsey 77min 6), Barnes 7 (Elanga 77min 6); Osula 7 (Wissa 77min 6) Booked: Gonzalez, Schar Manager: Matthias Jaissle 8 Referee: Paul Tierney 7

Clinical Magpies

At the opposite end of the pitch, it was a clinical Newcastle performance. They did not have many chances, amassing less than one expected goal but lethally punished Palace’s mistakes to climb to seventh in the league.

Osula's goal came from nowhere after the break. Newcastle had created very little in the first half but Jaissle's team talk seemingly sparked them into life - moving the ball quicker and with more purpose.

It was a simple goal, a neat cross in and some clever movement. A perfect response to their dull first half where they did not manage a shot on target.

Again, their second goal was another rapid move. Adam Wharton’s sloppiness on the edge of the penalty area was punished as Newcastle quickly shifted the ball to the right, crossed low into the box before laying off to Barnes.

Moving forward, Newcastle must create more chances because, aside from the goals, they crafted very little.

But the clinical display – alongside the defensive strength – marked a step in the right direction.

Sage’s time to go

The season’s first managerial sacking is imminent. Will it be Palace manager Sage or Michael Carrick at Manchester United?

At this rate, both clubs could release their statements at the same time. If at least one hasn’t posted the traditional corner flag picture alongside an official statement by Monday afternoon, something has gone seriously wrong.

Palace have the worst defence in the Premier League, conceding 19 goals in eight games, with only Oliver Glasner’s Nottingham Forest keeping them outside of the relegation zone.

There were signs of improvement in the first half against Newcastle. Palace defended as a solid unit and did not offer Newcastle a shot on target.

However, they imploded straight after half time, shipping two cheap goals. Soft goals have been a hallmark of Sage’s side, as have lapses of concentration and inconsistent performances within games.

An 11-minute spell straight after the break killed all the positive work Palace had done.

It feels like Pierre Sage's days at Crystal Palace are numbered after another disapponting loss

Meanwhile, this was the second game in a row they conceded less than one xG but shipped two goals.

It can be argued that they have been unlucky with every mistake punished. But that is a product of the defensive structure, where they are asked to be aggressive and come unstuck when they don’t have the ball.

Sage believes possession is the best form of defence, which is slightly worrying considering only three teams have had less possession than Palace this season.

Palace have won just one of their last six, and Sage’s defensive record is alarming decision-makers. It is difficult to see him fighting on much longer. Palace play again on Wednesday, and the quick succession of games may be Sage’s saving grace.

But supporters are growing restless, booing the team and manager off the pitch on Sunday.

Sports.title: Bitter Brighton boss Fabian Hurzeler bizarrely claims Liverpool were NOT trying to 'win the game' - after watching his side lose at Anfield
Sports.content:
Brighton boss Fabian Hurzeler said there was one team trying to create chances at Anfield after his team fell to a 2-0 defeat against Liverpool.

A Pascal Gross own goal was followed by Alexander Isak’s sixth strike of the season as Andoni Iraola’s Reds climbed into the top four with their fourth win in a row.

But Hurzeler, whose side missed a sitter through Yasin Ayari at 0-0, praised his team for going toe-to-toe with Liverpool.

‘Everyone in the stadium saw that there was one team who really tried to create and try to win this game and therefore I have to praise my players,’ he said.

‘Everyone in the stadium felt there was a missed opportunity for us, because it's not only after the goal or the goals they scored.

‘Also, before they scored, we had one, two big chances and today I think it was just the difference that they scored, we didn't score.

Fabian Hurzeler said that only his Brighton team were trying to win the game... after they lost to Liverpool

‘Overall I saw a team with a lot of good things to take away. I saw a team that really had the belief in our approach, that stuck to the match plan, that always kept going, and that is very frustrating because we all have the feeling that there is a missed opportunity here today.’

Meanwhile, Iraola praised goal-scorer Isak and said: ‘Yes, Alex, he's a striker (where) if we can put him in those positions, provide him good crosses and good situations, he will score the goals.’

Iraola was also delighted with his side’s defensive battling, especially right back Ronald Araujo. The boss added: ‘I think we all enjoyed watching Ronald fighting. I think he's very good in the duels.

‘Even the first goal, I think he wins two duels in a row, he arrives at the byline and after, it's not an assist, but it's worth an assist. And defensively, I think he's been really, really, really good.’

Sports.title: This was the end for Michael Carrick after his gang of the damned were relentlessly dismantled 3-0 by Bournemouth... he will be the next to walk into Man United's endless winter, writes OLIVER HOLT
Sports.content:
The yellowed leaves fell from the trees and danced and skittered across the forecourt at Old Trafford. Squalls battered the old stadium and Manchester United supporters bowed their heads into the winds of Storm Boelo. These are the rites of autumn and, in this part of the city, they double as chronicles of deaths foretold. In the great churn of unfortunates who have occupied the manager’s position at United since Sir Alex Ferguson’s retirement in May 2013, October, November and December is the favoured sacking season. Jose Mourinho, Ole Gunnar Solskjaer and Erik ten Hag have all met their fates as the branches have been stripped bare. Now, it was Michael Carrick’s turn. This was the end for him. There can be little doubt about that. The United boss, a favourite son of the fans here when he was a player, a decent, modest, self-effacing man, stood on the touchline in a coat of funereal black, his arms folded in front of him, his face set in a desperate grimace as he watched his gang of the damned being relentlessly dismantled by Bournemouth. It was hard to watch, just as it had been hard to watch United humiliated by Como in the Champions League last week. The truth was obvious: this United is a rabble, a loose collection of over-entitled, overpaid, over-promoted and overdone losers who have done their bit to throw their boss under the bus. It is easy to say but the way some of them played against Marco Rose’s intelligent, well-drilled, energetic team, they do not deserve to wear the United shirt. They are not fit for it. They are an embarrassment to it. This comprehensive 3-0 defeat left them in 16th place in the Premier League, one point above the relegation zone. It is where they deserve to be. Carrick cannot survive this and, particularly, he cannot survive the manner of recent defeats. This was the end for him and it ought to be the end for some of the hapless club apparatchiks who let him down in the summer with their hopeless recruitment in the transfer window. Manchester United were hammered 3-0 at home by Bournemouth on another dismal day The damaging defeat leaves Red Devils boss Michael Carrick on the brink of losing his job The club is in chaos, on and off the field. Bruno Fernandes, the club captain, was dropped after criticising Carrick in midweek. Lisandro Martinez, who was disciplined for criticising the club’s owners, did return against Bournemouth but only in the second half. He is a liability anyway. This is not all on Carrick, though. In fact, in the list of those responsible for this shambles, he is low on the list. The Glazers, who have pillaged the club, are top of the list. Sir Jim Ratcliffe, the minority owner, who has overseen the descent into this mayhem, is next. This is a club riven by dissent from top to bottom, a club that has declared war on its most loyal supporters by trying to accelerate the move away from season ticket holders towards tourists and day-trippers because money is king for this regime and season-ticket holders do not spend enough on match days. It was little wonder that, as Bournemouth scored goal after goal, the supporters turned their ire on the owners and their much-trumpeted plans for a move away from Old Trafford. How empty and futile those plans seem when the club is in this state. ‘You can stick your new stadium up your arse,’ the Stretford End sang. And so Carrick stood there in that black coat, arms folded, taking the brickbats. ‘You’re getting sacked in the morning,’ the Bournemouth fans yelled at him. Carrick and United are easy meat. ‘You’re going down with the City,’ they chanted delightedly as United melted away in front of them. The first drama of the day had come before kick-off with the publication of the United teamsheet. It showed that Fernandes, the club captain and the man who has carried the team through many of the lean years at Old Trafford, had been dropped. Harry Maguire was named as skipper in his stead. After his criticism of Carrick’s tactics following the humiliating Champions League defeat to Como last week, it was hardly a surprise that Fernandes paid the penalty. Carrick would have looked weak if he had started him. Carrick may be standing on a burning deck but he was still trying to reassert his authority amid the flames. The chants against the Glazers and Ratcliffe started soon after kick-off. So did the Bournemouth chances. Rayan headed just wide from Bournemouth’s first corner and burst through on a breakaway only to drive his shot straight at a defender as United retreated in disarray. Bournemouth were superb, yet United were woeful and another manager looks set to leave The defeat leaves United just above the relegation zone with seven points from eight games United's fans turned on the club's hierarchy as Bournemouth extended their lead (pictured - CEO Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox), but continued to support Carrick Bournemouth failed to capitalise as the opportunities kept coming. When Marcus Tavernier escaped yet again down the left wing, he drove his cross straight into the arms of Senne Lammens but as United’s defenders remonstrated with each other, the Stretford End lost its patience and roared out its dismay at what was happening. Ayden Heaven was lucky to escape with a yellow card for launching himself into the air and into a double-footed tackle that Evanilson skipped out of rather than risk serious injury. Then, from the resulting free kick eight minutes before half-time, Bournemouth took the lead that their play had deserved. Justin Kluivert swung the ball to the back post and sailed over the massed ranks of the United defence to where Rayan was ghosting in. Rayan was unmarked. He met the ball on the volley with his left foot and rammed it past Lammens. United tried to complain about a foul but they had no grounds. Five minutes later, Bournemouth doubled their lead. Leny Yoro slipped under pressure on the right side of the United box and Adrien Truffert pounced on the mistake and squared the ball to Tavernier. Tavernier completed the formalities, turning the ball past Lammens from close range. Old Trafford erupted in a fusillade of boos. A black flag was lowered from the back of the first tier of the Stretford End that said, in red letters, ‘Standards’. The outline of the faces of Roy Keane, Eric Cantona and Bryan Robson were below it, symbols of better times and better players. ‘You’re getting sacked in the morning,’ the Bournemouth fans sang at Carrick. United were dire. Djordje Petrovic did save well from Bryan Mbeumo just before the interval but it was a rare moment of threat. There were more groans from the crowd when Mason Mount’s corner failed miserably to clear the first defender. It was another symbol of a miserable half for the home team. Things were still not bad enough to prompt Carrick to call on Fernandes. Maybe nothing would have been. He did bring Matheus Cunha on for Youri Tielemans but Evanilson had a goal disallowed for offside seconds after the restart. Bournemouth should have been three up a couple of minutes later. Rayan, one-on-one with Lammens, hit the ball too close to the goalkeeper. But United barely posed a threat. They hardly ever do. In seven of their 11 games this season United have failed to score more than once. United have only 10 goals in eight league outings now. They are toothless as well as gutless. Carrick dropped Bruno Fernandes for the match and then left him on the bench throughout Bournemouth were superb as they capped off one of the best weeks in the club's history Bournemouth should have won by more but their third was a beauty. Twenty minutes from time, Lewis Cook played a ball down the line and Lammens hurtled out of his goal in a doomed attempt to try to get to it first. Evanilson got to it first, took it round the goalkeeper and clipped the ball brilliantly into the empty goal from a tight angle. United’s humiliation was almost complete. In the dying minutes, the United fans chanted abuse at Ratcliffe’s henchmen Jason Wilcox, the director of football, and Omar Berrada, the chief executive. But everyone knows that it will not be them who pay the price. In autumn’s parade of the damned, Carrick will be the next to walk into Manchester United’s endless winter.

Sports.title: Man United 0-3 Bournemouth PLAYER RATINGS: Which 3/10 star was totally off the pace in Old Trafford disaster? Who looked reckless and naive? And which Reds midfielder has escaped criticism for too long?
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick is hanging on to his job as Manchester United manager by a thread after his side were handsomely turned over 3-0 at Old Trafford by Bournemouth.

Goals from Rayan, Marcus Tavernier and Evanilson did the damage but by the time the boos rang out at full-time, Carrick will have been fully aware that this may be his final act as manager.

He did so by dropping captain Bruno Fernandes, and choosing not to bring him on at any stage, which felt a significant message, albeit one that will fall on deaf ears after another shocking defeat.

Bournemouth were excellent just days on from drubbing Ruben Amorim's AC Milan and they look everything United are not: hungry, organised, and going places.

Daily Mail Sport's NATHAN SALT was at Old Trafford to run the rule over the two sides...

Evanilson made it 3-0 to cap a painful afternoon for Manchester United and Michael Carrick

Carrick knew this may have been the end of his brief reign at Old Trafford

Manchester United (4-2-3-1)

Senne Lammens – 3

Looked to be coming out relatively blame-free – the defence in front of him isn’t giving him a chance on goals like the first two – but all the blame fell at his feet for the third, which killed the game. Rushed out and was left looking foolish by the brilliant Evanilson.

Leny Yoro – 4

Recently, Yoro has played relatively well for large spells of a game, only for key moments to undo all the good. He made a crucial clearance in the six-yard box eight minutes in to deny Evanilson a tap in but later made a costly slip on the stroke of half-time as Bournemouth made it 2-0. Looked like he wanted Old Trafford to swallow him up.

Harry Maguire – 5

Wearing the captain’s armband in the Premier League for the first time since May 2023, Maguire made an attempt to encourage team-mates before kick-off – evidently it all fell on deaf ears. A couple of driving runs got the crowd off their seats but he could do nothing to stop the bleeding.

Ayden Heaven – 3

Flew in recklessly with both feet off the ground to give away the free-kick from which Bournemouth opened the scoring. Was very fortunate to get away with another mistake early in the second when his misplaced pass set Rayan free. Looked naive out there – which was probably why Carrick eventually hooked him.

Ayden Heaven was booked for a two-footed challenge that Evanilson evaded

Diogo Dalot – 3

Got torched defensively by Rayan and wasted so many good opportunities at the other end when United were crying out for one good cross into the box. It would never arrive. He’s best described as a willing runner who is well short of the required standard.

Andrey Santos – 4

Looks so pedestrian in the middle of the park when the hope was he would bring that youth and exuberance you would expect from a 22-year-old. Maybe he’s been ground down by the malaise at United but he’s fallen well short of expectations and this display was no different.

Carlos Baleba – 5

Made a couple of smart interceptions but we’re clutching at straws from a desperately drab display. Needs to get better at finding the decisive pass when he does break up opposition play – which he does better than anyone else in this side.

Amad – 5

Got one of the biggest cheers of the day from the home crowd with a clever piece of skill to nutmeg Adrien Truffert. But he’s a moments player that isn’t producing enough of them. His lack of pace is a real problem, too, given United are already badly short in that department.

Youri Tielemans – 3

Looked totally off the pace in his preferred No 10 position and was hooked at half-time. Tielemans has shown flashes of real quality in recent weeks as it’s all unravelled but there was none of that here. Booked.

Youri Tielemans looked off the pace and was replaced at half-time

Mason Mount – 4

He’s been here too long now to keep going through games making little to no positive impact on it from an attacking sense. Starting on the left he was largely invisible and that changed little when moved to No 10 at half-time. Has escaped criticism for too long.

Bryan Mbeumo – 5

Started the game as the only Manchester United player to have scored a Premier League goal in 2026, which helped underline how far this club has fallen. Looked like the only one capable of scoring on another disastrous day for the club.

MANAGER: Michael Carrick – 3

Was ballsy in dropping captain and talisman Bruno Fernandes to the bench after his comments in Como but this was a performance that showed both he and his players have no idea what it is they want or are trying to do. A dead man walking, unfortunately.

SUBS

Matheus Cunha (for Youri Tielemans, 46) – 5

Tried to inject some energy into proceedings and quickly discovered those around him were not on the same page.

Lisandro Martinez (for Ayden Heaven, 64) – 4

Slipped soon after coming on and Rayan should have scored. No idea what he was unhappy with as Bournemouth made a mockery of the back-line for the third.

Joshua Zirkzee (for Carlos Baleba, 71) – 5

Chucked on in hope more so than expectation and unsurprisingly found chances hard to come by.

Shea Lacey (for Amad, 78) - 5

AFC BOURNEMOUTH (4-2-3-1)

Djordje Petrovic – 7

Made a huge save moments after Bournemouth scored to tip Mbeumo’s cross-goal shot wide and he's quickly showing himself to be a very good young goalkeeper.

Bryan Mbeumo had an early effort saved by Djordje Petrovic, who impressed

Adam Smith – 6

Been here since the League One days and shows no signs of becoming any less influential for this group. His leadership is so important to all the good that comes from the more creative players ahead of him.

Antonio Silva – 8

The 22-year-old has taken to the Premier League like a duck to water and showed with his reading of the game here why Bournemouth once again face a fight to keep hold of a rising young star at the back for the long term.

James Hill – 7

His long throw gave United – a dreadfully poor team from set pieces – plenty to think about early on and he made a crucial sliding intervention to stop Mbeumo getting a back post tap-in in the first half. Not flashy but he’s ever so reliable.

Adrien Truffert – 7

Would not have believed his luck after his harrying forced Yoro into a costly mistake, leaving Truffert the chance to deliver his easiest assist of the season to tee up Tavernier. Managed to limit Amad to relatively little at the other end so a good day all told for the Frenchman.

Adrien Truffert capitalised on Leny Yoro's slip to set up Bournemouth's second

Lewis Cook – 6

Didn’t do a great deal to catch the eye but that’s not why Marco Rose has him in that midfield pivot. Reads the game really well and he managed to unsettle both Baleba and Santos, which was a job well done.

Tyler Adams – 6

Will have taken headlines for his decision not to take the knee pre-match but thereafter he had a very quiet afternoon where he let those ahead of him do the talking.

Rayan – 7

A brilliant display that deserved more. A couple of spurned finishes before Evanilson added the cherry on top will be the bug-bear as he watches the film back. He's got all the potential to be one of the best players in the league at his current trajectory.

Justin Kluivert – 7

Left the pitch having created the most chances of any player out there for the 63 minutes of action he got. His delivery for Bournemouth’s opening goal was as brilliant as United’s defending for it was awful.

Marcus Tavernier celebrates scoring the second goal with Justin Kluivert

Marcus Tavernier – 7

A name that has cropped up in United recruitment meetings of late and you can see why with his boundless energy. An under the radar gem in the league.

Evanilson – 8

A constant menace that is rapidly ascending the rankings as one of the Premier League’s very best attackers. He’s not the biggest, nor the quickest, but he’s clever and his movement at times here was magnificent. His goal here to make it 3-0 was absolutely outstanding. Expect a huge bid or two for Evanilson in the summer.

MANAGER: Marco Rose – 8

Has bemoaned his side for not killing games off in second halves and he will have been thrilled that his side, just days removed from the Milan rout, never let up against this hapless United.

SUBS

Ben Gannon-Doak (for Justin Kluivert, 63) – 6

Was busy without setting off fireworks. The game was won at this stage and his role was not to put on a show.

Ryan Christie (for Lewis Cook, 75) – 6

Junior Kroupi (for Evanilson, 87)

Bafode Diakite (for Adam Smith, 87)

Sports.title: Hallgrimsson urges UEFA to keep Ireland and Israel apart in future
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland drew 1-1 with Israel in a behind-closed-doors contest in Serbia; there were allegations of spitting by an Israeli player at half-time, while the Israeli government criticised the Irish players for bowing their heads during the national anthem

Republic of Ireland: Heimir Hallgrimsson calls on UEFA to keep Ireland and Israel apart in future after tense draw

Ireland's head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson has called for UEFA to keep his team and Israel separate in future

Heimir Hallgrimsson has called on UEFA to keep Ireland and Israel apart in future.

The Ireland boss was speaking following his side's 1-1 UEFA Nations League draw with Israel behind closed doors in Serbia.

The games between the two nations this international break were overshadowed by politics, with the Football Association of Ireland (FAI) urged to boycott the internationals amid ongoing conflict in the Israel-Gaza War.

This continued in Serbia, as Ireland fitness coach Damien Doyle was allegedly spat on by an Israeli player at half-time, according to reports in the stadium.

Irish media reported that the incident took place as the teams went down the tunnel. Ireland boss Hallgrimsson confirmed there was an allegation, but he admitted he didn't see it and declined to comment further on it.

However, when asked if the two countries should be playing each other again, he told RTE Sport: "No, they shouldn't. That's not ours to decide - that's UEFA who decides that. Obviously, there's a big support for Palestine in Ireland. There's not many countries that support Palestine as much as Ireland does.

"I wouldn't wish any national team to go through what we've gone through in these two weeks, so maybe UEFA just needs to step in and do something."

Sky Sports News has contacted UEFA for comment.

Israeli Government accuses ROI of 'moral blindness'

The Israeli Government have accused the Ireland football team of "moral blindness" for bowing their heads during their national anthem.

For the second time in a week, the Irish players, coaching team and FAI all bowed their heads while the Israeli national anthem was played pre-match.

Image: Republic of Ireland players bowed their heads during the national anthem

The official Israeli Government X account posted: "While some use the football field as their political theatre, for us this is personal.

"1939: Irish players raised their arms in salute to Nazi Germany.

"2026: Irish players bowed their heads during Israel's anthem.

"Different generations. The same moral blindness.

"Today, Israel's players wear black armbands to remember those brutally massacred by Hamas on October 7 - including former professional footballer Lior Asulin.

"Some of us have skin in the game. Others just make a show of it."

Sky Sports News has contacted the FAI for comment.

Two Israeli journalists banned for post-match press conferences

Meanwhile, prior to the match, UEFA confirmed that two Israeli journalists were banned from the post-match press conferences, after Saturday's pre-match Ireland press conference descended into chaos.

The media access for Ireland was cut short after an Israeli journalist alleged that Israeli players had claimed Irish players had racially abused them during the match in Hungary last weekend.

The journalist alleged that a derogatory term had been used, which Sky Sports has chosen not to repeat. The term is not associated with antisemitic or anti-Israeli abuse.

An Irish press officer refuted the allegation, saying: "That's completely untrue," before bringing the news conference to a premature close.

After the press conference ended abruptly, Serbian police were called following an allegation of assault by an Israeli journalist, who said a microphone had been taken from them by an FAI press officer.

Sky Sports News understands that no further action was taken by police.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland draw with Israel in second Nations League meeting
Sports.content:
Match report and reaction as Republic of Ireland drew 1-1 with Israel in behind-closed-doors contest in Serbia; Troy Parrott's first-half penalty was cancelled out after the break; sides clashed at half-time

Republic of Ireland 1-1 Israel: Troy Parrott scores again as sides draw second controversial Nations League meeting

The Republic of Ireland drew 1-1 with Israel in the second controversial Nations League fixture between the sides.

Troy Parrott's first-half penalty was cancelled out by Dor Peretz after the break in the behind-closed-doors game in Serbia.

The Republic's 'home' fixture was held on neutral territory at the 4,500-seat TSC arena in Backa Topola, due to "operational challenges that could impact on the delivery of the game on home soil" according to a June Football Association of Ireland (FAI) statement.

Both sides wore black armbands. The Republic's, the same as in Hungary to acknowledge - as the Football Association of Ireland chief David Courrell explained before that contest - "all lives lost" in the ongoing Israel-Hamas conflict.

Israel's armbands - which read "7.10" - were to commemorate the October 7, 2023 Hamas-led attack on southern Israel, their official X account confirmed.

The pitch featured no sponsored content or branding, just UEFA graphics with slogans like "football for all", a decision taken by the FAI.

Image: The referee pleads with the benches in Serbia

Tensions rose at half-time after a fracas broke out in front of the tunnel and players from both sides engaged in a heated argument, with the Israeli Government later accusing Irish players of "moral blindness" for bowing their heads during Israel's national anthem, as they did in Monday's first match.

Officials broke up a second altercation in three minutes of added time, and there were more heated words exchanged after the final whistle.

On the pitch Parrott, who has now scored 10 times in his last seven competitive internationals, fired the Republic in front from the spot in the 39th minute before Dor Peretz drew the sides level two minutes after the restart.

The result puts Ireland third in Nations League Group B3, level on points with second-placed Kosovo.

Hallgrimsson calls on UEFA to keep Ireland and Israel apart in future

Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson has called on UEFA to keep Ireland and Israel apart in future.

Speaking after the 1-1 draw, Hallgrimsson also declined to comment on the half-time fracas between the two sides.

When asked if the two countries should be playing each other again, he told RTE Sport: "No, they shouldn't. That's not ours to decide - that's UEFA who decides that. Obviously, there's a big support for Palestine in Ireland. There's not many countries that support Palestine as much as Ireland does.

"I wouldn't wish any national team to go through what we've gone through in these two weeks, so maybe UEFA just needs to step in and do something."

On the half-time incident, he said in his post-match press conference: "I was there. I'm not going to comment on it. It's something that a disciplinary committee is probably going to look at."

Sky Sports News has contacted UEFA for comment.

Two Israeli journalists banned for post-match press conferences

Meanwhile, prior to the match, UEFA confirmed that two Israeli journalists were banned from the post-match press conferences, after Saturday's pre-match Ireland press conference descended into chaos.

The media access for Ireland was cut short after an Israeli journalist alleged that Israeli players had claimed Irish players had racially abused them during the match in Hungary last weekend.

The journalist alleged a derogatory term was used - which Sky Sports has chosen not to repeat. It is not a term associated with being antisemitic or anti-Israeli.

An Irish press officer refuted the allegation, saying "that's completely untrue", and brought the news conference to a premature close.

After the press conference ended abruptly, Serbian police were called due to an allegation of assault by an Israeli journalist who had the microphone taken from them by an FAI press officer.

Sky Sports News understands there was no further action was taken by police.

Sports.title: Ireland news conference cut short after tense exchanges with Israeli media
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland vs Israel is being played in Serbia as the FAI moved the game to a neutral venue for "operational reasons" in June following widespread calls for a boycott; protests briefly halted Ireland's draw with Austria on Thursday over opposition to Sunday's Israel fixture

Republic of Ireland vs Israel: Heimir Hallgrimsson's press conference cut short after tense exchanges with Israeli media

Republic of Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson's pre-match press conference ahead of Sunday's match against Israel in Serbia ended abruptly after a tense exchange with Israeli media.

The media access was cut short after an Israeli journalist alleged that Israeli players had claimed they were racially abused by Irish players during their match in Hungary last Sunday.

The journalist alleged a derogatory term was used - which Sky Sports has chosen not to repeat. It is not a term associated with being antisemitic or anti-Israeli.

An Irish press officer refuted the allegation, saying "that's completely untrue", and brought the news conference to a premature close as one of his colleagues remonstrated with the reporter.

Image: Ireland's players bowed their heads before facing Israel in the reverse fixture last week

Hallgrimsson later labelled the accusation a "verbal attack" during a separate briefing for members of the Irish press.

The exchange in the main press conference took place after Hallgrimsson was also asked a question about a co-pilot who attacked a pilot and tried to hijack a flight travelling from Dubai to Tel Aviv earlier this week.

The reporter's question was shut down by the FAI press officer.

Sky Sports News understands there are no open UEFA investigations at this stage from the previous meeting between Israel and Ireland last weekend.

The FAI are conducting their own investigation into whether striker Adam Idah was racially abused by Israeli supporters during their 3-0 UEFA Nations League win but have yet to make an official complaint to UEFA.

Image: Protesters interrupted Ireland's draw with Austria by throwing tennis balls onto the pitch with Palestine flags on them

Despite the high-profile nature of the fixture, members of the Irish media later reported that there was no UEFA delegate present at the news conference.

Sky Sports News was told a UEFA match delegate does not have to attend press conferences. The duty is left to the venue media manager, whose job it is to report anything if there is an incident.

Sunday's match is being played in Backa Topola, Serbia, as the FAI moved the game to a neutral venue for "operational reasons" in June following widespread calls for a boycott.

Sky Sports News has approached the FAI for comment.

Sports.title: Ireland held by Austria despite Parrott double as protests interrupt game
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott scored twice but the Republic of Ireland were forced to settle for a 2-2 draw after Austria came back in the second half of their Nations League encounter at the Aviva Stadium in Dublin.

The contest was twice interrupted in the opening 45 minutes, first due to what campaign group Stop the Game later referred to in a statement as a "limited tennis ball protest", when - around the 20th minute - tennis balls wrapped in stickers featuring the Palestinian flag and the text '#StopTheGame' were launched onto the pitch.

The match paused a second time when an invader carrying what appeared to be a Palestine flag entered the pitch and was promptly tackled and carried off by security.

The protests came after Ireland's decision not to boycott their game against Israel last week - although goalkeeper Gavin Bazunu did make himself unavailable.

Ireland are due to face Israel again on Sunday.

Image: Tennis balls with Palestine flags were throw onto the pitch

Before the protests, Parrott scored a sensational 12th-minute opener, and then added a penalty on the stroke of half-time.

A pair of substitutes proved Ireland's undoing after Alexander Prass halved the deficit in the 71st minute and Michael Gregoritsch drew the sides level six minutes later.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had a chance to top Group B3 with a victory, but they sit third behind Austria and Kosovo at the halfway point of the group stage.

Hallgrimsson made three changes, including the reintroduction of Finn Azaz, who was greeted warmly when his name was announced over the PA system before the match.

Bazunu was back in the squad, while Liam Scales and John Egan were awarded starts.

There was a significant security and police presence outside the stadium, where a small group of protesters also gathered before kick-off.

There was an audacious early effort from Sasa Kalajdzic, who tried to catch Caoimhin Kelleher off his line with a lob from midfield, before Ireland enjoyed a couple of attacking spells deep in the visitors' half.

Image: Parrott is congratulated after scoring his second goal against Austria

It was a brilliant opener from Parrott, who realised he was on his own after bringing down Adam Idah's glanced-on header from a goal kick.

The Real Betis striker was sandwiched in a triangle of white shirts, before nutmegging Philipp Lienhardt and evading every other challenger with a mazy run before planting the ball past Florian Wiegele and into the bottom corner.

Image: A protestor was carried off the pitch during the game

Kelleher denied Patrick Wimmer and there were a few more promising spells for Austria before Parrott doubled their lead.

Ryan Manning won the penalty after he was clipped in the box by Nicolas Seiwald. Parrott stepped up after a VAR check and blasted it past the Austria 'keeper.

Austria cut the deficit after Liam Kitching was caught out and Austria worked the ball to the unmarked Prass, who blasted the ball beyond Kelleher. The offside flag was initially raised, but the decision was reversed after a VAR check.

The Brentford goalkeeper then failed to stop Gregoritsch's free-kick as Ralf Rangnick's side fought back for a point.

Ireland captain Dara O'Shea was denied by an excellent leaping Wiegele save, Gregoritsch directed a shot over the crossbar and both sides fended off attempts at a late winner.

Sports.title: Hallgrimsson admits 'toughest days' of career after Ireland beat Israel
Sports.content:
The Republic of Ireland beat Israel 3-0 in their controversial Nations League fixture at a neutral venue in Hungary.

Players did not shake hands with each other before their meeting at the Nagyerdei Stadion in Debrecen and there was no exchange between Ireland captain Dara O'Shea and Israel's Manor Solomon.

Ireland players also appeared to bow their heads while Israel's national anthem was played out before kick-off.

Black armbands were worn by Ireland players, which Football Association of Ireland (FAI) chief executive David Courell said was a gesture to recognise "all lives lost" in the Israel-Gaza conflict.

Goalkeeper Gavin Bazunu was the only player who chose not to play after the squad voted to proceed with the match on Saturday amid calls for the game not to go ahead.

Goals from Troy Parrott, Adam Idah and Jack Moylan sealed the victory for Heimir Hallgrimsson's side.

Moylan celebrated his goal by kissing and raising his black armband before kissing his badge.

Hallgrimsson: I couldn't be more proud of the players

Republic of Ireland manager Heimir Hallgrimsson:

"It has been some of the toughest days of my coaching career, but its not about me.

"The game, the desire the players showed to make a statement on the pitch - they are football players, they wanted to show on the pitch, make that talking with their feet.

"What they did was impressive. In tough times that's when you find your leaders, there were so many players that stepped up in these tough times. The energy levels they showed was impressive.

"The performance was good given all the preparation, the lack of training, all of our meetings were about something other than football.

"I couldn't be more proud of the players.

"By playing I know we are making some people unhappy. By playing we are making others happy. Winning probably pleases everyone, but there will still be people angry that we played the game.

"I hope we can settle that slowly down and stay together as a team. I wish people in Ireland continue supporting these boys, because they certainly deserve it."

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland slip to deserved defeat in Kosovo
Sports.content:
The Republic of Ireland slipped to a 1-0 defeat away to Kosovo in their Nations League opener in Pristina.

The build-up to the League B3 encounter had been overshadowed by the controversy around upcoming fixtures against Israel, which Republic boss Heimir Hallgrimsson had admitted many of his squad members were uncomfortable about playing.

Chiedozie Ogbene had fired an early chance over before Kosovo responded to finish the first half strongly at the Fadil Vokrri Stadium.

The home side saw two shots cleared off the line and Ireland goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher then clawed away a header from Vedat Muriqi as Hallgrimsson's side got to the break on level terms.

Ireland - who are scheduled to play Israel in Hungary on Sunday and then again in a 'home' tie at another neutral venue in Serbia seven days later - dug in for the second half but were eventually undone with seven minutes left when Kosovo captain Muriqi bundled the ball in from close range.

Udinese defender James Abankwah was handed a first competitive start as part of a back five, with in-form Real Betis striker Troy Parrott the lone forward and Dara O'Shea taking the captain's armband.

Image: The Republic of Ireland have won two of their six games in 2026 so far

Ireland created what ended up being their only real clear chance in the 22nd minute. Abankwah got away down the right and ran into the Kosovo penalty area before cutting the ball back to Ogbene, who sent a curling effort over the crossbar.

Kosovo, who are in League B for the first time, went close on the half-hour mark when a cross from the left found its way through to Muriqi, whose angled shot was cleared off the line by Jayson Molumby.

Veldin Hodza then saw his 10-yard strike blocked in front of goal by O'Shea before Kelleher got up to claw away a looping header from Muriqi, which was set for the top corner.

Ireland made a positive start to the second half, with a deep cross from the right by Abankwah finding Parrott at the far post and his header was gathered by Kosovo goalkeeper Arijanet Muric.

Image: Vedat Muriqi scored the winner for Kosovo

Kosovo, though, continued to carry a threat themselves. Baton Zabergja sent a 20-yard effort just wide of the top corner, which again got the home supporters into full voice.

Muriqi forced Kelleher into another smart reaction save from an angled shot at the near post before Kosovo eventually made the breakthrough in the 83rd minute.

Ermal Krasniqi's shot was deflected onto the crossbar and Muriqi reacted quickest in a crowded six-yard box to nod the ball over the line.

Kosovo should have got a second late on when substitute Krasniqi dragged his shot wide after being set up by Muriqi following a break onto a long ball.

Ireland pay price for 'off day'

Ireland manager Heimir Hallgrimsson told RTE:

"[Kosovo are] a good team, momentum with them, crowd with them, and to be honest they deserve the win.

"There was nothing that we didn't know about how they would play, where their threats would be, but [it was] an off day for a lot of our players and [it is] a tough place to come to if you have an off day, so a deserved win for Kosovo."

Hallgrimsson added: "We were the team that needed to defend today and didn't connect in possession or passes, not as sharp as we have done.

"We have to quickly find out the reason that we had an off day. We can all do better than we did today.

"It is a two-day turnaround for the next one, so we better be quick…and do better than this versus Israel. They are probably in the same position as us [having lost to Austria]."

Asked if the controversy from playing the fixtures against Israel had impacted on his team's performance against Kosovo, Hallgrimsson said: "I couldn't say now. It is difficult to measure that one."

He added: "This is the situation, we have to cope with it. And like I said before the game, this camp is a test of character.

"We need to do better in that area than we did here today. We knew that we needed to win the duels, win the one-vs-ones, but sadly they had the upper hand on all the basics."

What it means and next fixtures

Sports.title: Why have the Republic of Ireland's two games against Israel become so controversial?
Sports.content:
The Republic of Ireland will face Israel in a men’s football fixture for the first time since 2005 in this international break, but there have been calls for the two UEFA Nations League games not to be played at all.

Both meetings - the first played in Debrecen, Hungary on Sunday and the second scheduled for the Serbian town of Backa Topola on October 4 - have been overshadowed by politics, with the Football Association of Ireland (FAI) urged to boycott the internationals amid ongoing conflict in the Israel-Gaza War.

Uncertainty over the games going ahead might have subsided, but the tensions between the two nations have not.

Heimir Hallgrimsson, the Republic of Ireland head coach, has been accused of "stupidity and hypocrisy" by the Israel Football Association after last week suggesting his team would be "playing against genocide" when facing Israel, while his players are not ruling out their own protests ahead of the games.

The Athletic examines the key issues ahead of the first meeting this weekend.

Why have these games caused controversy?

This has been a contentious issue rolling down the tracks ever since the 2026-27 Nations League draw was made in February. Group B3 saw the Republic of Ireland pitted against Kosovo, their opening opponents this evening, and Austria, but it was the prospect of facing Israel which created immediate unease.

The Football Association of Ireland (FAI) had overwhelmingly approved a motion that called on UEFA to ban Israel from its competitions just four months earlier due to violations of the governing body's statutes, including "the organisation of clubs in illegal settlements in the occupied West Bank without the consent of the Palestinian Football Association".

The Nations League draw duly reignited the row. Irish politicians, including the FAI member Joanna Byrne, were quick to call for a boycott of the Israel games in the following days and protests ensued when Qatar visited Dublin's Aviva Stadium for a friendly in May. Tennis balls featuring the Palestine flag were thrown on the pitch by supporters, twice causing brief interruptions.

Image: Tennis balls with a Palestinian flag on were thrown onto the pitch in Dublin during protests in May 2026

The FAI had already confirmed its plans to go ahead with the Israel games by then, and that decision was formally approved at an EGM in July.

That saw only 32 votes in favour of a boycott, with 75 members voting for the games to be played. The FAI had argued that boycotting games would cause "significant and lasting harm to Irish football" due to the likely disciplinary sanctions from UEFA.

A measure of the opposition to the Republic of Ireland facing Israel also came with the acceptance that the "home" fixture would not be played in Dublin. The FAI cited "operational challenges (that) could impact the delivery of the game on home soil" and the decision was eventually made in late June, with the support of UEFA, to move the game to Backa Topola, a small town in northern Serbia, on Sunday week.

No tickets for the game will be made available to Ireland fans.

The FAI has subsequently revealed that a request to see the two nations kept apart in future competition draws has been rejected by UEFA.

"The answer I got was very clear," FAI chief executive David Courell told reporters on September 18. "That would not be possible because Ireland and Israel have never been in direct conflict."

What is the political backdrop?

The Republic of Ireland has consistently outlined its backing for the Palestinian people since the conflict with Israel began almost three years ago, joining Norway and Spain when officially recognising a Palestinian state in 2024. Taoiseach Micheal Martin has also made his stance clear, accusing Israel of committing "genocide" last year in comments reported by the Irish Mirror.

The conflict in Gaza began after Israel responded to attacks by Hamas militants on October 7, 2023, which saw around 1,200 people, mostly civilians, killed in Israel and 250 taken hostage. The war has subsequently seen 73,000 people killed, according to figures from the Gaza Health Ministry and used by the UN.

Strained relations between the Republic of Ireland and Israel have continued this year. Two Israeli government ministers were the subject of travel bans in June, while foreign minister Helen McEntee also confirmed Ireland's intent to limit goods trading with settlements in the Israeli-occupied West Bank this summer.

Image: Taoiseach Micheal Martin

A meeting between the Republic of Ireland and Israel on a football field this weekend has subsequently taken on enormous significance against such a backdrop.

There are similarities in Ireland's political stance with those of Norway, who faced similar calls for a boycott when Israel travelled to Oslo last October. The Norwegian Football Federation (NFF) had aligned itself with its government and said in a statement leading up to Israel's visit that the "tragic humanitarian suffering in Gaza" had made the fixture challenging.

That World Cup qualifier, won 5-0 by Norway, saw thousands take part in a protest march to the stadium.

Who has opposed the games taking place?

Moving a home game 1,500 miles away has not stopped the objections building ahead of the two teams meeting on Sunday. More than 160 Irish sportspeople signed an open letter asking their national team to boycott the Israel games under the banner of the Irish Sport for Palestine Group, who have also run the "Stop the Game" campaign that protested outside of the Irish team hotel in Dublin on Monday.

"This is a significant moment and with this moment you have an opportunity to do the right thing," the letter said.

Kevin Kilbane, the former Republic of Ireland international who holds 110 caps, has also been unequivocal in his views. "The Republic of Ireland should not be playing Israel… not while Israeli forces are committing genocide," he wrote in a column for the Irish Times.">he wrote in a column for the Irish Times.

Amnesty International also issued a fresh statement on Tuesday that said UEFA risked letting football "rubber-stamp apartheid" by allowing Israel's continued participation in its club and international competitions. A spokesperson for the Israeli FA responded to that by saying: "Their obsession with the idea of Israel as a state is incurable, as is their need of attention."

The Irish media, meanwhile, has faced its own dilemmas in the coverage of the Israel games. RTE, the public broadcaster behind Ireland's boycott of the Eurovision Song Contest in the last two years due to Israel's continued involvement, has stripped back its coverage. Contractual obligations will be met, RTE confirmed in a statement, but there would be no studio coverage or commentators sent to either fixture.

Image: Kevin Kilbane, former Ireland international, has spoken out

What have the key stakeholders said ahead of this weekend?

Relations between the two nations have grown increasingly hostile in the last week. Hallgrimsson appeared in front of the media to announce his squad for the upcoming friendlies and made pointed remarks when asked how his players would focus on football.

"We're not playing with genocide, we're playing against genocide," the former Iceland head coach told reporters. "We're playing against Israel, we're not playing with Israel."

The reaction to those words, in a social media post from the Israel FA account, raised temperatures further still. "We have contributed to the world and humanity in countless fields, earning an impressive number of Nobel Prizes along the way," it read. "Unfortunately, we have not yet found a cure for stupidity, ignorance and hypocrisy displayed by @IrelandFootball team coach. We're not playing with ignorance, hypocrisy and stupidity, we're playing against the coach who embodies them."

Martin, who was among the world leaders attending the UN General Assembly in New York, was then drawn back into debate on Tuesday. "I think those are unacceptable remarks. They should be withdrawn. Israel can't keep denying what the world knows and what the world understands."

The FAI has not addressed Hallgrimsson's comments publicly, but the Republic of Ireland's head coach said on Wednesday that he had been "grateful for the support" he had received.

"Maybe from a leadership point of view, it was not clever from me to take the attention (away) like this. It's a tricky time for us," Hallgrimsson said in his pre-match press conference ahead of facing Kosovo.

The same extends to his players, too. Dara O'Shea, the Ipswich Town defender, said, according to the BBC, that he and the rest of the players would come together on Friday to "openly discuss" the prospect of a protest ahead of the first Israel game in Debrecen on Sunday.

Image: Dara O’Shea, left, and head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson during Wednesday’s press conference

Why are the games being played in Hungary and Serbia?

Hungary has acted as an adopted home for Israel since the start of the conflict. They first played there in November 2023, when resuming their attempts to qualify for Euro 2024 when hosting Switzerland at the Pancho Arena in Felcsut, a small village 26 miles west of Budapest.

Victor Orban, who lost his position as Hungary's prime minister this year, had been a long-standing ally of Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu and claimed Hungary to be the "safest country in Europe" for Jews.

The World Cup 2026 qualifiers against Estonia, Norway and Italy were all held in Debrecen, which has also previously hosted European games for Israeli sides Maccabi Haifa and Maccabi Tel Aviv.

The Republic of Ireland's choice of Backa Topola, Serbia, is less clear. Dublin ceased to become an option, even behind closed doors, as the opposition to Israel visiting became clear, which left limited options for relocation.

It needed to be a nation sympathetic to Israel to avoid further protests and Serbia, neighbouring Hungary to the south, has forged strong diplomatic relations. According to the Associated Press, Serbia's president Aleksandar Vucic inaugurated an assembly factory for Israel-made drones last week, with plans for three more production sites.

A switch to Serbia was reliant on UEFA approval and it will be Backa Topola's home of the TSC Arena where this story ends on October 4.

This article originally appeared in The Athletic.

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

YouTube YouTube , which may be using cookies and other technologies. To show you this content, we need your permission to use cookies. You can use the buttons below to amend your preferences to enable YouTube cookies or to allow those cookies just once.
