This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, The LatAm Brief. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

More Coverage From Election Day

Our earlier reports covered an incident at a care home and the turnout figures. The race pits President Aleksandar Vučić’s ruling Serbian Progressive Party (SNS) against a list backed by the student protest movement.

What Prediction Markets Say

On Kalshi, a US prediction market, the SNS-led list was priced at 64% to win and the student-backed list at 47% at 3:26 p.m. ET on 25 October, with 105,084 contracts traded. The two prices need not add up to 100% because each is the last trade in its own market.

Kalshi is regulated in the US by the CFTC, and its prices are last-traded bets, not polls. Why we show this: prediction markets turn real-money bets into a live probability that moves within minutes of the news, which is why investors, campaigns and newsrooms in the United States now follow them closely.

We show them next to polls and official results, never instead of them.

What It Means for You

If you follow European politics from the United States, a disputed or violent count would test how the EU and Washington respond to a Balkan state that both courts. Calm in the coming hours would make the result easier for outside governments to accept.

If you plan to travel to Serbia, expect rallies around the count in Belgrade and check your government’s travel advice. Preliminary estimates are expected after polls close, but the official result can take up to four days.

What Is Not Known

The EU statement does not say which polling stations saw violence or who was responsible. No official count of incidents or injuries was available at the time of writing.

No result is known yet, and polling-station closing figures have not been released. We will update this story when the Republic Electoral Commission publishes data.

World.title: Serbia’s Vučić Says He Would Accept Defeat
World.content:
The Government Palace in Chihuahua City, capital of the state whose former attorney general is charged, decorated for Christmas (file photo). Photo: Lyricmac, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons

Key Facts Pledge: Aleksandar Vučić, who leads the United Serbia list of the ruling Serbian Progressive Party (SNS), said he will accept defeat if voters hand him one.

Results: He expects a first estimate around 22:00 to 22:30 Central European Time, CET (5:00 to 5:30 p.m. ET).

Vote: Polling stations were due to close at 20:00 CET (3:00 p.m. ET) for 250 parliamentary seats.

Prediction markets: Kalshi, a US-regulated market, prices the SNS-led list at 57% and the list backed by the student protest movement at 49% to win (3:10 p.m. ET).

Published Sunday, 25 October, 3:10 p.m. ET · Source: N1, a Belgrade news channel, and Kurir, a Serbian daily

Aleksandar Vučić, who leads the United Serbia list of the ruling Serbian Progressive Party (SNS), said on Sunday he will accept defeat if voters reject him. N1 and Kurir report that he expects a first estimate around 22:00 to 22:30 CET (5:00 to 5:30 p.m. ET).

He spoke to reporters after voting in Belgrade in the early parliamentary election. We covered the build-up in our Sunday preview, the campaign ban before the vote, the 6.45 million voter register and the final opinion polls.

Vučić Promises to Accept the Result

N1 and Kurir, a Serbian daily, quoted him as saying: “You can win or lose elections.” He added that if his list loses, it will recognise the voters’ will, and if it wins, nobody will take the win away.

N1 reported that he waited about two hours in the queue at a polling station in New Belgrade, a district of the capital and voted with his wife. He also said Serbia is choosing between a future and a past of what he called looting privatisations and economic ruin.

Asked by foreign journalists, he said he would not be “the leader of the opposition.” He then said it would be clear that evening whether he is in opposition or in power.

File photo: Serbian flags at a night protest in central Belgrade.

First Estimate Expected Tonight

Vučić told reporters that voters should wait, and that he expects a preliminary estimate around 22:00 to 22:30 CET, according to N1 and Kurir. N1 quoted him as saying the estimate will be accurate whatever the outcome.

Kurir reported that he expects high turnout. Our latest turnout report has the figures from the monitoring group CeSID and the polling firm Ipsos.

What Prediction Markets Say

On Kalshi, the SNS-led list was priced at 57% to win and the student-protest list at 49% at 3:10 p.m. ET, with 101,875 contracts traded. On Polymarket, a global prediction market, the contract on Vučić’s United Serbia list to win the election priced at 53%, with US$8.48 million traded.

Kalshi is regulated in the US by the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC), and all of these prices are bets, not polls. The contracts are priced separately, so they need not add to 100%.

Why we show this: prediction markets turn real-money bets into a live probability that moves within minutes of the news, which is why investors, campaigns and newsrooms in the United States now follow them closely. We show them next to polls and official results, never instead of them.

What It Means for You

For readers in the United States, a leader who publicly commits to accepting a loss lowers the risk of a disputed result. The first estimate, due in about two hours, will show whether that pledge is tested.

If you plan to travel to Serbia, check your government’s travel advice before you go.

What Is Not Known

No result or projection has been published, and the winner and the size of any majority are unknown. The timing of the first estimate is Vučić’s expectation, not an official schedule, and other outlets have reported a slightly later window.

It is also unclear whether the student-protest list and other opposition parties will accept the first figures. The Republic Electoral Commission (RIK), the state body that runs the vote, has not yet released counts.

Sources

N1 · Kurir · Republic Electoral Commission of Serbia · Kalshi · Polymarket

Frequently Asked Questions

Will Vučić accept defeat in Serbia’s election?

After voting in Belgrade, he said that if his list loses he will recognise the voters’ will. He added that if it wins, nobody will take the victory away.

When will Serbia’s first election estimate come?

According to N1 and Kurir, Vučić expects a preliminary estimate around 22:00 to 22:30 CET, which is 5:00 to 5:30 p.m. ET. Official counts from the Republic Electoral Commission (RIK) follow.

Who is Aleksandar Vučić?

He heads the United Serbia list in the parliamentary vote and is a member of the Serbian Progressive Party (SNS).

What do prediction markets say about the vote?

At 3:06 p.m. ET, Kalshi priced the SNS-led list at 57% and the student-protest list at 49% to win. These are bets, not polls.

World.title: Brazil Replaces 900 Voting Machines by Noon
World.content:
Soybean plants in a field at Novo Barreiro, Rio Grande do Sul, photographed in the evening of 18 December 2018 (cropped). File photo; it does not show the 2026/27 crop. Photo: Lucas Friederich, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

BRAZIL · ELECTIONS

Published Sunday, 25 October, 3:03 p.m. ET · Source: Superior Electoral Court (TSE) bulletin

Key Facts What happened The Superior Electoral Court (TSE), Brazil’s election authority, replaced 900 electronic voting machines by noon Brasília time (11 a.m. ET) on runoff day.

The numbers That is 0.18% of 499,248 machines in use, and the court logged 138 incidents.

Paper ballots No polling section had to switch to paper, said Kassio Nunes Marques, the TSE president.

Power Index Brazil ranks 1st of 14 in Brazil ranks 1st of 14 in The Rio Times Latin America Power Index , with 75.0 points (October 2026 edition).

Prediction markets Kalshi, a US prediction market regulated by the CFTC (Commodity Futures Trading Commission), prices a Flávio Bolsonaro win by 1 point or more of valid votes at 75% and a Lula win by 1 point or more at 17% (3:01 p.m. ET, 25 October). Polymarket puts Flávio Bolsonaro’s chance of winning at 78% and Kalshi at 78% (Lula: 23% and 22% ), as of 25 October, 3:00 pm ET ; prices are bets, not polls.

Still open The court has not said what caused the replacements or how many follow after noon.

The Superior Electoral Court (TSE), Brazil’s election authority, replaced 900 voting machines by noon on Sunday 25 October, 0.18% of the 499,248 in use, according to a TSE bulletin reported by Agência Senado, the Brazilian Senate’s news service. The court also logged 138 incidents during the first hours of the Brazil election 2026 runoff.

Brazil Election Data Room Runoff poll average: Flávio Bolsonaro 51.0 %, Lula 49.0 % 45 national polls from 21 pollsters since 4 October, updated hourly. Every poll, free to download. Open the Data Room · Download the CSV · Embed the chart

Voters choose between President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and Flávio Bolsonaro, senator for Rio de Janeiro and son of former president Jair Bolsonaro. Polls close at 5 p.m. Brasília time (4 p.m. ET), and the TSE president expects results between 8:30 and 9 p.m. Brasília time (7:30 and 8 p.m. ET).

What the Court Reported by Noon

The TSE said 900 machines were swapped out, and 48,815 spare machines are held in reserve, according to Brasil de Fato, a Brazilian news outlet. The court said no polling section needed manual voting.

How This Compares With the Morning

Agência Brasil, the state news agency, said 467 machines had been replaced in the first two hours of voting. The figure then reached 900 by noon Brasília time.

The court did not publish a reason for each replacement. It put the total at 0.18% of machines in use.

What Prediction Markets Say

On Kalshi, a US prediction market regulated by the CFTC, traders price Flávio Bolsonaro winning by at least 1 point of valid votes at 75% and Lula winning by at least 1 point at 17% (3:01 p.m. ET, 25 October). These are bets, not polls.

Why we show this: prediction markets turn real-money bets into a live probability that moves within minutes of the news, which is why investors, campaigns and newsrooms in the United States now follow them closely. We show them next to polls and official results, never instead of them.

What It Means for US Readers

A low replacement rate and no paper-ballot fallbacks point to a smooth vote, which matters to investors holding Brazilian bonds, stocks or US-listed shares of Brazilian companies. Disputes over how the count is run would be a bigger market risk than a few hundred swapped machines.

Results will be announced by the TSE tonight, and our Brazil runoff date and results guide shows where to follow them. Official figures come only from the TSE.

What Is Not Known

The court has not said why the machines were replaced, or how many more were swapped in the afternoon. The TSE publishes updated bulletins through the day, and the final count is not yet available.

Reports of vote buying and secrecy attempts are incident counts, not findings of crime. The court has not said how many will lead to charges.

Frequently Asked Questions

How many voting machines were replaced in Brazil’s runoff?

The TSE said 900 machines were replaced by noon Brasília time on Sunday 25 October. That is 0.18% of the 499,248 machines in use.

What incidents did the TSE report on runoff day?

The court logged 138 incidents by noon, including 40 attempts to violate the secrecy of the vote and three cases of vote buying. It is not yet known how many will lead to charges.

Did any Brazilian polling station use paper ballots?

No. TSE president Kassio Nunes Marques said no polling section needed to vote on paper.

When will Brazil announce the runoff result?

The TSE president expects the result between 8:30 and 9 p.m. Brasília time, which is 7:30 to 8 p.m. ET on Sunday 25 October.

World.title: Brazil Court Chief Admits Voter Bus Gaps
World.content:
Supreme Court Justice Cármen Lúcia. File photo. (Photo: Fernando Frazão, Agência Brasil, CC BY 3.0 BR, via Wikimedia Commons)

BRAZIL · ELECTIONS

Published Sunday, 25 October, 2:35 p.m. ET · Source: Folha de S.Paulo, Jovem Pan, O Tempo

Key Facts What happened Kassio Nunes Marques, president of Brazil’s Superior Electoral Court (TSE), admitted on Sunday that voter transport is struggling in some places.

Where Bahia, a north-eastern state, is the focus, with bus cuts reported in Salvador, Feira de Santana and Lauro de Freitas.

His words “In some places there is still a difficulty with transport, which is already being corrected.”

Court order The Bahia regional electoral court set a fine of R$1 million (about US$200,000) per hour until the full bus fleet returns.

Power Index Brazil ranks 1st of 14 in Brazil ranks 1st of 14 in The Rio Times Latin America Power Index , with 75.0 points (October 2026 edition).

Prediction markets Polymarket puts Flávio Bolsonaro’s chance of winning at 79% and Kalshi at 80% (Lula: 22% and 21% ), as of 25 October, 3:20 pm ET ; prices are bets, not polls.

Still open Whether voting hours in Salvador will be extended; Nunes Marques did not answer.

Prediction markets · who wins the runoff Implied chance of winning Brazil’s presidency on 25 October, from traders’ prices. Polymarket Flávio Bolsonaro 78.5% · Lula 21.5% (US$199 million traded) Kalshi (regulated in the US by the CFTC) Flávio Bolsonaro 80% · Lula 21% As of 25 October, 3:20 pm ET (19:20 Lisbon), updated every 20 minutes. Prices are bets, not polls, and can move fast. Why we show this: prediction markets turn real-money bets into a live probability that moves within minutes of the news, which is why investors, campaigns and newsrooms in the United States now follow them closely. We show them next to polls and official results, never instead of them. Want prediction market reports on Brazil? Get yours free, right after you confirm →

Brazil’s top electoral judge admitted on Sunday 25 October that some voters are struggling to reach polling stations during the Brazil election 2026. Kassio Nunes Marques, president of the electoral court (TSE), said the problem was “already being corrected”, Folha de S.Paulo, a leading Brazilian daily, reported at 2:35 p.m. ET.

The sharpest complaints come from Bahia, a north-eastern state where voters report missing buses. For readers in the US, the story matters because turnout in Bahia, a stronghold of President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, could shape a result that moves Brazilian markets and Washington’s relations with Brasília; see the Brazil election odds for current prices.

What the Electoral Court President Said

Nunes Marques spoke to reporters at the TSE headquarters in Brasília on Sunday. He said transport programmes are run by the regional electoral courts (TREs) and are “going very well” in general, Folha reported.

Latin America Power Index · October 2026 edition Brazil ranks 1st of 14 with 75.0 points. Strongest pillar: military means (100); weakest: state capacity & security (56). Alignment group: Hedging. WatchRating below investment grade (BB); public debt at 93% of GDP. See the full index, the business lens and the data →

Asked about Bahia, he said the TSE receives periodic reports from the state court and that “any and all action will be analysed in due time”. Asked by O Tempo about extending voting hours, he replied that the law decides who is competent to oversee voter transport.

He also pointed to “Seu Voto Importa” (Your Vote Matters), a TSE programme that offers free transport to people with disabilities, quilombola communities (descendants of escaped slaves), Indigenous people and riverside communities.

Bus Cuts in Salvador, Bahia

Ricardo Villas Bôas Cueva, the TSE’s inspector-general of electoral justice, ordered the Bahia court to report on alleged bus cuts in Salvador, Feira de Santana and Lauro de Freitas. Jovem Pan, a Brazilian broadcaster, reported that a complaint from Lula’s Brasil da Esperança federation (his Workers’ Party and two smaller allies) alleged a reduction of more than 50% in bus supply in the capital, Salvador.

The president of the Bahia electoral court (TRE-BA), Judge Mauricio Kertzman Szporer, ordered the Federal Police, Brazil’s national law-enforcement agency, to arrest Salvador’s mobility secretary, Pablo Souza, Jovem Pan reported. He also ordered the full fleet back on the road, with a fine of R$1 million (about US$200,000, at 4.97 reais per dollar) per hour for non-compliance.

Reports differ on how many buses were held in garages: Jovem Pan counted 217 in two garages, while O Tempo, a newspaper from Minas Gerais state, reported about 375. Salvador City Hall said Souza is in Paris on an official mission and will present himself to police on Monday 26 October, Jovem Pan reported.

Lula Campaign Seeks More Voting Time

O Tempo reported that the Brasil da Esperança federation asked for voting to run until 7 p.m. local time (6 p.m. ET) in the three affected cities. Polls normally close at 5 p.m. in Brasília time (4 p.m. ET), and our earlier report on the Lula campaign request has the background.

No ruling on that request had been published at the time of writing. Nunes Marques declined to say whether the TSE would extend voting hours.

What It Means for US Readers

A court-ordered fleet restoration shows Brazil’s institutions acting on election day, which supports confidence in the count. A disputed result or a challenge over turnout in Bahia would be a different matter, and investors in Brazilian stocks and the real would price that risk.

Follow our Brazil elections coverage page for official TSE results from 5 p.m. local time. Official numbers, not prediction-market prices, decide the winner.

What Is Not Known

It is not known whether voting hours will be extended in Salvador, or whether the arrest order will be carried out. The number of voters who could not reach their polling station has not been published by the TSE.

Reports also differ on the number of buses held. We will update this report when the electoral courts publish figures.

Frequently Asked Questions

What did Brazil’s electoral court president say about transport?

Kassio Nunes Marques said on Sunday 25 October that some places still have transport difficulties that are being corrected. He said the programme is going well overall.

Where are voters struggling to reach polling stations?

Reports centre on Salvador, Feira de Santana and Lauro de Freitas in Bahia state. The TSE asked the Bahia electoral court for a report.

What did the Bahia electoral court order?

Its president ordered the full bus fleet back and set a fine of R$1 million (about US$200,000) per hour. He also ordered the arrest of Salvador’s mobility secretary, according to Jovem Pan.

Will voting hours in Salvador be extended?

Not decided as of 2:35 p.m. ET. Lula’s federation asked for voting until 7 p.m. local time, and Nunes Marques did not answer the question.

When do polls close in Brazil?

Polls close at 5 p.m. in Brasília time on Sunday 25 October, which is 4 p.m. ET. Results follow that evening.

Sources: Folha de S.Paulo, 25 October 2026; Jovem Pan, 25 October 2026; O Tempo, 25 October 2026.

World.title: France Arrests 1,314 at Latest Protests
World.content:
File photo: the Élysée Palace in Paris, the French president's official residence. (Photo: ScareCriterion12, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons)

Key Facts Arrests: 1,314 people were arrested across France on Saturday, 24 October, in a provisional Interior Ministry count.

Injured: 53 police and gendarmes were hurt, and police responded to 75 fires and 24 looted shops.

Turnout: The ministry counted 410,000 marchers, including 110,000 in Paris, while organisers claimed about 800,000.

Next dates: Yellow Vest groups, a protest movement born in 2018, plan rallies on Saturday, 31 October.

Strike: The CGT, a major French trade union, has called a general strike for Thursday, 5 November.

Prediction markets: Kalshi, a US exchange regulated by the CFTC, prices a 19% chance of a French state of emergency before 1 January 2027 (as of 25 October, 2:22 p.m. ET).

This story is part of our coverage of the why France is in crisis. Dates, times and how to follow it are in our guide. Latest: Paris Police Detain 142 After Protest Day

France arrested 1,314 people at cost-of-living protests on Saturday, 24 October, the Interior Ministry said on Sunday morning. That is about half the roughly 2,600 arrests counted for 17 October, and our guide to why France is in crisis explains how the unrest began.

For US readers, the figures matter because France is the eurozone’s second-largest economy and a NATO ally. Paris is five hours ahead of New York until 1 November, then six.

Provisional Toll of the Weekend

The ministry’s provisional tally recorded 53 injured police and gendarmes (France’s paramilitary police), 75 fires and 24 looted shops. It said the rest of Saturday night was calm after the clashes subsided, and that several investigations have been opened.

Protesters were hurt too: reports describe a 20-year-old in Toulouse who was gravely injured in the hand, and a second serious injury in Clermont-Ferrand. No full national count of injured protesters has been published.

Follow this story Get an email when there’s news on France in Turmoil Email address Follow Free. One email a day at most, and only when there is news. This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, The LatAm Brief. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

How Big Were the Marches

The Interior Ministry counted 410,000 people at demonstrations across the country on 24 October, including 110,000 in Paris. Organisers claimed about 800,000 nationwide and 250,000 in Paris.

A week earlier, on 17 October, the ministry had counted about 550,000 marchers at 441 events, against 289 events this time. Organisers claimed around 800,000 on both days.

The protests are about the cost of living and fuel prices. Students, workers, Yellow Vest activists and other groups have joined the marches.

File photo: protesters hold cardboard placards at a Paris march on 17 October 2026.

What Comes Next

Yellow Vest groups, a street movement that began in 2018 over fuel taxes and living costs, have announced rallies for Saturday, 31 October. They had framed 24 and 31 October as stages before a wider push on 5 November.

On 21 October, after a meeting with French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu, Sophie Binet, head of the CGT union, called for a general strike on Thursday, 5 November. The CFDT, France’s largest union, also backed 5 November as a day of mobilisation, though the seven unions at the meeting reacted differently.

The next presidential election is due in April and May, after President Emmanuel Macron reaches his two-term limit. That puts pressure on every party to be seen responding to the street.

What Prediction Markets Say

Kalshi, a US exchange regulated by the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC): “Will France declare a state of emergency?”

Before 1 January 2027: 19%. Before 1 November 2026: 6%.

Volume: 82,503 contracts traded, as of 25 October 2026, 2:22 p.m. ET (7:22 p.m. Paris).

These prices are real-money bets, not polls. Why we show this: prediction markets turn real-money bets into a live probability that moves within minutes of the news, which is why investors, campaigns and newsrooms in the United States now follow them closely.

We show them next to polls and official results, never instead of them.

What It Means for You

Travellers to France in the coming fortnight should expect disruption on 31 October and 5 November, including possible strike disruption and heavy police presence in city centres. Check airline and rail notices before booking, and avoid the main march routes in Paris, Lyon and other large cities.

Investors should note that a prolonged strike would weigh on French activity, while traders so far price a state of emergency as unlikely in the short term. The cost-of-living anger behind the marches has parallels in the United States.

What Is Not Known

The arrest figure is provisional and may change as investigations continue. The turnout total is disputed, and no official count of injured protesters has been released.

It is not yet clear how many of the other unions will join the 5 November strike or how many people will take part in the 31 October rallies.

Frequently Asked Questions

How many people were arrested in the latest French protests?

France’s Interior Ministry reported a provisional 1,314 arrests at 7:30 a.m. Paris time on Sunday, 25 October, for the Saturday demonstrations. The final count for 17 October was about 2,600.

What are the next planned protest dates in France?

Yellow Vest groups plan rallies on Saturday, 31 October. The CGT union has called a general strike for Thursday, 5 November.

Why are people protesting in France?

The marches are about the cost of living and fuel prices. Students, workers and Yellow Vest activists have joined them.

Will France declare a state of emergency?

Traders on Kalshi, a US exchange regulated by the CFTC, put the chance at 19% before 1 January 2027 and 6% before 1 November 2026, as of 25 October. These are bets, not official forecasts.

World.title: Serbia Turnout Passes 60%, Far Above 2023
World.content:
The House of the National Assembly in Belgrade. File photo. (Photo: Kallerna, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons)

Key Facts Turnout: An estimated 60.9% of registered voters had voted by 17:00 Central European Time, CET (noon Eastern Time, ET).

Pace: At the same hour in December 2023 it was 47.2%, so this vote runs 13.7 points ahead.

Polling stations: Close at 20:00 CET (3:00 p.m. ET) for 250 parliamentary seats.

Irregularities: 260 reports of possible irregularities had been logged by 17:00 CET.

Prediction markets: Kalshi, a US-regulated market, prices President Aleksandar Vučić’s party list at 55% and the student-protest list at 48% to win (2:00 p.m. ET).

Published Sunday, 25 October, 2:00 p.m. ET · Source: CeSID, a Belgrade election-monitoring group, with Ipsos, a polling firm

More than 60% of Serbia’s registered voters had cast a ballot by 17:00 CET (noon ET) in Sunday’s early parliamentary election. CeSID, the Centre for Free Elections and Democracy, and Ipsos, a polling company, estimated turnout at 60.9% from a sample of 750 polling stations.

That is 13.7 points above the same hour in December 2023. We covered the build-up in our Saturday preview, the campaign ban before the vote, the 6.45 million voter register and the final opinion polls.

Turnout Runs Far Above 2023

CeSID said turnout at 17:00 CET in 2023 was 47.2%, according to N1, a Serbian news channel. Its estimate for 14:00 CET today was 46.4%, so turnout rose by about 14.5 points in three hours.

The Republic Electoral Commission (RIK), the state body that runs the vote, put turnout at 56.38% at 16:00 CET, against 42.36% in 2023. The CeSID figure is an estimate from a sample, not a count of every polling station.

File photo: Serbian flags at a night protest in central Belgrade.

This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, The LatAm Brief. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

Reports of Irregularities Pile Up

CeSID recorded 260 reports of possible irregularities by 17:00 CET, according to Danas, a Belgrade daily, and N1. It is not clear how many of the reports will be confirmed.

Danas and N1 also reported incidents at polling stations across the country, and RIK’s chairman described a care home incident in Mladenovac, a town near Belgrade. We have not confirmed the overall scale independently.

What Prediction Markets Say

On Kalshi, the list of the Serbian Progressive Party (SNS), President Aleksandar Vučić’s party, was priced at 55% to win, and the student-protest list at 48%, at 2:00 p.m. ET. The two contracts are priced separately, so they need not add to 100%, and 99,057 contracts had traded.

On Polymarket, a global prediction market, a turnout contract with US$152,179 traded priced a final turnout of 70% or more at 73% and 66% to 70% at 26%, at 2:00 p.m. ET. Kalshi is regulated in the US by the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC), and all of these prices are bets, not polls.

Why we show this: prediction markets turn real-money bets into a live probability that moves within minutes of the news, which is why investors, campaigns and newsrooms in the United States now follow them closely. We show them next to polls and official results, never instead of them.

What It Means for You

For readers in the United States, high turnout makes the outcome harder to call, and it shows how many Serbians want to be heard in a vote that tests President Vučić’s long hold on power.

If you plan to travel to Serbia, check your government’s travel advice, because incidents were reported at polling stations today.

What Is Not Known

No result or projection is available, and the winner and the size of any majority are unknown. Danas reported that CeSID and Ipsos expect first projections between 21:30 and 22:00 CET (4:30 to 5:00 p.m. ET).

The number of confirmed irregularities is unclear. The final turnout is not yet known.

Sources

N1 · Danas · Tanjug, Serbia’s state news agency · Nova.rs, a Belgrade news site · Republic Electoral Commission of Serbia · Kalshi · Polymarket

What was Serbia’s turnout at 5 p.m. CET?

How does turnout compare with 2023?

At 17:00 CET in December 2023, turnout was 47.2%, so this vote is 13.7 points ahead at the same hour.

When do polling stations close in Serbia?

Who is CeSID?

World.title: Brazilians Abroad Split in Runoff Count
World.content:
Voters queue at the Colégio Leonardo da Vinci polling station in Brasília during Brazil's first round on 4 October 2026. Photo: Lula Marques/Agência Brasil

Published Sunday, 25 October 2026, 1:58 p.m. ET · Unofficial press tallies of ballot-box reports

Brazilians living abroad voted first in Sunday’s presidential runoff, and their early count is split: Flávio Bolsonaro leads the overseas total, while Lula leads in more countries. These are press tallies, not official results, and the electoral court publishes its first numbers from 4 p.m. ET.

Key Facts — Who Brazilians abroad voted first in the runoff between Lula, Brazil’s president, and Flávio Bolsonaro, a senator.

— Count At 1:42 p.m. ET the early overseas tally gave Flávio Bolsonaro 45,720 votes to Lula’s 41,101 (52.7%), while Lula led in 30 places to 12.

— Why Japan supplies 62% of Flávio’s votes; without it, Lula would lead the overseas count.

— Electorate 918,876 registered voters abroad, about 0.6% of the total, 265,437 of them in the United States.

— Official numbers The electoral court (TSE) publishes results from 4 p.m. ET; the last US and Canadian polls close at 8 p.m. ET.

— Prediction markets Polymarket puts Flávio Bolsonaro’s chance of winning at 82% and Kalshi at 81% (Lula: 19% and 20% ), as of 25 October, 2:20 pm ET ; prices are bets, not polls.

— Power Index Brazil ranks 1st of 14 in Brazil ranks 1st of 14 in The Rio Times Latin America Power Index , with 75.0 points (October 2026 edition).

Live results Brazil Election Data Room Runoff poll average: Flávio Bolsonaro 51.0 %, Lula 49.0 % 45 national polls from 21 pollsters since 4 October, updated hourly. Every poll, free to download. Open the Data Room · Download the CSV · Embed the chart Follow Brazil’s runoff count on our results page Official TSE numbers, state by state, as soon as the electoral court publishes them from 4 p.m. ET. Open the live results page →

Exame, a Brazilian business magazine, adds up the ballot-box reports posted from 42 places abroad. Its running count at 1:42 p.m. ET gave Flávio Bolsonaro, the conservative senator for Rio de Janeiro, 45,720 votes (52.66% of valid votes, which exclude blank and spoiled ballots) and Lula, the left-wing president, 41,101 (47.34%).

The overseas vote is a tiny slice of the runoff results guide explains when and where official numbers arrive.

Latin America Power Index · October 2026 edition Brazil ranks 1st of 14 with 75.0 points. Strongest pillar: military means (100); weakest: state capacity & security (56). Alignment group: Hedging. WatchRating below investment grade (BB); public debt at 93% of GDP. See the full index, the business lens and the data →

In Plain English Runoff: the second round between the top two candidates, held because nobody won more than half of the valid votes on 4 October.

the second round between the top two candidates, held because nobody won more than half of the valid votes on 4 October. Ballot-box report: the results sheet each voting machine prints when its polls close, which news sites add up before any official count.

the results sheet each voting machine prints when its polls close, which news sites add up before any official count. TSE: the Superior Electoral Court, Brazil’s election authority, which publishes the official results.

Where Brazilians Voted First

Voting abroad runs from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. local time, so Asia and Oceania finish first and Europe follows hours later. Brazilians in the United States and Canada vote last: the final polls in San Francisco, Los Angeles and Vancouver close at 9 p.m. in Brasília, which is 8 p.m. ET.

The Superior Electoral Court (TSE), Brazil’s election authority, counts 918,876 registered voters abroad in 186 cities. The United States is the largest bloc with 265,437 (28.9%), followed by Portugal (134,797), Japan (88,366), Canada (46,488) and Germany (41,551).

What the Early Polling-Station Tallies Show

Japan decides the early sum. Metrópoles, a Brasília news site, counts 28,538 votes for Flávio Bolsonaro and 7,098 for Lula there (80.08% to 19.92%), from ballot-box reports posted in Japan.

Japan’s 28,538 votes make up 62% of everything Flávio Bolsonaro has collected abroad so far, Exame calculates. Without Japan, Exame says, Lula would lead the overseas count.

A Brazilian electronic voting machine of the kind used at polling stations. File photo, not from a polling station abroad.

Exame reports Lula ahead in 30 places and Flávio Bolsonaro in 12. Metrópoles reports Flávio ahead in Taiwan, Malaysia and the Philippines, and Lula ahead in Australia and China; Exame adds Lula ahead in Singapore. Terra also lists Flávio ahead in Israel, Indonesia and South Africa.

In Europe, Exame lists Lula ahead in the Netherlands, Switzerland, Poland, the Czech Republic and Finland. Terra, a Brazilian news portal, gives him 85.06% in Denmark and 78.26% in Sweden, while Flávio Bolsonaro won Greece with 311 votes to 255 (54.95%).

The gap has narrowed as more places reported. Metrópoles’ count at 1:29 p.m. ET, covering 37 countries, gave Flávio Bolsonaro 58.43% of 66,131 valid votes; Exame’s count 13 minutes later, with 86,821 valid votes, gave him 52.66%. Exame also says Malaysia, which Lula won on 4 October, went to Flávio this time.

We could not find reported counts for Portugal, the second-largest overseas bloc, or for the United Kingdom. Germany and France were only partly counted in the tallies we saw.

Why Overseas Votes Are Not a Forecast

Brazilians abroad are about 0.6% of the roughly 158.7 million voters, so even a lopsided overseas result moves the national total very little. The count is also lumpy: one country, Japan, outweighs dozens of smaller ones, and each country leans differently.

World.title: Serbia Probes Care Home Incident at Polls
World.content:
Key Facts Care home: Unknown people entered a polling station inside a care home in Mladenovac, a town near Belgrade.

Who says: Vladimir Dimitrijević chairs the Republic Electoral Commission (RIK), Serbia’s election authority.

Claim: He said the intruders posed as observers and pressured residents who cannot move around.

Second case: Prosecutors in Sombor, a northern city, are probing a laptop and documents found in Deronje.

Prediction markets: Kalshi, a US-regulated market, prices President Vučić’s ruling Progressive Party (SNS) list 54%, the protest-born student list 48% (1:43 p.m. ET).

Serbia’s election authority said on Sunday that unknown people burst into a care home that doubles as a polling station in Mladenovac, a town near Belgrade. The Republic Electoral Commission (RIK) chair said they claimed to be observers and pressured residents who cannot move around.

Polls in the snap parliamentary election close at 20:00 CET (Central European Time; 3:00 p.m. ET). Follow every development in our Serbia Election 2026 coverage, and see our earlier turnout report.

RIK Chair Describes Care Home Intrusion

RIK chair Vladimir Dimitrijević told a press conference at 17:00 CET (12:00 p.m. ET) that “unknown persons” entered the care home, claiming to be observers. He said they exerted “impermissible pressure” on residents, including people who cannot move.

Police were alerted and were at the scene, he said, and he promised more information at the next RIK press conference. He said it happened just before the briefing, so he had no further detail.

Dimitrijević said voting was otherwise proceeding regularly, based on reports from local election commissions and polling boards. He described the other problems as minor and said polling boards resolved them, with the Interior Ministry (MUP) stepping in where they could not.

File photo: Serbian police on a Belgrade square.

This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, The LatAm Brief. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

Prosecutors Probe Laptop and Documents

The Basic Public Prosecutor’s Office in Sombor, a city in northern Serbia, said a laptop and several A4 documents were found in a hospitality venue in Deronje, a village in the north of the country. It said they are suspected of being linked to the election process and were handed to police in Odžaci, a town in northern Serbia.

Prosecutors told police to gather information without delay and to file a report so they can decide on further steps in the early preliminary stage. The office has not said what the documents contain or who left them.

In a separate statement, Sombor prosecutors said that shortly before 15:00 CET they received two electronic messages from the Higher Public Prosecutor’s Office, a more senior body, in Novi Sad, Serbia’s second-largest city. The messages passed on citizens’ reports of alleged irregularities at polling stations on two streets in Sombor and in Apatin, a town near Sombor.

Checks found that no polling stations exist at those addresses, and neither do the local communities named in the reports. Prosecutors also said there were no irregularities at the polling stations with the reported numbers, 39 and 13.

What Prediction Markets Say

On Kalshi, the SNS-led list, President Aleksandar Vučić’s ruling Serbian Progressive Party, was priced at 54% to win the parliamentary election and the student-backed Student List at 48%, at 1:43 p.m. ET on 25 October. The market had 97,961 contracts traded; the two prices do not add to 100% because each is a separate last-traded bet.

Our earlier Sunday report had the SNS-led list at 75% and the Student List at 26% at 4:27 a.m. ET. Kalshi is regulated in the US by the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC), and its prices are bets, not polls.

Why we show this: prediction markets turn real-money bets into a live probability that moves within minutes of the news, which is why investors, campaigns and newsrooms in the United States now follow them closely. We show them next to polls and official results, never instead of them.

Why Election-Day Pressure Claims Matter

The vote is mainly a contest between Vučić’s ruling camp and the student-backed Student List, born of nearly two years of protests, as our election-day report explained. Both sides have claimed to be ahead, and the integrity of the vote is a central issue, as our Saturday report noted.

The Mladenovac claim concerns residents who cannot move around, and police have not yet reported what they found. The Sombor checks, by contrast, found no irregularities at the two reported polling stations.

What It Means for You

If you follow European politics from the United States, these cases show how contested the integrity of Serbia’s vote already is before any result. Allegations on election day often shape how voters, observers and foreign governments judge the outcome.

If you are travelling to Serbia, expect heavy attention around the count in Belgrade and check your government’s travel advice. See also our report on the vote-silence period.

What Is Not Known

Dimitrijević did not say who the intruders were, which group they claimed to represent or whether anyone has been detained. The RIK chair gave no estimate of how many residents were affected.

Prosecutors have not said whether the Deronje laptop and documents relate to any party or list. It is unclear whether the two cases are connected, and no result or official turnout figure is part of this report.

What happened at the polling station in Mladenovac?

World.title: 1am motorcycle stop ends with three traffic charges and $800 bail
World.content:
1am motorcycle stop ends with three traffic charges and $800 bail

By Breaking Belize News Staff (HP): A late night ride through Orange Walk Town ended with a young man facing three traffic charges.

Officers on patrol early Saturday morning stopped a motorcycle carrying two men on Naranjal Street. The rider told police his licence was at home.

But when officers took him there to check, they found that his driver’s licence had expired more than a year ago, in September 2025. The motorcycle’s licence was also out of date, and its insurance disc had expired at the start of September.

Dathan Raasaun Smith, 24, a labourer of Savannah Street, was taken to the Orange Walk Police Station and formally charged around 2:30am.

The charges are driving an unlicensed motor vehicle, driving without third party risk insurance and driving without a valid driver’s licence.

He was released on $800 police bail.

Police are urging motorists and riders to keep their driver’s licences, vehicle licences and insurance up to date, warning that patrols are continuing day and night.

World.title: No licence, no insurance, no vehicle sticker: Douglas Village rider charged
World.content:
No licence, no insurance, no vehicle sticker: Douglas Village rider charged

By Breaking Belize News Staff (HP): A 19 year old domestic of Douglas Village, Orange Walk District, has been charged with traffic offences.

She is Irainy Yoanie Marin.

Police say that around 8:15am on Friday, October 23, officers on mobile patrol on Douglas Road stopped a black Meilun motorcycle travelling from San Juan Village toward the Philip Goldson Highway.

Marin, the rider, was asked for her driver’s licence but could not produce it. Officers also found no insurance disc or licence sticker on the motorcycle, and she allegedly said she did not have valid insurance or a motor vehicle licence.

She was taken to the Trial Farm Police Sub Station, and the motorcycle was impounded.

Marin was charged with failing to produce a driving permit, using a motor vehicle not covered by third party risk insurance and using an unlicensed motor vehicle. She chose to remain silent when cautioned.

World.title: Belize enjoys another pleasant Sunday with sunshine and little rain
World.content:
Belize enjoys another pleasant Sunday with sunshine and little rain

By Breaking Belize News Staff (HP): Belize can expect another pleasant day, with mainly fair and mild conditions continuing.

The National Meteorological Service says skies will be sunny with a few cloudy spells today and partly cloudy tonight.

Showers will be isolated, though a few more are possible offshore and over some coastal areas tonight.

Temperatures remain comfortable, with cool nights. Coastal areas will reach 86°F (30°C), with a low of 75°F (24°C). Inland areas will climb to 90°F (32°C), cooling to 68°F (20°C) overnight. The hills will see a high of 78°F (26°C) and a low of 64°F (18°C).

At sea, winds are from the north at 5 to 15 knots, with slight to light chop and waves of 1 to 4 feet.

Similar weather is expected Monday and Monday night.

Tropical cyclone formation is not expected over the region in the next 48 hours.

Today’s forecast was issued by forecaster Derrick Rudon.

World.title: Haiti gang crisis raises security concerns for Belize and Caribbean nations
World.content:
Haiti gang crisis raises security concerns for Belize and Caribbean nations

By Breaking Belize News Staff (HP): The escalating gang crisis in Haiti is raising serious security concerns across the Caribbean, including Belize, as a multinational force struggles to restore stability in the troubled CARICOM nation.

The latest concerns follow an ambush involving Salvadoran soldiers serving in Haiti, with four soldiers reported missing following the attack.

The incident marks the first major assault on the Gang Suppression Force, a United Nations authorized multinational security mission tasked with confronting heavily armed criminal gangs.

According to Reuters, the mission has approximately 2,000 personnel deployed, significantly below its authorized strength of 5,500.

The force replaced an earlier Kenyan led security mission that struggled with shortages of funding, equipment and personnel.

Belize was among the Caribbean countries that offered support to the earlier international security effort.

Haiti’s deteriorating security situation has become a regional concern because of its potential implications for migration, organized crime and the movement of illegal weapons throughout the Caribbean.

Since the assassination of President Jovenel Moïse in 2021, armed gangs have expanded their control over large sections of Port au Prince, forcing an estimated 1.4 million to 1.5 million people from their homes.

The crisis comes as Belize examines its own security challenges involving transnational criminal organizations.

Prime Minister John Briceño recently confirmed that Belize is holding preliminary discussions with the United States about possible cooperation under the Shield of the Americas initiative, which focuses on combating drug cartels and organized crime.

While the situations in Belize and Haiti are different, the developments highlight the growing importance of regional security cooperation.

Attention remains focused on the search for the four missing Salvadoran soldiers as the multinational mission faces another major challenge.

World.title: Halo BPO hiring Belizeans for work from home jobs paying up to $10 an hour
World.content:
Halo BPO hiring Belizeans for work from home jobs paying up to $10 an hour

By Breaking Belize News Staff (HP): Belizeans looking for an opportunity to work from home still have time to apply for full time employment with Halo BPO.

The company is continuing to recruit outbound sales agents, offering starting pay of $8.50 Belize dollars per hour, increasing to $9.00 after two weeks and $10.00 after 30 days.

Employees will receive weekly payments and work daytime hours from 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., Belize time.

Halo BPO is particularly interested in applicants with previous experience in appointment setting or home improvement sales.

Candidates must also have a suitable home office setup, including a reliable wired internet connection with minimum download and upload speeds of 40 Mbps.

Other requirements include a webcam, a clear USB headset and a computer with at least a quad core 2.0 GHz processor and 8GB of RAM.

An SSD is preferred, while Chromebooks are not accepted.

Applicants must also have a quiet, professional workspace suitable for handling customer calls.

Interested Belizeans can apply by emailing [email protected], using their full name in the subject line.

World.title: Tough cleaning jobs? Universal Hardware has NorthStar pressure washers starting at $4,614
World.content:
Tough cleaning jobs? Universal Hardware has NorthStar pressure washers starting at $4,614

By Breaking Belize News Staff (HP): From dirty driveways and concrete surfaces to outdoor equipment and commercial work areas, tough cleaning jobs call for the right tools.

Universal Hardware is highlighting its NorthStar electric pressure washers, offering Belizeans two powerful options for tackling demanding outdoor cleaning tasks.

Customers can choose between a 2,000 PSI model and a 3,000 PSI model, depending on their pressure washing requirements.

The NorthStar 2,000 PSI Electric Pressure Washer, Model 1571102, is priced at $4,614, providing an option for customers who need dedicated electric pressure washing equipment.

Those seeking higher pressure can consider the NorthStar 3,000 PSI Electric Pressure Washer, Model 1571103, priced at $4,978.

That means customers can move from the 2,000 PSI model to the 3,000 PSI option for an additional $364.

Both units feature wheeled designs, allowing users to move the equipment around suitable work areas.

Electric pressure washers can be useful for property maintenance, outdoor cleaning and other applications where pressurized water is appropriate.

For businesses, resorts, contractors and property owners across Belize, investing in suitable cleaning equipment can support regular maintenance and help keep outdoor areas presentable.
