World.title: Iraq, US discuss prospects to strengthen joint cooperation
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Minister of Defense Nayef al-Shammari and Chargé d’Affaires at the US Embassy in Baghdad Steven Fagin discussed approaches to strengthen cooperation between Baghdad and Washington on Sunday.

During their meeting in the Iraqi capital, Baghdad, the two sides discussed bilateral ties and strategies to enhance cooperation between the two countries, according to a statement cited by the state-run Iraqi News Agency (INA).

The meeting took place after the US-led international coalition formally completed its full withdrawal and ended Operation Inherent Resolve in Iraq on September 30, 2026.

Operation Inherent Resolve—the multinational military campaign formed in 2014 to fight ISIS—officially wrapped up after a 12-year presence.

The end of the combat mission shifts the relationship to a bilateral framework focused on non-combat intelligence sharing, targeted training, and security cooperation rather than active foreign military bases.

Iraqi security forces have assumed full operational control, and the government has set goals to bring remaining armed factions under state regulation.

World.title: Drone attack targets Iranian Kurdish base in northern Iraq
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – A drone attack carried out by Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) targeted on Saturday evening a base belonging to an Iranian Kurdish opposition group in the Kurdistan region of Iraq.

According to reports, the strike hit the headquarters and a guard post of the Komala party. The base is located in the Alana Valley within the Balisan region, northeast of Erbil.

Local security and party officials confirmed the strike caused material damage to buildings but resulted in no casualties.

This attack is a part of Tehran’s intensified campaign against Iraqi-based Iranian Kurdish opposition groups.

Since the military conflict broke out in the region on February 28, Iran has launched over 1,000 drones and missiles into Iraqi Kurdistan, claiming that these groups are directly endangering its national security and have Israeli support.

In mid-August, two explosive-laden drones launched from Iranian territory targeted Iraqi Kurdistan Prime Minister Masrour Barzani’s private office and the home of a top intelligence official.

The strikes took place in Erbil province’s Pirmam area, which is around 30 kilometers north of the capital.

Security personnel recognized the drone as an Iranian-designed “Hadid-110” kamikaze drone carrying explosive payloads.

While Tehran and Iran-backed armed groups have previously accused Iraqi Kurdistan of hosting hostile Iranian Kurdish opposition groups, the authorities in the Kurdistan region of Iraq have always denied using their territory to threaten neighboring nations.

World.title: Iraq, KBR discuss oil sector development
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Deputy Prime Minister for Energy Affairs Mohsen al-Mandalawi and a delegation from US-based KBR discussed on Thursday developing the country’s oil and gas sectors.

KBR’s delegation headed by the company’s president for sustainable technology solutions, Jay Ibrahim, discussed prospects for joint cooperation in the oil, gas, and energy sectors, as well as leveraging the firm’s expertise to develop infrastructure and enhance the efficiency of strategic projects, according to a statement cited by the state-run Iraqi News Agency (INA).

The meeting addressed the recovery of associated gas, the development of oil fields, the enhancement of production efficiency, and the modernization of oil facilities.

The two sides also discussed leveraging KBR’s cutting-edge technology solutions to help Iraq’s oil industry grow and to make it easier to carry out key projects that meet requirements for effectiveness, quality, and financial sustainability.

The Iraqi official stressed the importance of ongoing coordination among Iraqi authorities to identify potential areas for collaboration.

Al-Mandalawi noted that the government aims to develop actionable programs related to the Majnoon oil field, the recovery of associated gas at the West Qurna field, initiatives for ammonia production, and efforts to reduce gas flaring at oil fields.

World.title: Iraq sells 10 million barrels of oil at discounts up to $28
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq recently sold 10 million barrels of oil via its southern ports at a discount ranging from $25 to $28 per barrel.

Sources told Attaqa News that most of these shipments were acquired by Indian companies and that the loading took place at the southern ports a few days ago.

Iraq has been unable to sell any oil at a price higher than $100 per barrel since the outbreak of the military conflict in the Middle East, according to two more sources, even though world prices have risen to almost $117 per barrel.

A source at the State Oil Marketing Organization (SOMO) said that Iraq has not been able to sell oil for more than $85 per barrel.

About a month ago, the company sold some shipments of light crude at around $90 per barrel.

The spokesperson for the Ministry of Oil, Salim al-Rikabi, said that oil sales are still being conducted via the southern ports, and there are variable discounts in place to cover transportation and insurance costs for the purchasing companies.

Recently, Iraq’s average oil exports have risen to approximately 3.2 million barrels per day, according to statements made by Oil Minister Basim Khudair to the official news agency.

Oil shipments passing through the Strait of Hormuz account for roughly 3 million barrels per day.

Due to its inadequate tanker fleet, Iraq has resorted to giving substantial discounts on its oil since the start of the conflict in the region, often as much as $32 per barrel.

World.title: Iraq sells 10 million barrels of crude at steep discounts
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq recently sold approximately 10 million barrels of crude oil via its southern export terminals at steep discounts ranging between $25 and $28 per barrel against prevailing international benchmarks, according to industry sources cited by the energy platform Attaqa on Sunday, October 25, 2026.

Trade sources confirmed that Indian refining companies secured the bulk of the discounted shipments, which were loaded at southern offshore terminals in recent days.

Market participants highlighted that Baghdad has been unable to market its crude above $100 per barrel since the outbreak of regional hostilities involving Iran, even as international oil benchmarks surged toward $117 per barrel during recent trading sessions amid maritime risk and escalating conflict dynamics.

Confirming the pricing constraints, an official source at the State Organization for Marketing of Oil (SOMO) disclosed that recent spot transactions have struggled to clear above $85 per barrel.

The source noted that approximately one month prior, SOMO managed to offload select Basrah Light cargoes at around $90 per barrel before market pressures widened discount spreads. The steep price differentials emerge as the economic observatory “Eco Iraq” reported on Saturday that Iraq’s aggregate crude oil export revenues totaled $37.39 billion from shipments of 533.46 million barrels across the first nine months of 2026.

World.title: Iraq increases port capacity
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi Ministry of Transport has announced that the country’s ports can now handle twice as much cargo as they could in the past.

The ministry’s media director, Hussein Ahmed, said on Sunday that the current capacity of Iraqi ports exceeds 79 million tons of cargo and more than 3.6 million containers.

Ahmed noted that Iraqi ports can now handle twice the cargo volume previously recorded, which was over 40 million tons, as reported by the state-run Iraqi News Agency (INA).

The Iraqi official mentioned that improvements have been made to the ports, including the construction of new roads, upgrades to existing streets leading to the ports, and the establishment of marshaling yards to alleviate internal congestion.

Iraq’s State Company for Maritime Transport (SCMT), a government-owned maritime company operating under the Iraqi Ministry of Transport, announced on Sunday the reactivation of the Iraqi Line, marked by the arrival of the vessel Basra at the port of Umm Qasr.

SCMT’s director Ahmed Jassim said that the vessel arrived at the port of Umm Qasr carrying containers from the port of Jebel Ali in the United Arab Emirates, signaling the reactivation of the maritime route and the resumption of its commercial voyages after a hiatus that lasted for decades.

World.title: Iraq advances Japanese loan port projects as Grand Faw reach 98%
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s Ministry of Transport is moving to activate two major maritime infrastructure projects—a new floating dock and an integrated shipyards city—financed under the Japanese official development assistance (ODA) loan framework.

The initiative is aimed at expanding vessel repair, maintenance, and auxiliary maritime services across Iraqi ports, coinciding with significant construction milestones at the strategic Grand Faw Port in Basra.

According to statements delivered to the official newspaper by Hussein Ahmed, Director of Media and Government Communications at the Ministry of Transport, ministry officials held technical consultations with representatives of the Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA) loan authority.

The discussions centered on selecting construction locations and addressing civil and logistical engineering requirements for both the floating dry dock and the specialized shipyard zone to modernize national maritime support capabilities.

The operational expansion coincides with near-completion across primary infrastructure phases at the Grand Faw Port. General Director of the General Company for Ports of Iraq (GCPI), Abdullah Aati Abdullah, announced that the port’s core breakwater works have reached 100% completion.

Additionally, the submerged immersed tunnel connecting the port to Umm Qasr has achieved a 98% execution rate, while foundational infrastructure across the facility stands at 94%.

Speaking at a press conference, Abdullah stated that technical teams are preparing to transition toward superstructure and terminal installation phases under the oversight of Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi and Transport Minister Wahab Al-Hasani.

Abdullah confirmed that preliminary operational trials are scheduled to commence in the upcoming period. He noted that while broader regional shipping traffic has felt the ripple effects of security dynamics around the Strait of Hormuz, work remains focused on expanding container handling capacity, securing yard storage, and cementing Grand Faw’s position as a regional logistics hub connecting the Gulf to Europe.

World.title: Iraq to construct six dams with Turkey and 13 rainwater harvesting barriers
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s Ministry of Water Resources revealed plans on Sunday, October 25, 2026, to construct six new dams under the bilateral framework agreement with Turkey, while advancing technical designs and assessments for 13 additional rainwater and seasonal flood harvesting barriers across several governorates to bolster strategic water reserves, support agriculture, and combat desertification.

According to statements delivered to the official newspaper by Ministry Spokesperson and Director General of the General Authority for Irrigation and Reclamation Projects, Khaled Shamal, technical blueprints have been finalized for three dams under the first package of the Turkish framework agreement, preparing them for on-ground execution by Turkish contractors.

The three initial structures comprise the Kharaz Dam in Al-Muthanna Governorate, the Al-Abyad Dam in Ain Al-Tamr in Karbala Governorate, and the Abu Takiya Dam in Nineveh Governorate, with site evaluations underway for an additional three dams proposed under a secondary implementation package.

In parallel with the Turkish cooperation framework, Shamal detailed progress on domestic water harvesting infrastructure designed to capture torrential flash floods and surface runoffs. Technical engineering designs are complete for five submerged check dams in Nineveh Governorate—Sheikh Bakr 1 and 2, Ain Alaq, Ain Ba’shiqa, and Ain Bahzani—with active construction already launched at two sites.

An additional eight water barriers are undergoing hydrologic surveys and final design studies, distributed across Nineveh (3 dams), Najaf (2 dams), Al-Muthanna (2 dams), and Diyala (1 dam), providing vital localized water reserves to support nomadic resettlement, pastoral communities, and regional land reclamation initiatives.

World.title: Give mayors real powers, ensure timely civic audits, urban body heads tell Centre
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Even as the Centre moots directly elected mayors with a fixed five-year tenure and a mayor-in-council system, municipal heads from different cities at National Urban Conclave flagged that the move would serve little purpose without giving mayors adequate powers.

Rajkot mayor Nehal Shukla also called for time-bound financial audits of civic bodies, saying that âno municipal body can function without financial irregularitiesâ.

Participating in a discussion on proposed changes to the Model Municipal Law, Shukla said mayors in municipal governance were like governors, while standing committees wielded financial powers and executive officials remained under the control of state govts.

âWherever we have directly elected mayors, we must have a mayor-in-council. If you donât give power to the mayor, direct election hardly serves any objective,â he said.

Under the mayor-in-Council system, executive powers to run a city on a day-to-day basis are shared between the mayor and a small, cabinet-like group of elected councillors, who are individually accountable for their respective portfolios.

Shukla also suggested that municipal elections be conducted by the Election Commission, citing its track record of holding timely general and assembly elections.





He said state govts invariably found one reason or another to delay municipal polls.

âThe biggest missing thing that needs to be fixed is timely audits to bring financial discipline. Audit reports are delayed by six to eight years, and thatâs why irregularities do not come to light. We all know that no municipal body can function without financial irregularities,â he said.

Shukla pointed out that rules require tenders to be floated for works or services costing more than Rs 5 lakh, but alleged that this was often not followed.

Municipal commissioners, he said, were aware of such violations but approved the transactions because otherwise civic bodies could not function.

He suggested that audits be conducted by the Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG). If state auditors continued to conduct them, he said, the law should ensure that the audit backlog did not exceed two years.

âPeople have more expectations from directly elected mayors. But we have no power. Executive officers such as municipal commissioners are beyond the control of mayors, as we cannot write their annual performance reports or have any say in their appointments. Commissioners change frequently,â she said.

World.title: Delhi Police file FIR against opposition MPs over alleged trespassing at Jamia during student protest

Jamia Millia Islamia

Delhi Police have registered an FIR against opposition MPs who visited Jamia Millia Islamia University over alleged trespassing, following a complaint by the university authorities, amid ongoing student protests demanding the restoration of the students' union.According to news agency ANI, the FIR was registered following the MPs' visit to the campus to meet students protesting for the restoration of the Jamia Millia Islamia Students' Union (JMISU), withdrawal of disciplinary action against protesters and other demands.Jamia Registrar Md Mahtab Alam Rizvi had accused Congress MPs Imran Masood and Imran Pratapgarhi of entering the campus without authorisation. Rizvi alleged that Masood crossed a wall to enter the premises, while Pratapgarhi broke a lock.The protest began on October 12, with students demanding the restoration of the students' union and a definite schedule for elections. They have also sought the withdrawal of disciplinary action against students who participated in the agitation.According to the Press Trust of India (PTI), Jamia's last students' union elections were held in 2005, and the union was dissolved in 2006. The current agitation has also brought attention to student concerns over attendance policies, hostel facilities, scholarships and research stipends.The protests have drawn support from opposition leaders. PTI reported that Samajwadi Party MP Mohibbullah Nadvi was detained while travelling to meet the protesting students and was later released. Congress MP Imran Masood was also detained near the university during the agitation.The university administration has said a committee is preparing a draft constitution for the students' union. Registrar Rizvi told ANI that the election schedule would be announced after the draft constitution was submitted. The administration has also said disciplinary cases against students would be reviewed.The controversy has widened following reports of graffiti on campus walls, including the slogan âFree Kashmirâ. The university condemned the graffiti, while Masood told ANI that he had denounced the slogan and maintained that Kashmir is an integral part of India.The FIR marks a further escalation in the standoff between the university administration, protesting students and opposition politicians.

World.title: Women founders are building India's social startups, their representation in nonprofits outpaces corporate leadership by a big margin, shows study
World.content:
Women founders are building India's social startups

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: A survey of more than 145 organisations working in the social impact space shows that over 57% of non-profits have at least one female founder â more than three times the 18% share reported among Indian startups. Moreover, female representation in the nonprofit sector outpaces corporate leadership, where women hold just 1.8% of CEO positions, 4.4% of CFO positions, and 29% of executive director roles.These findings are part of accelerator for non-profits Change Engineâs âEast of Doing Goodâ report - âAccess to flexible funding: a Gender Lensâ. The survey covers small organisations (annual budgets less than Rs 1 crore), medium (annual budgets between Rs 1 crore -5 crore) and large organisations (Rs 5 crore and more). The study sample also had an almost equal split between organisations eligible for foreign funding (with FCRA or US 501(c)) and those that were not.Out of the 145 plus organisations surveyed, nearly 31% have only female founders, while around 27% have both male and female founders.The research also shows that women are not only founding more nonprofits, but women founded organisations are better funded and hold more long term flexible funding.The study found that non-profits with atleast one female founder also had bigger budgets. The data shows that 70% of organisations with at least one female founder have an annual budget of over Rs 1 crore, compared to 43.5% of organisations with only-male founders.Also around 21% of organisations with at least one female founder have more than 25% of their budget in flexible unrestricted funding, compared to just about 13% of organisations with only male founders. Flexible funding is the non-programmatic funding that nonprofits can use to invest in talent, technology, research and strengthening the organisation.As far as long-term grants are concerned it turns out that over 65% of organisations with at least one female founder have access to multi-year funding (three years or more), compared to around 56% of organisations with only male founders. Among these, around 27% of organisations with at least one female founder have received multi-year grants above Rs 1 crore, compared to just about 11% of only male founder organisations.The report highlights that when asked to rate (on a scale of 1-5) how easy it was to raise unrestricted funds from corporate social responsibility (CSR), high net-worth individuals (HNIs), domestic foundations, foreign foundations, and crowdfunding/retail, organisations with at least one female founder scored consistently scored higher across every category with an average score of 2.41 in comparison with 2.06 of organisations with only male founders.However, challenges remain. The study shows that cheque sizes remain small for everyone: âA staggering 82% of organisations with at least one female founder and 83% of only male founded organisations said typical unrestricted cheque sizes in India are less than Rs 25 lakh, showing that the small-cheque problem cuts across gender lines,â the study highlights.Varun Aggarwal and Shubham Bansal, co-founders, Change Engine highlighted that the findings show that women are leading Indiaâs social sector and building bigger and better resourced organisations. We need to encourage more women to come into this sector," Aggarwal asserted. âIn our accelerator, we meet women founders who are building strong, ambitious institutions to tackle some of Indiaâs biggest social challenges. Itâs encouraging to see that what weâve been observing on the ground is now backed by data. Six in ten nonprofits in our survey were founded by a woman founder,â Bansal added.However, the Change Engine founders highlight that the access to unrestricted flexible funding remains consistently low across the board with 80% of the surveyed founders reporting that they struggle to scale their work due to the lack of unrestricted funding. âThis funding rigidity forces organisations to spend disproportionate time on fundraising, rather than focusing on innovation and impact,â they added.

World.title: 'Pakistan has no right': Congress distances itself from ally Farooq Abdullah's Kashmiri remark
World.content:
J&K Congress distances itself from Farooq Abdullah's Pakistan remarks; Kashmiri Pandit groups seek FIR

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

What Farooq Abdullah said

NEW DELHI: The Jammu and Kashmir Congress has distanced itself from National Conference (NC) president Farooq Abdullahâs remarks that Pakistan was helping Kashmiris by keeping the Kashmir issue alive at international fora.âThe Jammu and Kashmir Pradesh Congress Committee has distanced itself from the statement of NC president Farooq Abdullah and asserted that Pakistan has no right to talk about or interfere in our internal affairs as J&K is an integral part of India,â J&K Congress chief spokesperson Ravinder Sharma said in a post on X.However, speaking to reporters, Sharma said Abdullahâs remarks appeared to reflect frustration over the Centreâs failure to fulfil its promise to restore statehood to Jammu and Kashmir.âPakistan has consistently waged a proxy war against India and caused the deaths of innocent people in J&K by sponsoring terrorism. Pakistanâs role in promoting terrorism must be condemned, and strict action should continue against it,â Sharma said, reiterating that the Congress was firmly opposed to any interference by Pakistan in Indiaâs internal affairs.Sharma said Abdullah should clarify the intent behind his remarks, adding that opposition to Pakistan-sponsored terrorism and the demand for restoration of statehood were separate but equally important issues.He also suggested that Abdullahâs comments were directed at what he described as discrimination against minorities across the country and the policies pursued by BJP governments in various states.âThe remarks reflected resentment against a pattern of oppression and discrimination,â the Congress leader said.Sharma further said Jammu and Kashmir continued to face resentment over the delay in restoring statehood, despite repeated assurances by the Centre before the Supreme Court, Parliament and the public.Meanwhile, some Kashmiri Pandit groups have filed a police complaint seeking an FIR against the former chief minister over his comments.His remarks drew criticism from some Kashmiri Pandit groups, which lodged a police complaint seeking the registration of an FIR against the former chief minister.Meanwhile, Kashmiri Pandit groups Panun Kashmir and the Jammu State People's Movement (JSPM) have lodged a police complaint at the Channi police station in Jammu, seeking the registration of an FIR against Abdullah over his remarks.The complaint, submitted by Panun Kashmir chairman Tito Ganju and JSPM chairman Col Ajay Raina (retd), sought an investigation into statements attributed to Abdullah concerning the constitutional status of Jammu and Kashmir and alleged religious polarisation.It cited his reported remarks questioning the prospects of justice from the Union government and warning that the people of J&K risked losing their identity if they failed to confront the prevailing political circumstances.The complainants also referred to remarks attributed to Abdullah about the demolition of mosques, homes and shops, as well as his assertion that Hindus and Muslims were being pitted against each other. They urged the police to examine the statements in their entirety, taking into account their context, the audience addressed and their potential implications.The complaint sought an FIR under Sections 152, 196 and 197 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), along with any other provisions that may apply based on the investigation.The provisions cited concern acts endangering India's sovereignty, unity and integrity, promoting enmity between groups, and certain imputations or assertions prejudicial to national integration, a Panun Kashmir spokesperson said.BJP leader Jahanzaib Sirwal also criticised Abdullah, accusing him of double standards for invoking Pakistan to question India's intentions while overlooking the suffering of people across the Line of Control.âIt was deeply unfortunate that a leader who has dominated J&Kâs political landscape for decades continues to rely on the Pakistan narrative rather than account for the consequences of his own politics.âFarooq Sahib has spent decades building a political narrative around Pakistan, but has he ever honestly answered what this politics has delivered to the people of J&K?âHis party does not have to seek votes in Pakistan-occupied Jammu and Kashmir, but that cannot be an excuse to remain silent on the atrocities and sufferings of the people living there. Human rights cannot be selective, and political morality cannot change with electoral convenience,â Sirwal said.He added that the NC leadership must stop treating Pakistan as a convenient political instrument to invoke whenever it suited its narrative.Addressing a party event in Baramulla on Saturday, Abdullah questioned whether people in Jammu and Kashmir could expect justice from the Centre.âWhat hope will you (people of J&K) have from them (Delhi)? Will you expect that they will do justice for you?" he said.Urging Kashmiris to remain courageous in confronting Delhi, Abdullah warned that their identity could disappear if they failed to do so.âIf not, you will be erased. Even our trace and identity will disappear. They are silent today because there is noise in the world, and our neighbour is constantly behind this. Everywhere they say, 'the decision regarding Kashmir has not been made'. That is what is saving us. Otherwise, their intentions are not good,â he said.

World.title: PM Modi inaugurates RBI's Rs 169-crore data centre, cybersecurity institute in Odisha
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Sunday inaugurated the Reserve Bank of India's (RBI) Rs 169-crore data centre and Cybersecurity Training Institute at Info Valley-II in Jatni, near Bhubaneswar, Odisha.

Spread across 18.55 acres, the facility's foundation stone was laid by then RBI governor Shaktikanta Das on March 22, 2023. The data centre will host mission-critical payment and settlement systems, along with other key RBI initiatives, according to a government statement.

It is expected to improve the reach, efficiency and reliability of digital financial services while providing a secure foundation for India's increasingly technology-driven financial sector.

The Cybersecurity Training Institute will focus on training, research and capacity building in cybersecurity and enterprise technology, helping strengthen capabilities across the financial sector.

The location was chosen for its geographical stability, away from seismically active zones and high-risk international border areas, officials said according to news agency PTI. This is expected to reduce the facility's exposure to natural disasters and geopolitical vulnerabilities.

World.title: BSF apprehends four Pakistani fishermen in Kutch, seizes boat
World.content:
The Border Security Force (BSF) has apprehended four Pakistani fishermen who allegedly entered Indian waters for crab-catching activities and seized a fishing boat near the India-Pakistan border in Gujaratâs Kutch district.

According to news agency PTI, the fishermen were apprehended from the Sir Creek area on Sunday following specific intelligence inputs, an official said. The fishermen were identified as Kadir Thaimor, Muhammad Mussa, Azgar Thaimor and Ahsan Jat, all residents of Chach Jaan Khan village in Pakistanâs Sindh province, according to information provided by the BSF.

Sir Creek is a narrow, marshy tidal channel in the Rann of Kutch, along the coastal region between Gujarat and Pakistanâs Sindh province.

The area is strategically sensitive because the longstanding India-Pakistan boundary dispute over the creek affects the demarcation of the maritime boundary in the Arabian Sea.

The regionâs shallow waters, tidal channels and extensive marshlands make navigation and border surveillance challenging. Fishing activities in the area can also lead to fishermen crossing into the other countryâs waters, prompting apprehensions by security personnel.

The BSF maintains surveillance along the sensitive western border to prevent unauthorised crossings and other illegal activities. The latest apprehension follows an operation based on specific intelligence inputs, during which the four fishermen and their boat were taken into custody.

World.title: Strike on Gaza university kills three: staff, hospital
World.content:
An Israeli strike on a university in Gaza City killed three people on Sunday (October 25, 2026), staff and a local hospital said, while the civil defence agency reported five others killed elsewhere in the territory.

Reached for comment on the strike at the Islamic University, the Israeli army said that it was currently under review.

Al Shifa hospital reported receiving three bodies and treating eight people who were wounded in the drone strike, with two sources at the university saying the dead were employees and the injured were students.

The university said the campus and its surroundings had been targeted twice on Sunday (October 25, 2026), condemning the attacks and mourning those killed in a statement.

Gaza's Education Ministry likewise condemned the strike and said, "The global silence regarding attacks on students and universities serves as encouragement for the continuation of these crimes".

"This strike occurs at a time when the higher education sector is facing total annihilation, with 95% of the buildings belonging to academic institutions having been damaged as a result of the war," it continued.

"This heinous assault is part of a continuous series of attacks on education; over the past six days, 10 students and educators have been killed by the occupation's fire."

In a statement, the army said it had been "targeting a terrorist from Hamas' military wing".

"Following the identification of uninvolved individuals in the area, the munition was diverted in order to mitigate harm to them. The incident is under review," it said, without specifying whether those killed at the university were hit by accident.

A truce has been in effect in Gaza for over a year, but it has failed to completely halt the violence there.

Gaza civil defence spokesman Mahmoud Bassal said five other people were killed on Sunday (October 25, 2026), three in strikes around the southern city of Khan Yunis, one in central Deir al Balah and one northwest of Gaza City.

One more person was wounded by Israeli gunfire in Jabalia refugee camp in the north.

World.title: Monsoon tracker LIVE: Depression over Bay of Bengal set to become ‘very severe cyclonic storm’, cross A.P. coast by October 28
World.content:
Under the influence of the impending Very Severe Cyclonic Storm over the Westcentral Bay of Bengal, extremely heavy rainfall is likely over Coastal Andhra Pradesh on October 27 and 28, Odisha and Telangana on October 28 and Chhattisgarh on October 28 and 29, 2026.

The Depression over Eastcentral and adjoining Southeast Bay of Bengal moved southwestwards with speed of 5 kmph during past 6 hours, intensified into a deep Depression and lay centered at 11:30 a.m. today, over the same region, near Latitude 15.1°N and Longitude 91.0°E, about 420 km north-northwest of Sri Vijaya Puram (Andaman Islands), 870 km east-southeast of Vishakhapatnam (Andhra Pradesh), 960 km east-southeast of Kakinada (Andhra Pradesh), 1060 km east-Southeast of Machilipatnam (Andhra Pradesh) and 1130 km east of Bapatla (Andhra Pradesh).

It is very likely to move nearly southwestwards, and intensify further into a cyclonic storm over eastcentral & adjoining southeast Bay of Bengal by tomorrow early morning. Then it is very likely to move west-northwestwards over the Eastcentral & adjoining Westcentral Bay of Bengal and intensify into a severe cyclonic storm over westcentral Bay of Bengal around Tuesday (October 27, 2026) morning.

Thereafter, it is very likely to move northwestwards, intensify further into a very severe cyclonic storm and reach Westcentral Bay of Bengal near Andhra Pradesh coast around morning of October 28, 2026. It is very likely to cross Andhra Pradesh & Yanam coasts between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam as a very severe cyclonic storm with the maximum sustained wind speed of 115-125 kmph gusting to 140 kmph by forenoon of 28th October, 2026.

Meanwhile, the Regional Meteorological Centre (RMC) has forecast heavy to very heavy rain at isolated places in Tamil Nadu’s Chennai, northern, delta and western districts.

World.title: Child rights panel seeks report on schoolgirl’s death within two weeks
World.content:
The Delhi Commission for Protection of Child Rights (DCPCR) on Sunday sought an inquiry report within two weeks from the Directorate of Education over the death of a 17-year-old Class 12 student who was found with severe burns at a government school in east Delhi’s Krishna Nagar on Saturday.

The girl was found behind the school’s guard room after school authorities heard cries from the area. She was taken to Dr. Hedgewar Arogya Sansthan, where she was declared dead on arrival. According to police, a water bottle used to carry petrol was recovered from the spot.

Taking cognisance of media reports, the commission raised concerns about student safety, questioning how the girl managed to bring an inflammable substance into the school without being noticed.

“The content of the news report, if true, are disturbing and raise serious concern on the safety of children inside the school premises. The incident as a whole has resulted in violation of child rights on account of negligence of public servants,” the commission stated in its notice.

The commission issued notices to the Directorate of Education, the school principal and the police, seeking action-taken reports within two weeks.

DCPCR member Kundan Kanskar said the commission would take action after receiving the reports. “Such incidents hint at a lack of accessible, quality mental health services for students in schools,” he said.

Police probe

Police have seized the school’s CCTV digital video recorder and are examining the footage to reconstruct the sequence of events. They are questioning the security guard, teachers and family members to ascertain how the incident went unnoticed. The school’s attendance register has also been examined.

Officers on Saturday said a three-page purported suicide note recovered from the student’s bag referred to “relationship issues and parental disappointment”. Sources said one page contained an apology to her family, while another requested that a friend not be harassed.

“We are investigating the matter. The circumstances leading to the incident are being examined,” a senior police officer said.

Police said they are also examining the family’s allegation that the girl could have been the victim of a conspiracy.

(With inputs from PTI)

World.title: Two feared trapped after building collapse in Delhi's Harsh Vihar
World.content:
Two men, aged 60 and 36, are suspected to be trapped after roof slabs collapsed during construction in north-east Delhi’s Harsh Vihar on Sunday evening, police said.

The collapse occurred in Milan Garden as an additional floor was being built on an old, single-storey house on a 200-square-yard plot, said an officer.

A resident said a newly laid slab gave way over an older slab.

The Delhi Fire Services received a call at 6.46 p.m. and sent five fire tenders. Teams from the National Disaster Response Force, police, Civil Defence and Delhi Disaster Management Authority joined the rescue efforts.

“Two people are suspected to be trapped, but there is no confirmation yet,” Additional Deputy Commissioner of Police Sandeep Lamba said.

No casualties had been reported till the time the report went to the press.

“Their family members suspect that they are trapped as their mobile phones are not reachable,” the officer said.

Some relatives alleged that rescue work was slow and tried to remove the debris themselves.

Later in the evening, Ministers Ashish Sood and Kapil Mishra also visited the building collapse site.

Police said, the cause of the collapse and the status of construction approvals are yet to be established.

(With inputs from PTI)

World.title: As 2000 attend Kashmir marathon, CM Omar says ‘strengthens J&K’s position as a global sports tourism destination’
World.content:
In a bid to project Kashmir as a safe destination for sports tourism, Srinagar on Sunday (October 25, 2026) hosted a marathon attended by over 2000 participants from across the country and overseas.

J&K Chief Minister Omar Abdullah flagged off the full marathon (42.195 km) at 6:30 a.m. and the half marathon (21 km) at 7:45 a.m. The participants started from the city centre, Lal Chowk, Polo View, Zero Bridge, the Jhelum riverfront and the picturesque boulevard around the Dal lake.

“The Kashmir marathon is emerging as a flagship sporting event, strengthening J&K’s position as a global sports tourism destination, boosting tourism and inspiring a culture of fitness and healthy living across the region,” said Mr. Abdullah.

Besides 1,221 local participants, officials said 513 runners were from different parts of the country and 73 foreign athletes, representing 12 countries. A total of 68 medals were awarded among the winners, comprising 34 medals each in the full marathon and half marathon categories. The third edition carries a total prize purse of ₹3.17 crore, with the winner in the open category receiving ₹25 lakh.

Two Kenyan runners, Emmanuel Sikuku Ndiwa and Lemensa Harpaa, won the men’s and women’s full marathon titles, respectively. Omolo, the Kenyan athlete who topped the race, praised the route along Dal Lake as “one of the most beautiful tracks”. Siyom Kumar, a resident of Uttar Pradesh, completed the 21-km half-marathon in one hour and 41 minutes.

Traversing through the city’s historic streets, picturesque waterfronts and celebrated gardens, the marathon offers a unique blend of competitive sport, cultural vibrancy and the Valley’s breathtaking landscape.

J&K Lieutenant Governor Manoj Sinha, who addressed the award ceremony of the Kashmir Marathon, congratulated all the winners for their outstanding achievements. He highlighted the growing international stature of the event. “The Kashmir Marathon has earned recognition on the global running circuit and has helped position Srinagar among the cities hosting prestigious long-distance races,” said Mr. Sinha. He said the participants from across India and abroad act as ambassadors of J&K, carrying back memories of its hospitality and natural beauty.

The L-G also commended the Jammu and Kashmir Police and security forces for fostering a conducive atmosphere over the past six years, “paving the way for hosting such prestigious international-level events in the Union Territory”.

World.title: Pulakeshinagar IED blast case cracked, personal rivalry behind the plot
World.content:
The Bengaluru police have cracked the case of the recent blast at an under-construction building on Jeremiah Road, injuring two, and arrested a 27-year-old bakery salesman, who allegedly conspired with two childhood friends to murder his uncle by assembling an improvised explosive device (IED) concealed inside a parcel.

According to the police, the prime accused held a grudge against his uncle, Allauddin M., over property and financial disputes, as well as a personal issue involving the breakdown of his sister’s marriage.

The incident occurred on October 20 when workers were at the building. A loud explosion was heard on the fifth floor, and an investigation revealed that an IED concealed inside a torch had exploded.

The IED was assembled in Raichur by one of the conspirators, who learned from YouTube. Material obtained from firecrackers was used as the explosive material in the IED, rigged inside a battery using an electrical circuit and pellets.

Investigators said the accused had prepared a parcel containing the device and left it at a petty shop near the building where Allauddin was working. The accused allegedly contacted him over the phone and pressured him to open the parcel.

Allauddin, who was having lunch, asked his colleague to open it and the device exploded when the parcel was opened. Allauddin and his colleague, Suraj Kumar, a security guard from Uttar Pradesh, sustained severe injuries.

The case had led to speculations of terrorism owing to the involvement of an IED, even as sleuths from the National Investigation Agency (NIA) also joined the probe.

Home Minister Priyank Kharge had appealed to not give into rumours, even as the Bengaluru City Police launched a massive operation to crack the case. Commissioner Seemant Kumar Singh said around 1,200 personnel had worked in different teams during the investigation and announced a ₹3 Lakh reward for those who cracked the case.

World.title: A Korean cultural evening in Hyderabad, with a distinctly Telangana touch
World.content:
What happens when the rhythms of Korean culture meet the beats of Telangana’s traditional drums? At Shilpakala Vedika here on Sunday, the answer unfolded through a lively mix of music, dance, martial arts and cultural exchange, as Korea Culture Day 2026 brought the traditions of two countries together on one stage.

From afternoon, stalls selling Korean products drew curious visitors, with crowds gathering around them to explore a slice of Korean culture. As the evening approached, the buzz moved towards the auditorium, where hundreds of people began assembling from 5 p.m., eager to witness the performances lined up for the occasion.

Inside, the anticipation gave way to a celebration that travelled between two cultures, from the precision and power of Korean martial arts to the vigorous movements of Telangana’s traditional dances.

The programme began around 5.30 p.m. with an address by Lee Seong-ho, Ambassador of the Republic of Korea to India, who welcomed the audience to Hyderabad and spoke of the cultural ties that the event hoped to strengthen.

Drawing a connection between Diwali, India’s festival of lights, and Chuseok, Korea’s harvest festival, Mr. Lee spoke about the shared values underlying celebrations in both countries: family, togetherness, gratitude and hope for the future.

Though the traditions may differ, he said, the emotions they evoke are remarkably similar. Cultural exchanges, he added, help people discover just how much they have in common.

Telangana Deputy Chief Minister Mallu Bhatti Vikramarka, who addressed the gathering, spoke about Korea’s transformation into a global economic and cultural force. He noted how Korean music, cinema and television had found audiences across the world, demonstrating that a country’s influence extended beyond its economic and military strength to the power of its cultural imagination. He also highlighted the historical connections between India and Korea and Hyderabad’s long-standing identity as a meeting point of cultures, languages and traditions. "Telangana’s festivals, arts and heritage were an important part of its identity as a state looking towards a globally connected future," he added.

Beyond culture, Mr. Vikramarka pointed to opportunities for closer cooperation between Telangana and Korean enterprises in areas such as electronics, electric vehicles, advanced manufacturing, renewable energy and emerging technologies.

The Daekyung Taekwondo Demonstration was among the evening’s most energetic acts. The performers combined agility, strength and precision in a series of martial arts displays, breaking tiles and executing impressive stunts that drew loud cheers from the crowd. Each demonstration was met with excitement, turning the auditorium into a space of applause and animated reactions.

The programme then shifted to the vigorous rhythms of Telangana’s Perini Shiva Tandavam. The traditional dance, known for its powerful movements and historical association with warriors, brought a distinctly local flavour to the evening. The Telangana Dappulu performance followed, filling the programme with the forceful beats of traditional drums.

The audience was then introduced to Korean traditional performance through Eolssigu, before a violin duo offered another musical dimension to the evening. The Atti Classic Vocal Crossover Performance further broadened the programme’s musical range, leading into an instrumental performance by a Korean band that brought the cultural showcase to a close.

World.title: Jharkhand BJP unanimously passes political resolution at State Executive Committee meeting
World.content:
On the final day of the Jharkhand Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) State Executive Committee meeting in Ranchi on Sunday (October 25, 2026), the committee passed a resolution calling the Hemant Soren-led government anti-people.

The Leader of the Opposition, Babulal Marandi, tabled the resolution, and former Chief Ministers Champai Soren and Madhu Koda seconded it. The resolution focused on the alleged administration’s failures across all fronts.

In the resolution, BJP said that Mr. Soren’s government failed to fulfil election promises, law and order is deteriorating, failed to ensure women’s safety, mineral resources are being looted, youth and students have been betrayed, and the tribal communities are being oppressed.

By questioning the State government’s policies and style of functioning, the resolution pledged to intensify the struggle against alleged corruption and unemployment following the guidance from National President Nitin Nabin who also attended the meeting on October 24, 2026.

Mr. Marandi alleged that the Congress and the Jharkhand Mukti Morcha (JMM) have looted tribal land in Jharkhand. Mr. Marandi accused Hemant Soren of being responsible for the land dispossession of the tribal population, urging party workers to take action; he called for a strong and vigorous protest against this.

Expressing concern over the alleged demographic shift, he pointed out that while the JMM and Congress view this issue merely through the lens of a ‘vote bank’ for the BJP, the changing demographics of the state are a matter of serious concern.

He also mentioned that, under the guise of a ‘tribal rally,’ efforts were made to involve the Christian community. He expressed concern over the alleged decline in the tribal population and the rising proportion of the Muslim population, warning that if this trend continues, the situation could mirror that of Bangladesh.

Former Chief Minister Champai Soren, speaking in support of the political resolution, said that in the Santhal Pargana region, more than 30,000 hectares of land belonging to tribal communities have been allegedly captured by infiltrators.

In the resolution, the party launched a sharp attack on the JMM-Congress-RJD coalition government, stating that since coming to power in Jharkhand in 2019, the administration has offered the public mere dreams of development, while the reality on the ground is defined by disappointment, unemployment, and corruption.

In the presence of State BJP President Aditya Sahu, the BJP demanded the immediate completion of the ‘triple test’ process—a prerequisite for reservation for the backward classes—and insisted that the three-tier Panchayat elections be held on schedule.

The Committee asserted that the BJP will not remain silent on matters concerning the rights of the people of Jharkhand, the future of its youth, and the state’s development.

The Committee resolution alleges that a growing sense of insecurity prevails among the public due to incidents of crime, shootings, robberies, and other criminal activities. The BJP asserted that the primary duty of any government is to ensure the safety of its citizens’ lives and property.

The Committee resolved that the BJP will intensify a State-wide public awareness campaign and democratic struggle against the Hemant Soren government—citing its failure to keep promises, rampant corruption, unemployment, a deteriorating law-and-order situation, and other issues affecting the public interest.

The State BJP decided that party workers will reach out to every village and household to inform the public about the government’s performance, while raising a strong voice for the rights of the youth, students, farmers, women, tribal communities, and marginalised sections of society.

World.title: Shadab Khan's maiden ODI century steers Pakistan into tri-series final after thrilling chase against England
World.content:
Fortune favours the brave, and on Sunday it favoured Shadab Khan just when he seemed to have been abandoned by it.

He had dragged Pakistan from the brink of defeat to within touching distance of victory in the One-day International tri-series match against England. And it had taken extraordinary bravery to do so.

With the last wicket standing and Haris Rauf holding firm at the other end, Pakistan needed 27 runs when Shadab swept Gus Atkinson for six over fine leg.

Before the sparse crowd at the Gaddafi Stadium could finish celebrating, Atkinson fired a full delivery into Shadab’s pads. England appealed in unison and the umpire raised his finger.

Shadab, already regretting the momentary lapse, tapped his bat against his helmet in frustration before reviewing the decision, more out of obligation than hope.

Then came the twist. The big screen showed a spike on UltraEdge as the ball passed the bat. The decision was overturned, disbelief gave way to delight and Shadab returned to the crease with a smile.

He responded by squeezing Atkinson for four between short third and backward point to bring up his maiden ODI century off 91 balls, then whipped another full delivery through square leg for four.

After two dot balls, he pumped Atkinson over long-off for six, leaving Pakistan one hit away from victory.

Haris, who had faced 18 balls for his three runs, settled the contest in the next over, drilling debutant Henry Crocombe straight down the ground for four.

Pakistan reached 243-9 in 47.1 overs to complete a remarkable one-wicket victory, seal their place in the Oct 31 final and condemn England to another agonising defeat.

Shadab remained unbeaten on 113 off 96 balls, with 13 fours and five sixes, while his unbroken 89-run stand with Haris set a record for the highest 10th-wicket partnership in a successful ODI chase, surpassing the previous mark of 64.

Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, extending his heartiest congratulations to the team, wrote on X: “The last wicket partnership between Shadab and Haris turned the game around. Shadab’s century was spectacular. Well done boys!”

He said, “Every run, every wicket and every catch showed the grit, discipline and fighting spirit that define Pakistan.”

The unlikely rescue began when Shadab walked in at 103-5 after Arafat Minhas fell for one.

Pakistan had been chasing England’s 241 all out but were already in trouble, having lost Fakhar Zaman (10), Saim Ayub (six) and Babar Azam (10) inside seven overs. Saad Baig briefly counter-attacked with 32 off 22 balls, including seven fours, before falling at 74-4.

Hasan Nawaz made 15 before Liam Dawson dismissed him at 102, and Arafat followed in the next over.

Shadab initially worked his way into the innings, but his task grew harder when Salman Ali Agha, who had made 26 off 49 balls, was caught off Dawson at 121-6.

Shaheen Shah Afridi and Razaullah also fell, leaving Pakistan 154-9 after 33.5 overs and still needing 88 runs.

Shadab, however, refused to surrender. He reached 32 before Haris arrived, then began to attack with greater conviction.

He drove Atkinson over mid-off and pulled him through deep midwicket for boundaries, while a six over midwicket from Razaullah at the other end briefly lifted the pressure before the debutant was bowled by Will Jacks.

Shadab’s fifty came off 49 balls, with a six over deep square leg against Crocombe. He then used his feet to Dawson, sweeping a full toss for four and carving another six over wide long-off.

Reverse-sweeps and crisp drives through cover kept the chase alive as England struggled to find the final breakthrough.

With Haris offering dogged support, Shadab brought up the 50-run stand for the last wicket and then moved into the 90s with a pull for four off Sam Curran.

He declined singles at times to retain the strike, taking responsibility for almost every scoring opportunity. His century made him only the third batter to score an ODI hundred at No. 8 or lower.

Pakistan’s bowling shines under Shaheen

Earlier, Ben Duckett had stood tall with a century as England crumbled around him, managing 241 in 46.4 overs.

Shaheen led Pakistan’s attack with 4-46, reducing the visitors to 19-3 inside five overs. Tom Banton fell for four, Joe Root made five and captain Harry Brook was run out for one. Haris then removed Jordan Cox for six as England slumped to 52-4.

Duckett rebuilt the innings, reaching his half-century off 56 balls and helping England past 100 in the 20th over.

He pulled Haris for four, launched Salman over deep midwicket for six and reverse-hit another boundary. Curran provided the only substantial support, scoring 42 off 52 balls as the pair added 93 for the fifth wicket.

Shaheen broke the stand by dismissing Curran, caught at fine leg, before Duckett reached his fifth ODI century off 104 balls — his first against Pakistan. He made 105 off 111 deliveries, including 10 fours and two sixes, before Arafat had him caught at short fine leg for 187-7.

Razaullah took two wickets, including Will Jacks for 13, while Arafat also dismissed Jamie Overton for 10. Atkinson’s unbeaten 36 off 28 balls, featuring three sixes, lifted England to 241 before Shaheen dismissed Crocombe for eight to finish with four wickets.

England’s total looked competitive when Pakistan collapsed, but Shadab’s extraordinary innings turned the match on its head and carried the hosts into the final.

Haris Rauf compounded England’s troubles when Jordan Cox edged behind to Babar Azam for six, leaving the visitors struggling at 52-4 in the 10th over.

Duckett, however, refused to let the innings unravel completely. The left-hander brought up his half-century off 56 balls as England reached 100 in the 20th over, keeping the scoreboard moving with well-timed cuts, drives and sweeps.

He pulled Haris through midwicket for four before launching Salman Ali Agha over deep midwicket for six. Duckett also produced a reverse-hit boundary against Salman and pierced the covers with a crisp drive off Shadab Khan.

At the other end, Sam Curran provided the only meaningful support, counter-attacking with a series of boundaries. He charged down the track to lift Saim over mid-on and later rocked back to dispatch the spinner through midwicket.

The pair added 93 runs for the fifth wicket, taking England from 52-4 to 145 before Shaheen returned to break the stand in the 27th over. Curran, who scored 42 off 52 balls with five fours, top-edged a pull off a short delivery to Salman at fine leg.

Duckett continued to hold the innings together, reaching his fifth ODI century off 104 balls and his first against Pakistan. He struck 105 off 111 deliveries, including 10 fours and two sixes, before Arafat dismissed him in the 37th over, with Salman taking the catch at short fine leg.

England then lost Will Jacks (13) to Razaullah, who took a sharp return catch for his maiden ODI wicket, while Liam Dawson (five) fell to another short ball, caught by Shadab at deep square leg. Arafat also removed Jamie Overton (10), caught by Babar at long-off.

Gus Atkinson offered late resistance with an unbeaten 36 off 28 balls, including three sixes, helping England cross 200. Shaheen eventually ended the innings by dismissing debutant Henry Crocombe for eight, with Babar completing the catch.

World.title: KP Governor Kundi says Sohail Afridi, assembly speaker 'in safe hands' after house arrest
World.content:
Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Governor Faisal Karim Kundi said on Sunday that Sohail Afridi and Assembly Speaker Babar Saleem Swati were “in safe hands” after being placed under house arrest.

Afridi, who has become non-functional as the KP chief minister, has not been seen since the Centre imposed governor’s rule and emergency in his province on Oct 11. After their whereabouts remained unknown that day, a federal minister confirmed the next day that he and some of his cabinet members were in preventative custody.

However, with no further details officially confirmed, Afridi’s brother and Swati’s cousin have approached the Peshawar High Court separately to seek their relative’s recovery.

Appearing on Geo News’ TV programme ‘Jirga’ aired on Sunday night, the governor — who now runs the province — was asked about the whereabouts of Afridi, Kundi said he had been placed under house arrest and was “in safe hands — there is no need to worry”.

He said that if there were cases against Afridi, action would be taken against him and he would be indicted. However, if there were no cases, he would be released.

Asked why Afridi was not being released if there were no cases against him, Kundi replied he could provide an update tomorrow regarding the matter.

The governor further said that Speaker Swati was also under house arrest and would also be freed if there were no charges against him. Responding to another question, Kundi accused the PTI member of committing “illegal and unconstitutional” acts in his role as the KP Assembly Speaker.

Asked how many people were self-arrested and how many were “genuinely” arrested, Kundi said he did not have these numbers but that about 40 or 50 per cent of them were “under self-imposed arrest or self-concealment”.

The governor also addressed the imposition of emergency and governor’s rule in KP, stressing that it had been the “absolute last option”.

Regarding the potential duration of the emergency, he said, “We will see … after six months are complete, we will talk about what will and will not happen.

“But in my opinion, maybe it will run longer,” he added, clarifying that this was a “personal opinion” and he could be wrong.

He said that the basis for saying this was that the Centre and province needed to be “on the same page” in the fight against terrorism and “streamline” efforts against it, and was making plans accordingly, which he believed would take some time.

Kundi also distanced himself and the state policy from purported remarks made by Malik Khan Marjan — a member of the newly formed Area Representative and Development Council (ARDC) for 12 districts of KP — wherein he favoured dialogue with the Afghan Taliban.

“I will definitely check on this, but our policy is very clear: for now, we will not be holding talks with Afghanistan,” he maintained.

The governor condemned acts of terrorism carried out against Pakistan from Afghan soil and criticised Kabul for “allowing” India to use its soil against Pakistan while also asking for dialogue.

“If there is terrorism from there … our army knows how to fix it,” he added. “There is no dialogue and no talks of any kind about this.”

“I think this is his (Marjan’s) personal opinion, but it is not our policy,” Kundi said.

World.title: Jhang DC removed over use of Pera vehicle for 'non-serious purposes' in jeep rally: CM Maryam
World.content:
Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz said on Sunday that Jhang Deputy Commissioner Babar Sahib Din was being removed immediately over the recent use of an official vehicle of the Punjab Enforcement and Regulatory Authority (Pera) in a jeep rally, terming it a breach of discipline.

A three-day Jhang Thal Jeep Rally, which concluded last week, was organised in collaboration with private sponsors, according to Jhang District Information Officer Riaz Marth. He added that the event had received appreciation from provincial government authorities.

The chief minister took notice of the incident when a video surfaced on social media showing a Pera vehicle participating in the rally alongside other vehicles.

“The deployment of a regulatory authority’s resources for non-serious purposes, beyond its officially prescribed mandate, constitutes a serious breach of administrative discipline and a violation of established policy,” Maryam said on X on Sunday, sharing a post with the video.

“In view of this matter, the deputy commissioner is being removed from the post with immediate effect,” the chief minister said.

She also posted a notification issued by the Punjab government’s Services and General Administration Department on Sunday, which said that on the governor’s orders, DC Sahib Din “is hereby transferred, with immediate effect” and directed to report to the department for further orders.

In a later response to a claim that the vehicle was accompanying the rally for security and rescue purposes, the chief minister pointed out that security was the responsibility of the police, while rescue and emergency response were within the mandate of Rescue 1122.

“Neither function falls within Pera’s statutory mandate,” she said. “The activity in question, therefore, has no apparent connection with Pera’s prescribed duties and raises serious concerns about the rationale for deploying its vehicle in the rally.”

The Punjab CM also shared a letter issued by Pera Director General Farrukh Atiq Khan on Oct 21 — after the jeep rally concluded — wherein he directed all DCs and chairpersons of DERBs (District Enforcement and Regulatory Boards) to look into the misuse of Pera vehicles.

“It has been observed that Pera double-cabin vehicles issued to your good offices, for Pera field operations exclusively, are being engaged in unauthorised activities/operations,” the letter by the retired captain read.

It noted that some DCs had handed over Pera vehicles to assistant DCs, which was a violation of the authority’s official policy. DG Khan directed the DCs to retrieve or withdraw Pera vehicles from “any unauthorised allocation”.

The Pera force, created in the middle of last year, was aimed at conducting anti-encroachment and price control operations across various parts of Punjab, but in May, complaints poured in about its officials taking bribes from vendors and shopkeepers.

Subsequently, Maryam had ordered a crackdown on its officials involved in illegal actions and harassment of the public. She also set a deadline of June 30 for the field officials to wear body cams in a bid to ensure transparency and accountability.

The chief minister had also directed the authorities concerned to upgrade Pera’s internal intelligence and whistleblower system. At the time, she raised serious concerns regarding Pera’s credibility and discipline.

World.title: Billionaire Trump backer Bill Ackman says Ben-Gvir, Smotrich should not serve in next Israeli govt
World.content:
Billionaire American investor Bill Ackman on Sunday said that Itamar Ben-Gvir and Bezalel Smotrich should not serve in Israel’s next government, saying the two far-right politicians had caused enormous damage to the country’s reputation.

The public intervention by the prominent hedge fund manager, who is Jewish, comes just two days before Israel’s general election, in which polls show a tight race between Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s coalition and the opposition.

Ackman wrote on X that from the perspective of someone who had an understanding of how Israel was perceived in the United States, “Ben-Gvir and Smotrich have caused Israel enormous reputational damage with their statements and actions”.

The founder of Pershing Square Capital Management, who praised Netanyahu last week, said a government without the two ministers would send a message that Israel was “turning a new page”.

“This will allow Israel to rebuild lost credibility, increase the opportunity for an expansion of the Abraham Accords, and enjoy a better relationship with Democrats and Republicans and Americans at large,” he said.

The Abraham Accords are the 2020 agreement, mediated by US President Donald Trump’s first administration, that saw Israel establish relations with the United Arab Emirates and Bahrain. It later re-established official ties with Morocco.

Representatives for Ben-Gvir and Smotrich did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

As ministers in Netanyahu’s religious-nationalist coalition, Ben-Gvir and Smotrich have overseen policies widely perceived as discriminatory against Israel’s minority Arab population and Palestinians living in the occupied West Bank.

Several countries, including Britain, Canada and Australia, have imposed sanctions on the two ministers over accusations that they have incited violence against Palestinians in the West Bank.

Ben-Gvir’s Jewish Power party is projected to win around 10 parliamentary seats at Tuesday’s election, up from 6, while Smotrich’s Religious Zionism is projected to win 8, up from 7.

Ackman, who was visiting Israel last week, and who along with his wife Neri Oxman owns 5 per cent of the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange, supported Trump’s candidacy for president in 2024. Trump last week publicly endorsed Netanyahu for prime minister.

Nimrod Goren, the president of Israeli think tank Mitvim, said Ackman’s statement appeared to reflect a desire among Trump’s circles for Netanyahu to drop his far-right allies after the vote to form a ‘unity government’ with opposition parties.

However, Gadi Eisenkot, the leading challenger to Netanyahu, and other opposition party leaders have ruled out forming a government with Israel’s longest-serving prime minister.

Speaking at a Tel Aviv conference on Thursday, Ackman praised Netanyahu, who he said had done a good job in protecting and defending Israel since the Oct 7, 2023 Hamas attack.

Thousands of Israelis rallied in Tel Aviv on Saturday, calling for an independent inquiry into the attack that killed around 1,200 people.

World.title: Flights resume at Riyadh airport after two-week closure as Houthis attack Saudi Arabia
World.content:
Flights resumed at Riyadh’s international airport on Sunday following a series of deadly attacks on the facility that saw it closed for two weeks, even as Yemen’s Houthi rebels targeted the country with strikes.

King Khalid International Airport’s website showed several domestic and international flights scheduled on Sunday, including arrivals to the kingdom from Dubai, Paris and Cairo.

The renewed operations at the airport came as explosions rattled Riyadh early Sunday, after a text message was sent to residents warning of a hostile threat targeting the city.

Alerts warning of possible attacks were activated across the kingdom’s south throughout the day, with the Saudi-led military coalition fighting the Houthis saying at least 10 ballistic missiles were intercepted.

Saudi officials did not provide additional information when asked by AFP about the scope of the renewed operations at the airport.

But the tracking website Flightradar24 showed a small number of flights had departed, though the vast majority were cancelled.

Saudi Arabia, which leads a military coalition fighting the Houthis, has faced a barrage of strikes from the group in recent weeks.

The fighting erupted after a years-long truce between the Houthis and Yemen’s government fell apart.

The Houthi fighters have carried out waves of strikes on the airport, including an attack this month that killed 13 people and wounded more than 300, the deadliest in the kingdom in more than a decade.

The group has also targeted oil infrastructure and other sites.

Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree earlier warned that Riyadh airport was still “unsafe” and a “military target”.

“The Yemeni Armed Forces warn all international, regional and local airlines — as well as staff and travellers — against using King Khalid Airport in Riyadh, as it is unsafe and serves as a military target for our forces,” he said.

“The Saudi regime shall bear the consequences of any operations at the airport.”

Later on Sunday, Saree said Saudi Arabia had struck Yemen dozens of times over the previous 24 hours.

“During the past 24 hours, Saudi warplanes launched 56 airstrikes and missiles targeting civilian objects in the governorates of Hajjah, Lahj, Amran, Saada, Al-Jawf, Taiz and Ibb using F-15 and “Typhoon” planes that took off from the bases of Khamis Mushait and Taif, and missiles from Najran,” he said on X.

Attack warning

As the airport prepared to open, AFP journalists in Riyadh heard three explosions in the early hours of Sunday, with residents receiving alert messages for a “hostile aerial threat” urging them to stay in a safe place.

The warning came as the Saudi-led coalition fighting the Houthis said it had downed a ballistic missile launched by the group towards the capital, as well as two drones in the capital area.

“Air defences intercepted and destroyed a ballistic missile launched by the terrorist Houthi militia toward Riyadh,” the coalition posted on X.

Later on Sunday morning, the coalition said its forces intercepted a cruise missile fired by the Houthis at the kingdom’s southern city of Khamis Mushait.

Attacks appeared to target areas across the south, with warnings also issued for Abha city along with areas in Taif, Namas and Jazan.

“The bombardment has been very heavy since this morning — may God keep us safe. Everything is shaking because of the explosions,” one resident in Khamis Mushait told AFP on Sunday on condition of anonymity.

The attacks came after the Houthi fighters said that — in the space of 24 hours — they targeted three Saudi airports, including in Riyadh, energy installations, a pipeline and an air base.

The Saudi civil defence agency said it had also responded to falling debris in the Makkah and Madina regions on Saturday after intercepting two Houthi missiles.

The Houthis denied targeting the cities, the two holiest in Islam, calling the Saudi claim a “huge lie”.

The Houthis also fired at the southern Yemeni city of Aden, the interim seat of the government, saying they targeted a naval base and military camp overseen by Saudi forces.

The flare-up in Yemen, with the Houthis taking control of the entire Red Sea coast in a lightning offensive last month, has further destabilised the region and disrupted oil markets.

The Houthi attacks have impacted Saudi Arabia, the world’s biggest exporter of crude, disrupting businesses, airlines and residents.

World.title: 6 terrorists killed, 2 soldiers martyred during Dera Ismail Khan IBO: ISPR
World.content:
Security forces killed six terrorists in an intelligence-based operation in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa’s Dera Ismail Khan district, Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) said on Sunday.

The IBO was conducted on Saturday in DI Khan’s general area of Zarkani on the “reported presence of khawarij belonging to Indian proxy Fitna Al Khawarij”, the military’s media affairs wing said in a statement.

Fitna al Khawarij is a term the state uses for terrorists belonging to the banned Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP).

“Owing to [the] meticulous conduct of operation by security forces, six India-sponsored khawarij were sent to hell,” ISPR said.

It added that 36-year-old Naik Ghulam Murtaza, who hailed from Punjab’s Gujrat, and 30-year-old Sepoy Taseer Ahmed, a resident of Punjab’s Talagang, “fought gallantly, paid the ultimate sacrifices and embraced martyrdom”.

Weapons and ammunition were also recovered from the killed terrorists, who “remained actively involved in numerous terrorist activities against the security forces and law enforcement agencies, as well as the killing of innocent civilians”, the ISPR statement noted.

A sanitisation operation was being conducted to eliminate any other terrorist found in the area, ISPR said.

It affirmed that the “relentless counterterrorism campaign under vision ‘Azm-i- Istehkam’ (as approved by Federal Apex Committee on National Action Plan) by security forces and law enforcement agencies of Pakistan will continue at full pace to wipe out the menace of foreign-sponsored and supported terrorism from the country”.

“These sacrifices of our brave soldiers further reinforce our unwavering commitment to safeguarding our nation at all costs,” the military’s media wing stated.

Surge in terrorism

KP has been witnessing terrorist attacks and security challenges for a long time. The province, excluding the merged districts, recorded 54 terrorist attacks in August compared with 36 in July, representing an increase of 50 per cent, according to data compiled by the Pakistan Institute for Conflict and Security Studies (PICSS).

In response to these incidents, security forces have been conducting operations in various parts of the province.

Earlier this month, security forces killed eight terrorists during an IBO in DI Khan, state media reported, citing security sources.

On Friday, Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of the Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir affirmed that the armed forces will continue the counterterrorism campaign against India-sponsored terrorist groups “to the fullest”, vowing to “hit them hard wherever they are”.

CDF Munir visited the Corps Headquarters in Peshawar, where he was briefed on the security situation, ongoing counterterrorism operations, border management measures and the operational preparedness of formations deployed in the province.

According to a report from the Centre for Research and Security Studies, Pakistan recorded a sharp 83 per cent increase in violence-linked fatalities during the third quarter of 2026, reversing a declining trend reported in the first and second quarters.

Balochistan and KP remained the epicentres of violence, jointly accounting for 98pc of all fatalities during the period.

World.title: NCCIA says child pornography network busted, with father allegedly involved in selling videos of his children
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: The National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA) on Sunday claimed to have busted an international child pornography network in which a father was allegedly involved in making and selling explicit videos of his own children.

Islamabad NCCIA Additional Director Mohammad Shoaib Khan, speaking at a press conference in the capital, asserted that this was the first case in Pakistan’s history where a father was found involved in such a heinous crime against his own minor children.

The NCCIA official claimed the man was “involved in making indecent videos of his children, aged between four and five, and selling them”. The videos were bought and sold in secret Telegram groups through cryptocurrency, he added.

Khan added the investigation also revealed disturbing scenes of animal abuse in the videos. He said the alleged ringleader of the gang belonged to Skardu and was arrested with the assistance of international agencies.

During the investigation, important links and evidence were recovered from Islamabad, Multan and South Punjab, and raids were being conducted to arrest other network facilitators, according to Khan.

“Those involved in such heinous crimes will be brought to justice,” the NCCIA official declared.

Recalling another case, Khan said the agency arrested four members of an alleged child pornography gang after investigating around 60 videos recovered from a child’s mobile phone.

He said the suspect used to befriend children aged between six and 14 on Instagram, lure them with money and make indecent videos, which were then sold internationally via WhatsApp groups.

Khan claimed that two Chinese nationals had also been convicted earlier in this crime.

Sharing details of another case, the additional director said a minor girl from Karachi attempted suicide after being fed up with harassment. The girl is currently under treatment at a hospital, he added.

Khan claimed the NCCIA team, with the help of the victim’s family, traced and arrested the main suspect from Islamabad in just 13 hours. He added that the suspect had allegedly been harassing and blackmailing the victim for the last two to three years.

“Providing justice to the affected families is our top priority. Strict implementation of a zero-tolerance policy against those harassing women and children is being ensured,” he said.

The additional director further advised social media users to remain vigilant. “Think before uploading any indecent material. The law is in action; those uploading wrong content will not escape the law in any case,” he said.

He urged citizens not to share their one-time password, bank account details or personal information with anyone and to beware of fake numbers on fake websites, as calling them may lead to emptying of accounts.

“If you are a victim of cybercrime, do not remain silent; NCCIA stands with you,” he said, adding that citizens can call helpline 1799 for complaints, which is available 24 hours.

‘Zero-tolerance’ policy against cyber harassment of women, children

According to a separate statement issued by the NCCIA, the agency’s Director General (DG) Syed Ali Nasir Rizvi directed adopting a zero-tolerance policy against “elements harassing citizens,” particularly women and children, on social media.
